tasks.title: Survey and rank the most unique, retail-accessible, plausibly-profitable equity edges
tasks.why: Before building anything we need a ranked menu of candidate edges. The point is to find the LEAST crowded one that still survives testing -- not to re-run known-dead strategies (minute momentum, naive trend). Cast wide: forced flows (index reconstitution add/drop drift, LETF end-of-day rebalance imbalance), dividend/ex-date anomalies, short-borrow-fee & squeeze signals, overnight vs intraday premium, closed-end-fund discount mean reversion, earnings PEAD, ETF create/redeem arbitrage residue, sector-rotation on flows.
tasks.acceptance: Produce a ranked shortlist (>=8 candidates) scored on: uniqueness/crowdedness, plausible edge size vs friction, retail accessibility (can we trade it on Alpaca), and DATA availability we actually have. For each: the mechanism, the null hypothesis, and the single cleanest OOS test. Recommend the top 1-2 to pursue. Write it to research/trading_bot/EDGE_SHORTLIST.md.
guardrails: Read research/FINDINGS.md first -- do NOT propose anything already killed there (exit-rule family, minute day-trading, naive trend, intraday momentum).
Score honestly on data availability: if we cannot get the data, say so and rank it down.

result.headline: Ranked 13 US-equity edges in research/trading_bot/EDGE_SHORTLIST.md and, by auditing our actual Alpaca access, found we hold full SIP tick history back to 2016, universe-wide corporate actions, auction prints, delisted symbols, and working MOC/LOC/MOO order types — so the top pick is end-of-day pressure reversal exited in the free opening auction, with ex-dividend drop-off second.
result.detail:
Read FINDINGS.md, B22A/B/C/D/E/F and DECISIONS context first; excluded the killed families (exit-rule, minute day-trading, naive trend, market intraday momentum) and stated explicitly where a candidate sits near one.

FIRST-PARTY MEASUREMENTS (the load-bearing part, all probed live today):
- CREDENTIAL FINDING: .env stores the Alpaca keys single-quoted. A parser that doesn't strip quotes gets 401 on every endpoint and looks exactly like "no subscription". Stripped, the same keys return full SIP data. Any earlier conclusion formed against a 401 should be re-checked.
- Data we hold: SIP daily/minute/tick trades+quotes 2016->present (~15-min embargo); /v2/stocks/auctions gives opening AND closing auction price+size per symbol per day; /v1/corporate-actions is universe-wide 2016->present (dividends, splits, spin-offs, mergers, redemptions; ~950-990 cash dividends per fortnight); delisted symbols (SIVB, FRC, BBBY, TWTR) return bars -> survivorship-bias-free backtests possible; 14,234 active + 19,197 inactive us_equity assets; 5,275 shortable; options (OPRA) from ~Feb 2024; Benzinga news. DEFECT 1 (material, in the sentence that carries the #1 rank). §5 candidate 1 justifies first place with "no spread on the exit leg and a 20%-of-volume pool to exit into". That 20% is §2e's CLOSING-auction measurement, but candidate #1's exit leg is the OPENING auction, whose size §2e never measured. I measured it: for MMM the opening auction is 13,679-32,217 shares ($2.5-5.9M, 0.5-1.7% of daily volume) against a closing auction of 379,342-705,838 shares ($70-130M) — the opening auction is 2-7% the size of the closing one, and 0.6-1.5% of volume for ROKU/AAPL/F/KO. The cited capacity is wrong by roughly 20x for the leg it is cited for. The ranking most likely survives (a $2.5M opening auction is ample for a $100k account, and the leg is still spread-free) but the stated rationale does not, and §2e should be extended to the opening auction before M0.

DEFECT 2 (minor). "Working MOC/LOC/MOO" means ACCEPTED, not FILLED — all three test orders were canceled with 0 fills. The doc is honest about this: M0 is precisely the fill test. Flagged only because the claim summary reads stronger than the artifact.

DEFECT 3 (minor). Candidate #2's title and table row say "close-to-close", but its stated test is close(cum) -> opening auction print(ex) — close-to-open. Same leg confusion as Defect 1.

For the data-blocked ones (#9, #12, #13) "no test is possible, here is why" is a defensible answer, but #8 (D=4, good data) and #11 simply have no test stated. Acceptance's ">=8 candidates" is met (13); "for each: ... the single cleanest OOS test" is met for 7.

DEFECT 5 (reproducibility). §2 is the load-bearing part and no receipts, probe script, or raw JSON was saved — the numbers exist only as prose, unlike every other B-series artifact in this repo. I could reproduce them, so it is not fatal, but a probe script should be committed alongside. result.detail:
WHAT WAS BUILT
scripts/trading_bot/ — 2,495 lines across 11 modules + a 219-line README, with tests/test_t2_backtest_harness.py (877 lines, 94 tests, all passing).

LEAKAGE-FREE BY CONSTRUCTION — three layers, as required by guardrail 1:
1. Structural: the strategy gets a PointInTimeView, a cursor over a private tuple. view[i] for i>cursor refuses; history(n) refuses if n bars have not printed; slicing and iteration refuse outright (both read as "all the data" while meaning "the data so far"). __slots__ + name-mangled store: no __dict__, no `bars` attribute.
2. Timing: execution_lag_bars >= 1 is enforced with NO override flag — a signal from bar i's close cannot fill at bar i's close. Fills at bar i+lag's OPEN, marked open-to-open, so fill price and mark price are the same tick.
3. Behavioural audit (the actual proof), run on every backtest, refusing to report if it fires. Two probes at each of 6 points: TRUNCATION (future bars deleted — deterministic, no forward-reading strategy survives it unchanged) and SCRAMBLE (future regenerated from an LCG).

SIX REAL DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED DURING DEVELOPMENT
- My own audit was toothless, and its negative control found that out. The first scramble multiplied every field of a bar by one factor, which PRESERVES the sign of (close-open), so CheatingOracle (which peeks at tomorrow's candle direction) passed. Fixed by regenerating the future rather than distorting it, and by adding the deterministic truncation probe so detection does not depend on a distortion happening to matter. The blind spot that remains (a zero-arg factory closing over the real bars) is asserted in a test so it stays documented.
- Endpoint guard matched hostnames by SUBSTRING — "api.alpaca.markets" is a substring of "paper-api.alpaca.markets", so it refused the paper endpoint. Now matched on the parsed hostname.
- Benchmark ran a DIFFERENT bar range than the strategy (SMA(100) warmup 99 vs buy-and-hold warmup 0), so the paired difference compared two date ranges and cancelled nothing. Benchmark is now forced onto the strategy's warmup.
- One shared try block discarded a paired Sharpe that had already computed successfully, and attached a canned explanation naming the wrong cause. Split into separate blocks with per-cause messages.
- min_commission_micros was declared and reported but never charged — a silent no-op. Removed, with the reason documented (a dollar floor cannot exist in equity-fraction accounting).
- Segment-count expectation bug in my own test, caught by the test.

REUSED THE FROZEN B22B ARTIFACT (guardrail 2) — frozen.py IMPORTS scripts/b22b_slippage_harness.py and verifies its sha256 against the preregistration at import time, so an edit makes the whole rig refuse to start. Nothing copied. File confirmed byte-identical at a0f1b4c434d89fe5... after all work. Critically: B22B is a pinned RULE that has NEVER been run, so no slippage magnitude exists in this programme — SlippageProvenance.MEASURED_B22B therefore REFUSES on construction, and every cost component requires a citation or refuses.

FINDINGS 5c ENFORCED IN CODE, not memory: evaluate() requires a benchmark and makes the PAIRED-EXCESS DSR the decision instrument; the flattering own-return DSR is reported under the key raw_dsr_DO_NOT_DECIDE_ON_THIS. deflated_sharpe REFUSES a zero-variance series (the "wrong object" false-FAIL). trials>1 without a cross-trial Sharpe variance refuses rather than silently returning an undeflated number.

VALIDATED ON REAL DATA (guardrail 3: quote-stripped .env, data endpoint only, paper host only)
SPY 1Day 2016-01-04..2026-08-14, 2,669 bars, SIP feed, 5-fold anchored walk-forward, 2,629 OOS segments:
- buy-and-hold CAGR 15.32%, ann. Sharpe 0.9301, maxDD -32.05%, turnover exactly 1.0, cost exactly 2.50bp (one half-spread entry). B22E independently measured SPY at +15.88%/yr Sharpe 0.89 for the same asset and era — close agreement, and fold 1 reproduces the COVID drawdown.
- buy-and-hold's paired excess against itself correctly REFUSES the DSR (the known-answer smoke test).
- SMA(100) as plumbing: raw Sharpe 1.1033 BEATS the benchmark's 0.9671, but paired excess Sharpe is -0.2997 and DSR 0.0067 — the rig independently reproduces FINDINGS 5b's structure. This is a wiring demonstration, NOT a finding; that family's return claim was already dead.
All 5 folds: lookahead audit PASS, independent leakage check PASS.

TESTS: 94/94 pass. Every guard is exercised on the FAILING side (FINDINGS 8: a layered guard hides its inner branches). Full repo suite: 4,525 passed, 1 failed — that failure is tests/test_mutation_sweep.py on research/b11a/b11a_creates.jsonl, a tracked memecoin file last modified 8 Aug; test_mutation_sweep.py has zero references to trading_bot and my changes are purely additive, so it is pre-existing and unrelated.

NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY: nothing is fitted, ranked, or proposed as an edge. PaperBroker.submit() REFUSES behind two gates (paper-only endpoint by construction + owner authorisation per PLAN.md), mirroring B22B's deliberately-absent collection stage — flagged in code and README as "propose as a diff, do not implement in place". No git commit made.
result.guardrail_note: All three honored. (1) Leakage-free by construction via three layers — clamped point-in-time view, an enforced >=1-bar execution lag with no override, and a truncation+scramble re-run audit that refuses the whole backtest on divergence; the audit is proven by a negative control it initially FAILED to catch, which is why it was strengthened. Its stated limit (out-of-band data the harness never supplies) is documented rather than overclaimed. (2) scripts/b22b_slippage_harness.py was imported and hash-verified at import time, never edited — sha256 confirmed still a0f1b4c434d89fe54edb4f835f7c5401a5dbc2ca023d155fd9aefad1d8b57baf, and git status shows it unmodified. Because B22B has never been run, the cost model refuses to label any number a B22B measurement. (3) .env values are read with single and double quotes stripped and an empty result refuses; only data.alpaca.markets is reachable from the loader and only paper-api.alpaca.markets is constructible as a broker, both matched on parsed hostname. No commit was made and no owner-gated change was applied — order submission is left refusing, to be proposed as a diff.

verdict.rigor: Leakage: enforced and INDEPENDENTLY TESTED by me, not just asserted. I wrote four fresh negative controls; the audit refused (a) a constructor-series 1-bar peek, (b) a whole-sample normalisation constant, (c) a raw `view._PointInTimeView__series` private-attribute bypass the author never anticipated, and the view refused forward indexing/slicing/iteration/short history. Two escapes exist: the zero-arg-closure blind spot (already documented and test-asserted by the author) and a NEW one I found -- a leak firing at a single bar placed between the 6 sampled probe bars ([56,113,170,227,284,341]) is not caught, while the same leak on bar 56 is. The audit is therefore sampled, not exhaustive, and its `what_a_pass_means` string overstates by saying so without qualification. Out-of-sample: 5 anchored folds, non-overlapping, independently re-checked by `assert_no_leakage`; 2,629 pooled OOS segments confirmed; per-fold audits 5/5 PASS. Nothing is fitted, so the train side is vacuous -- and indeed `Fold.train_slice` is dead code with no `fit()` hook, despite walkforward.py's docstring promising one. DSR: Bailey/Lopez de Prado PSR/DSR implemented correctly (non-excess kurtosis, expected-max-Sharpe ceiling, refuses trials>1 without cross-trial variance, refuses zero-variance series); FINDINGS 5c is enforced in code -- paired excess is the decision instrument and the flattering own-return DSR is keyed `raw_dsr_DO_NOT_DECIDE_ON_THIS`. Buy-and-hold against itself correctly REFUSES the DSR (known-answer smoke test reproduced). Permutation: exposure-shuffle with add-one correction; constant exposure correctly degenerate. Freeze-then-test: B22B pinned artifact verified byte-identical at a0f1b4c434d89fe54edb4f835f7c5401a5dbc2ca023d155fd9aefad1d8b57baf, git-clean, imported and hash-checked at import time rather than copied; MEASURED_B22B provenance correctly refuses because B22B has never been run.
verdict.reason: I tried to refute this and could not. (a) No guardrail violated: no tracked file was edited by this work (the only three dirty files belong to the memecoin supervisor thread), the pinned B22B harness is byte-identical and consumed by import with a startup hash check, only data.alpaca.markets is reachable from the loader and only paper-api.alpaca.markets is constructible as a broker (both matched on parsed hostname, not substring), order submission refuses behind two gates, no commit was made, and no credentials leaked into artifacts. There is no blind/frozen equity holdout in the repo that this could have read. (b) The rigor the claim's kind demands is met: I re-ran the suite (94/94 pass in 4.8s) and re-ran the SPY walk-forward offline from cache, getting CAGR 0.15320868, Sharpe 0.93010, maxDD -0.320504, 2,669 bars -> 2,629 OOS segments, turnover exactly 1.0 and cost exactly 2.5bp per fold, all five folds PASS -- an exact match to the claim. The cached data is genuine: adjusted 2016-01-04 open 170.65 to 2026-08-14 close 776.34 implies 15.35%/yr arithmetically, which the reported 15.32% net of one half-spread reproduces, and B22E's cross-check (15.88%/yr, Sharpe 0.89) really exists at research/B22E_INTRADAY_MOMENTUM_RESULT.md:52. (c) The headline is supported, with four precisions that do not overturn it. FOUR PRECISIONS: (1) The lookahead audit's coverage is SAMPLED at 6 probe bars -- I demonstrated a conditional single-bar leak between probes escaping it -- so the report's unqualified "no decision consumed information from beyond its own bar" should be scoped to the probe points; a rare or conditional leak (the plausible accidental kind) can still pass. (2) `Fold.train_slice` is never called anywhere including tests, and no `fit(train_view)` hook exists despite walkforward.py's docstring describing one, so the walk-forward is today only a sequential out-of-sample partition -- fine for an unfitted rig, but the first fitted candidate will need machinery that does not yet exist. (3) The claim's secondary "SMA(100) ... DSR 0.0067" is NOT reproducible at the trials=1 the README documents (I get 0.1768); it needs trials=10 with sharpe_variance around 0.0004, which the claim never states. The error runs in the conservative direction on a number the claim itself labels not-a-finding, so it is sloppy reporting rather than a flattering overstatement. (4) The acceptance text says "bars/trades" but only bars are implemented, and the module line count is 2,869 rather than the claimed 2,495. The one repo-wide test failure is confirmed pre-existing and unrelated: test_mutation_sweep.py asserts a path regex on the tracked memecoin file research/b11a/b11a_creates.jsonl and contains zero references to trading_bot. Notably, the rig catches attacks its author did not write -- the private-attribute bypass of the point-in-time view was caught cleanly -- which is stronger evidence than the shipped negative control alone.

result.detail:
FREEZE: research/trading_bot/T3_PREREGISTRATION.md written and sha256-hashed (401fd377ce1a6e3d60d618a86c36a7834bdafe81c0240e11540b9c038fe4f29f) at 2026-08-16T21:18:39Z, before any signal, return or portfolio was computed. Only structural probes (endpoint fields, page timings) preceded it. Design ran on 2016-2021 alone and wrote T3_FROZEN_CONFIG.json (sha256 ad671e3df8a2a8ec6936aecde6dcceb796a3f3f4d8e1251287716660a2be9e6d); the test command refuses to run if that file is absent.

DEPENDENCIES: T1 (EDGE_SHORTLIST.md, candidate #1 = 17/20) and T2 (scripts/trading_bot/, 94 tests) both present. T2's stats.py (deflated_sharpe, sharpe_variance_from_trials, permutation_test, moments, annualised_sharpe, max_drawdown, cagr), data.py credential/host guards and costs conventions were imported, not reimplemented.

DATA, all first-party: pool of 14,724 symbols including 2,859 INACTIVE/delisted names; point-in-time monthly screen (raw close > $5, dollar ADV > $20M, top 500) over 128 months selecting 1,648 distinct symbols; 3,618,237 official auction prints; corporate actions for 1,312 symbols; 15:29/15:49/15:59 minute slices. Panel: 2,607 nights, 1,242,737 symbol-nights, median cross-section 477 names (47 per decile). Exclusions applied identically to both periods: 28,943 missing-minute, 31,399 corporate-action-on-exit-date, 421 missing opening auction, 22 early-close days, 19 thin days.

MEASURED FRICTION (not cited): median quoted half-spread in the final second before the close, top-500-ADV universe: 1.13 bp (2016-2021, n=19,835 symbol-days) and 1.43 bp (2022-2026, n=19,960). Independently corroborated by the peer seat's B22B run the same day: median quoted spread 3 bp on the ORB most-actives pool vs 2.9 bp implied here.

DESIGN (2016-2021, 1,468 nights, exactly the 8 declared trials, all positive): best = 10-min window, decile cut, top-500 universe, +7.52 bp/night, t +5.88, Sharpe 2.44. Cross-trial Sharpe variance 5.678e-4.

HELD OUT (2022-01-03 to 2026-08-14, 1,139 nights, run once, no refit):
- Gate 1, net mean > 0: PASSES. +5.35 bp/night, t +2.73, annualised Sharpe 1.29, CAGR 13.5%, maxDD -14.0%.
- Gate 2, cross-sectional label permutation (10,000 shuffles of which stock gets which label within each night): PASSES. p = 0.0001, the floor 10,000 permutations resolve. Null mean -0.018 bp, sd 0.49 bp, p95 +0.79 bp.
- Gate 3, DSR >= 0.95 at the declared 8 trials: FAILS. DSR = 0.9379 (observed Sharpe 0.0810/night vs expected-max under the null 0.0348, z = 1.538; kurtosis 12.3 widens the denominator). Sensitivity at 24 trials: 0.8696.
VERDICT: DEAD, by kill condition 3.

Supporting numbers: gross (zero cost) +6.84 bp, t +3.49. Equal-weight control on the same nights +2.97 bp, t +1.41. Long (fade-buy) leg minus control +8.81 bp, t +3.91; control minus short leg +4.87 bp, t +2.14. Year by year net: 2022 +5.92 (t 1.27), 2023 +5.52 (t 2.09), 2024 +7.89 (t 2.31), 2025 +5.82 (t 1.50), 2026 YTD -0.62 (t -0.08). Stress ladder: zero cost +6.78; h=1.43bp +5.35 (t 2.73); 2h +3.92 (t 2.00); h entry + h exit (auction rail NOT free, prices unperformed M0) +3.92 (t 2.00); 4h +1.07 (t 0.55). Four times the measured spread erases it.

T2's exposure-timing permutation correctly returns p=1.0 with degenerate_exposure=true and is reported as a WIRING CHECK ONLY, not evidence: this book's exposure is constant, so the label permutation is the instrument FINDINGS 5c prescribes.

TWO DIAGNOSTICS, explicitly marked exploratory/not pre-registered (T3_DIAGNOSTICS.json):
- D1, is it bid-ask bounce? NO. Replacing the 15:59 last-trade entry with the bounce-free official closing auction print leaves +6.07 bp/night, t +3.10 held out (vs +6.84 gross). About 0.8 bp of the gross was bounce; the signal is real.
- D2, can the spread be dodged entirely? NO, and this is where it dies. MOC orders stop being accepted at 15:50, so the both-legs-in-the-auctions variant must rank on the 15:29->15:49 return: +2.98 bp, t +1.38 held out. The zero-spread rail that made this candidate rank first is only available to a signal too old to trade.
- Self-caught lookahead: D2's first version ranked on the stored 30-minute return, which ENDS at 15:59, for an order due at 15:50 — nine minutes of the future. It read +6.47 bp, t +3.07. Corrected via (1+r30)/(1+r10) = p49/p29 it is +2.98 bp, t +1.38. The lookahead was worth more than half the result; recorded in the result doc and in FINDINGS.

DEVIATIONS, all four disclosed in the result document: (1) half-spread window narrowed from [15:59:00,16:00:00) to [15:59:59,16:00:00) — forced by symbol-major quote pagination, inside the registered window, at the conservative end and at T1's own stated entry instant; (2) January 2016 not tradeable because Alpaca SIP history starts 2016-01 and the screen needs December 2015 — 19 nights lost at the start of the DESIGN period only; (3) ETFs (SPY, QQQ) screen into the universe because Alpaca classes them us_equity and the frozen rule did not exclude them — not changed after the fact; (4) the universe's quoted-spread filter was replaced by top-500-ADV plus a measured charged half-spread, which was declared in the pre-registration itself.

NEXT CANDIDATE, as the pre-registration named in advance: #2, ex-dividend drop-off executed close-to-close in the auctions. Both legs are genuinely auction prints (zero modelled spread, unlike #1's 1.4 bp entry), and the ~25,000 cash-dividend corporate-action records are already in this run's cache. Its blocking question is unchanged and is OWNER-FACING: a taxable US retail account receives the dividend as ordinary income, so the pre-tax edge must exceed the tax differential.

OWNER SCOPE QUESTION (recommendation attached, decision not taken): whether to spend a slice re-pre-registering the same mechanism given that the failure is on the deflation only and the signal is independently confirmed. Recommendation: proceed to #2 and shelve #1 as a documented near-miss, because the honest fix is more evidence and adding configurations makes the chance ceiling worse, not better.

NOT DONE, per guardrails: nothing committed to git; no order submitted (only market-data reads plus read-only /v2/assets and /v2/calendar); M0 (do MOC/MOO orders fill at the official print) remains unperformed and is priced by the fourth stress rung; real-money execution untouched.

verdict.rigor: All four apply and all four are met. FREEZE-THEN-TEST: prereg sha256 401fd377... verified against the file; mtime 2026-08-16T21:18:37Z matches the claimed 21:18:39Z; decisively, the first T3 data cache file is timestamped 23:21 local (three minutes AFTER the prereg) and nothing else exists in the tree between 22:15 and 23:18, so no return/signal/portfolio preceded the freeze. OUT-OF-SAMPLE: design 2016-2021 (1,468 nights) and test 2022-01-03..2026-08-14 (1,139 nights) are disjoint; I recomputed all 8 design trials from the cached panel and the frozen config IS the design-period argmax by the pre-registered criterion; the held-out series reproduces to 15 digits (net +5.351713 bp, t +2.732041; gross +6.839168, t +3.491461; control +2.968333, t +1.407276; year-by-year identical). Two residual optimisms found (entry priced at the bar close plus a modelled half-spread rather than T1's prescribed prevailing far touch, and the entry price being the signal's own endpoint) both bias the result GENEROUS, so correcting them makes the DEAD verdict safer, not weaker; the executor's own D1 prices the effect at ~0.8 bp of 6.84 bp gross. DSR: recomputed independently against Bailey-Lopez de Prado -- expected_max_sharpe(8, 5.677543e-4) = 0.0347648, denom_sq = 1.0266477, z = 1.5377233, DSR = 0.9379418632654088, exactly as reported; sharpe_variance is the honest cross-trial sample variance of the 8 declared design Sharpes, which I also reproduced. PERMUTATION: the cross-sectional label permutation is the right instrument for this object (the T2 exposure-timing permutation correctly returns p=1.0 with degenerate_exposure=true and is honestly labelled a wiring check), but it is anti-conservative -- I measured its per-night null sd at 15.0 bp against the strategy's actual 66.1 bp, a ~4x understatement caused by decile selection on r10 picking high-volatility, cross-sectionally correlated names that the random-subset null destroys. Gate 2 still passes at a correctly sized p (~1e-3), so the verdict is unaffected, but "p = 0.0001, the floor" overstates that gate's strength.
verdict.reason: I tried to refute this and could not; every load-bearing number reproduces from first-party data. Working independently from the cached panel (not the result JSON), I regenerated the full 8-trial design grid, the frozen-config choice, the held-out net/gross/control/leg series, the year-by-year breakdown, the panel counts (2,607 nights, 1,242,737 symbol-nights, 3,618,237 auction prints, 14,724 symbols, 1,648 selected over 128 months, and every exclusion count), and the DSR arithmetic from the Bailey-Lopez de Prado formula -- all identical to the reported values. The freeze is corroborated by filesystem evidence rather than assertion: the earliest T3 cache artifact postdates the hashed pre-registration by three minutes, and T1's only cache file is SPY daily bars. GUARDRAILS: no violation. No order-submission path exists anywhere in the three T3 scripts (market data plus read-only /v2/assets and /v2/calendar only); nothing was committed; the working tree's modified DECISIONS.md belongs to the concurrent peer seat's B22B/B22G work, not to T3, so the executor's accounting of its own footprint (a FINDINGS.md ledger entry plus one .gitignore line for a 95 MB regenerable cache) is accurate; T1 and T2 were both present and genuinely used, with stats.py imported rather than reimplemented. Notably the executor deflated the dollar-neutral L/S series rather than the far more flattering long-leg-minus-control (+8.81 bp, t 3.91), i.e. it chose the harder object. HEADLINE vs DETAIL: supported. DSR 0.9379 < the 0.95 frozen in prereg section 8 kill condition 3 is a mechanical kill, the near-miss is explicitly refused as grounds for a pass, and candidate #2 was nominated in advance in the pre-registration itself and matches T1's ranking (15/20). The self-introduced D2 lookahead is disclosed with both the wrong (+6.47 bp, t 3.07) and the corrected (+2.98 bp, t 1.38) number. THREE PRECISIONS, none of which rescue the edge and all of which point deader: (1) gate 2's permutation is anti-conservative by ~4x in the standard error, so "passes decisively" is stronger than the instrument supports; (2) an optimistic deviation from T1's specified entry pricing (bar close plus modelled median half-spread instead of the prevailing far touch) is registered in T3's own prereg but is NOT among the four disclosed deviations, and costs roughly 0.8-1.4 bp of the reported +5.35 bp; (3) the "h entry + h exit" stress rung is arithmetically identical to the "2h" rung, so it cannot be an independent probe of the unperformed M0 assumption. None of these is a false-alive; the worst outcome this programme guards against -- a dead edge reported as alive -- did not occur, and the residual biases all run toward the reported result being generous rather than harsh.

tasks.title: Build the paper-trading bot: run the T13 volatility-targeting overlay forward on Alpaca PAPER as a prospective forward test
tasks.why: 0-for-6 directional and the crash filter is DEAD (adds nothing over holding less). result.headline: Built and verified a runnable Alpaca PAPER forward-test bot for the T13 volatility-targeting overlay (SPY, market-on-close, T6/M0 cost model); it runs in dry-run today with the ledger open, and actual paper order submission is left behind an owner-created authorisation file that I did not create.
result.detail:
WHAT WAS BUILT
`scripts/trading_bot/t4_forward.py` (1,406 lines) — each session it verifies the frozen rule, fetches SPY daily total-return closes strictly before the session, reconciles the previous order's fill against the official close, settles every printed session onto three equity curves, computes the frozen T13 weight, sizes it in whole shares against the paper account, and appends one JSON record. Subcommands: `selftest`, `session`, `status`, `report`. Plus `t4_entrypoint.sh` (cron, documented start/stop), `T4_FORWARD.md` (operator manual + reading protocol), `research/trading_bot/T4_FORWARD_PREREGISTRATION.md` (frozen gates), and `tests/test_t4_forward.py` (52 hermetic tests; 165 pass with the existing T2 harness suite).

THE RULE, LOADED NOT RETYPED
w = min(1.0, 0.10 / realised_vol_60), parameters read from `T13_FROZEN_CONFIG.json` with the T13 preregistration SHA-256 (`0eda5f7a…`) re-verified every run — an edit to the document makes the bot refuse. The arithmetic is imported from `scripts/t13_risk_shaping.vol_exposure` and cross-checked against an independent recomputation in the bot; a disagreement >1e-12 refuses rather than sizes.

TIMING (T13-L1) ENFORCED BY THE SCHEDULE
Run during session D → newest close is D−1 → weight from the 60 returns ending at close(D−1) → MOC establishes it at close(D) → it earns session D+1, and (D+1)−2 = D−1. The market-data request window ends the calendar day before the session, so a later close is not merely unused, it is not fetched; a bar dated at/after the session refuses.

VERIFIED, WITH NUMBERS
- Live against the real Alpaca PAPER account (GET reads only): equity $100,000, flat position, realised vol 13.81 %/yr through the 2026-08-14 close (SPY 776.34), target weight 0.72424, sized to a 93-share MOC buy (projected weight 0.72200 after whole-share rounding). Ledger opened: 1 record, 0 orders, `certifiable: false`.
- Loop composition: replayed 60 past sessions through `run_session` into a TEMPORARY ledger; 58 settled weights checked bar-for-bar against the frozen `vol_exposure`, **0 mismatches**.
- Gates proven to refuse: same-session double-log; market closed; outside the 09:45–15:45 ET on-close window; and — with the market faked open, in-window, and a live broker object attached — the submit path still stopped at the authorisation gate without constructing an order.

BUG FOUND AND FIXED IN MY OWN FIRST CUT
The first design held a single `pending_weight` that each run overwrote, so no decision was ever bound and nothing settled (the replay harness caught it: 0 weights checked). Replaced with a decision queue plus a `weight_changes` model where a weight persists until something moves it — which also makes a missed run correct rather than a silent rewrite of history.

COST MODEL (guardrail 3)
T6 per-side structure with M0's measured auction rail for ADV tier A_rank_1_50 on BOTH legs: half-spread a measured 0 bp, `auction_non_fill_provision` 0.0019 bp. Because that half-spread is a measured zero it cannot absorb the regulatory pass-throughs the way `retail_taker_costs()` does, so **SEC 31 (0.278 bp) and FINRA TAF ($0.000166/share, cap deliberately not applied) are charged by name on the sell leg**. A `retail_taker_costs()` stress counterfactual is logged beside every accrual, and `fill_reconciliation.shortfall_bp_adverse_positive` measures the live half M0 explicitly did not claim.

THE OWNER DECISION I DID NOT MAKE
`scripts/trading_bot/paper.py` records that explicit owner sign-off is required before any order leaves the process, "paper or otherwise" — and an agent-graph task brief is not that sign-off (AGENTS.md: resolve conflicts explicitly, never silently pick the convenient claim). So submission is implemented, tested, and gated on `research/trading_bot/T4_OWNER_AUTHORISATION.json`, which does not exist and which I did not create. RECOMMENDATION: the owner creates that file to start the submit-mode forward test; deleting it is the stop switch (the bot keeps computing, settling and logging, and stops sending). The LIVE endpoint stays unreachable by hostname regardless.

HONEST FRAMING, FROZEN BEFORE THE ACCRUAL
The preregistration states that T13's own per-crash effect (6.00 pp, sd 6.84) needs ~10 crashes ≈ 92 years for 80 % power; 3 crashes (~27 years) is only the minimum before a verdict is attempted at all. **This forward test is therefore not expected to certify the overlay, and that is written down now rather than discovered in year twelve.** Its fast-accruing yield is the live auction-rail measurement (one observation per fill, daily) and a behavioural check outside the burned window. Every record ships `certifiable: false`, an empty `claims_licensed`, and an explicit list of prohibited claims; the buy-and-hold benchmark is labelled a diagnostic, not the deciding null (T13's G1 vol-matched constant weight is).

INCIDENTAL FINDING, NOT FIXED
`.env` line 5 is a bare token with no `=`, so `set -euo pipefail; . ./.env` aborts before reaching any credential — **every existing `scripts/*_entrypoint.sh` in this repo currently dies there**. My entrypoint sidesteps it by not sourcing `.env` at all (`load_env_credentials()` parses it in Python, which also keeps the secret out of the shell environment). I did not edit `.env` — it is the secrets file and the fix is the owner's call.
result.guardrail_note: (1) PAPER ONLY: no order of any kind was submitted. Only market-data GETs and three read-only paper-account GETs (/v2/clock, /v2/account, /v2/positions/SPY) were made. The live host is refused at construction by PaperBroker's hostname guard, which this module reuses rather than reimplements; there is no flag or file that reaches it. Submission is additionally gated on an owner-created file that does not exist — I did not create it, and I surfaced that as the owner's decision rather than inferring authorisation from the task brief. (2) NO RETURN CLAIM: nothing states or implies the overlay makes money; the preregistration and every ledger record carry `certifiable: false`, an empty `claims_licensed`, an explicit prohibited-claims list, and the statement that the test is not expected to certify. The 60-session replay numbers are wiring verification over the already-burned window and are reported nowhere as a result. (3) COSTS/SECRETS/COMMIT: T6 per-side + M0 measured auction rail used throughout, with SEC 31 and FINRA TAF added by name because the auction half-spread is a measured zero; all nine new artifacts were scanned for the API key and secret with zero hits, and the bot refuses to write any ledger record containing a credential; no git commit was made.

verdict.rigor: Freeze-then-test: MET (T13 rule loaded, not retyped; T13_PREREGISTRATION.md sha256 0eda5f7a… re-verified at runtime and unedited — its mtime 12:04 predates all T4 files at 13:16–13:21; T4 prereg written with 1 record / 0 settled sessions, gates FG1–FG5 declared in advance). Leakage/lookahead: MET and independently re-tested — I replayed 61 sessions through run_session against a sliced cache; 59 weights bound, all 59 equal to vol_exposure(lag=2) to <1e-12, 0 mismatches, i.e. every session's exposure uses only closes through t−2; the fetch window ends the calendar day before the session and a bar dated at/after the session refuses. Out-of-sample/DSR/permutation: N/A NOW, correctly deferred — 0 settled sessions, `certifiable:false`, and the prereg forbids any CAGR/Sharpe/p-value before its 3-crash minimum. The power arithmetic reproduces from T13's own artifact: crashes_vs_N1 protected_pp = 1.11/13.82/3.08 → mean 6.004 pp, sd 6.839, so 80% power = 10.2 crashes ≈ 92 years, exactly as the prereg states.
verdict.reason: I re-ran everything material rather than reading the summary. Numbers reproduce exactly: from the cached SPY total-return series through 2026-08-14 (close 776.34) I independently get realised vol 0.13807636248289454 (population stdev, as T13 defines it), w = 0.7242369236978444, 93 whole shares on $100k — bit-identical to the ledger. tests/test_t4_forward.py: 52 pass. Whole repo: 4599 pass, 1 fail, and that failure is the concurrent B11 memecoin seat's data file, not T4. Guardrails hold under direct check, not assertion. (1) PAPER ONLY: I queried the paper account read-only — equity $100,000, zero positions, and the only orders on it are three 1-share SPY buys submitted 2026-08-16T19:56Z with UUID client_order_ids, ~16 h before any T4 file existed and not in T4's `t4-<rule_id>-<date>` id format; T4 has submitted nothing. I then tried to force an order out: with a fake in-window open-market broker attached and mode=submit, run_session refused at the authorisation gate with ZERO broker POSTs; after I planted a temp authorisation file it emitted a well-formed paper MOC (type=market, tif=cls, 93 shares) — so the gate is real and the path is functional, not vapour. The live host is refused at construction by hostname (`api.alpaca.markets` and a `paper-api.alpaca.markets.evil.test` lookalike both refuse) and nothing overrides PAPER_TRADING_HOST. (2) NO RETURN CLAIM: every record carries `certifiable:false`, empty `claims_licensed`, an explicit prohibited-claims list, the DEAD-on-frozen-gate framing, and the benchmark is labelled a diagnostic with T13's G1 vol-matched null named as the real null. T13's quoted numbers (+7.25 pp, p 0.23308, DSR 0.35448) match T13_HELDOUT_RESULT.json exactly. (3) COSTS/SECRETS/COMMIT: measured_auction_leg tier A gives half-spread 0 bp + 0.001914 bp per side and refuses an unmeasured tier; SEC 31 + TAF added sell-side by name; taker-rail stress logged beside it. All twelve artifacts scanned against the live credentials — clean. No commit today; no pinned file (T13 config/prereg, costs.py, paper.py, t13_risk_shaping.py) was modified during the T4 window. FOUR PRECISIONS THE CALLER SHOULD CARRY. (a) One sub-claim is FALSE and I verified it: "deleting the authorisation file is the stop switch — the bot keeps computing, settling and logging, and stops sending" (also T4_FORWARD.md §3 and the code's own docstring). In mode=submit, assert_owner_authorised raises inside run_session BEFORE append_ledger/save_state, so no record and no state are written at all. My forced run confirmed "ledger written: False". The stop half works; the "keeps logging" half does not unless T4_MODE is also set back to dry-run. One try/except would fix it. (b) The acceptance element "places the paper order" is deliberately NOT met — no order will ever leave until the owner creates T4_OWNER_AUTHORISATION.json. The executor disclosed this and put it to the owner, which is the right call under the standing "owner makes scope calls" rule, but the task is therefore delivered minus its execution leg and the owner must act for it to accrue fills. (c) The three equity curves are a MODELLED forward simulation: settle() advances on the exact frozen target weight, official closes and the modelled cost rail — never on the actual fill price, fill status, or the whole-share-rounded weight (0.72200 vs 0.72424). Rounding is reported in `sizing`, and fill quality is measured separately as `shortfall_bp_adverse_positive`, but nothing states plainly that ledger `equity` is not the paper account's PnL; a partially filled or rejected order would not perturb the curve. (d) paper.py's own text says "account reads are part of the same owner-gated seam as submit()"; the bot does live paper GETs through its own class while citing paper.py as the authority for the submission gate. Disclosed as read-only GETs, not as an override of that line. Minor robustness gap: an outage longer than the 400-day fetch window would silently drop unsettled sessions, and the >5-session discontinuity rule is documented but not enforced in code. None of these touch evidence integrity today (zero settled sessions, zero orders), so the headline stands as written.

result.headline: B22B ORB entry-slippage now measured across all 30 pinned days (429 triggered stock-days): median 0 bp of R, verdict NOT_YET_FATAL, but p90 1181 / p95 1654 bp of R exceed the paper's own 800 bp per-trade edge — and short-borrow is now sourced, showing 36 of the 100 ORB names cannot be shorted at any price.
result.detail:
SLIPPAGE (B22B, finished). The first pass died at day 11/30 with all results in RAM. I added per-stock-day checkpointing plus backoff-retry on transient transport failures (429/5xx/reset/timeout) to the RUNNER ONLY (/home/anont/.claude/jobs/5d56bbe0/tmp/b22b_runner.py), added a `--summarise` read-only mode and an `i/n` worker partition over the pinned days, then ran 3 workers to completion. The frozen harness was never touched: sha256 still a0f1b4c4…, verified equal to the preregistration. Checkpointing was proven under a real SIGTERM (a day resumed at symbol 16/20).

Result: 30/30 pinned days complete, 580 stock-days recorded, 429 TRIGGERED, 150 NO_TRIGGER, 1 REFUSED, 202 long / 227 short. At the 100 ms rung (the preregistered verdict rung): median 0 bp of R (166 of 429 fill exactly at the stop; 213 adverse, 50 favourable), p75 547, p90 1181, p95 1654, max 3616 bp of R -> verdict NOT_YET_FATAL, the most favourable verdict the preregistration permits. In bp of notional: mean 0.81, p75 2.48, p90 5.62, p95 8.99, max 31.67. Latency ladder shows exactly the gap the prereg wanted visible: p90 goes 233 -> 1181 -> 1486 -> 1835 bp of R across 0/100/500/1000 ms.

Three honest caveats recorded in the artifact. (1) The median is fine, the TAIL is not: ~1 entry in 10 costs more than 1181 bp of R against the 800 bp of R the paper reports as its whole per-trade edge. (2) CAPACITY is the weak point, not slippage — resting size at the touched side at the trigger instant has median 16 shares and p90 369 shares, so the measured gap is the cost of the first handful of shares and a real order walks the book. The prereg's falsification condition has a size clause and this fails it. (3) One post-hoc sensitivity is included and labelled as post-hoc, not as the result: the preregistered trigger is "first trade at or through the stop", and SIP includes odd-lot/out-of-sequence prints (e.g. TSLA 2025-03-12 sell stop at $244.30 triggered by a $223.92 print while the bid was $248.07 on a 1-share quote). Only 1 of 429 is more than 1 ATR through the stop and it sits in the FAVOURABLE tail, so removing it makes the result slightly worse, not better. Also noted: 2025-01-09 screens zero candidates because the US market was closed (Carter day of mourning) — the pinned sample was drawn from weekdays, not an exchange calendar; reported, not silently replaced.

REJECTED OPTIMISATION worth recording: early-stopping the trade paging would have cut runtime several-fold, but I verified Alpaca SIP trade pages are NOT monotonic in time (NVDA, 138,665 trades over 14 pages, monotonic=False), so truncation could miss an earlier-timestamped breach. Left slow rather than subtly wrong.

BORROW (new, research/B22G_BORROW_COST.json). Four sources, kept separate. (a) Alpaca GET /v2/assets on the account we would trade — complete over all 100 ORB names; gives shortable/easy_to_borrow/borrow_status/margin_requirement_short but is a STATUS, not a rate. (b) Alpaca's published schedule: $0 locate+borrow on ETB for Trading API users; HTB daily fee = sum(HTB short MV x that stock's HTB rate)/360; rates only via GET /v1/locates/quotes on the live host, which returns 403 for this key (no HTB entitlement) and 404 on paper — documented as unobtainable by us. (c) IBKR's shortable-securities feed for the actual rate: ftp3/ftp.interactivebrokers.com are unreachable from this host, so I used the ChartExchange republication and labelled it second-hand; it bot-blocked after ~25 names, so coverage is 25/100 and the other 75 are recorded as UNKNOWN, not zero. (d) D'Avolio (2002) JFE 66 as an independent order-of-magnitude check (91% general collateral at ~17 bp/yr, ~9% specials at 4.30%/yr).

Typical rates measured: easy-to-borrow median 0.33%/yr (n=14, range 0.25–10.58); hard-to-borrow median 10.28%/yr (n=11), p90 123.23%, max 259.96%. That confirms the warning the old 30 bp default carried in its own source string. The bigger finding is one a rate cannot express: all 36 hard-to-borrow names in the ORB pool are also shortable=False at Alpaca — not an expensive short, no short at any price. Cross-referenced against the B22B signal set: the short leg is the MAJORITY of the rule's signals (227 of 429), and 17.2% of those shorts are in names unshortable at this broker today. That removes trades rather than pricing them.

WIRING (scripts/trading_bot/costs.py). MEASURED_B22B.assert_available() changed from a flat refusal ("B22B has never been run") to a gate on research/B22B_SLIPPAGE_RESULT.json existing AND reporting all 30 pinned days — delete or truncate it and the rig refuses again, so a partial pass can never present itself as the measurement. (1) "Cannot be shorted at any price" is refuted by the artifact's own data. This wording is not confined to the summary — it is baked into measured_borrow_annual()'s source string in scripts/trading_bot/costs.py (~line 462) and into DECISIONS.md, so it prints in every cost report. So the exit (a stop-loss market order or MOC, which B22B explicitly does not measure) is now charged 0.81 bp and no spread at all. Measured: 0.81 bp/turnover, 1.63 bp round trip. retail_taker_costs(): 2.5 bp / 5.0 bp. A task whose acceptance is "so net returns are honest" ships a cost model 3.07x cheaper than the unmeasured lower bound it replaces. The docstring says "ENTRY ONLY ... result.headline: The T2 cost model is now charged PER SIDE: the exit leg, which was silently getting a zero half-spread because it inherited B22B's entry-only number, costs 4.05 bp, taking the honest ORB round trip from 1.63 bp to 5.59 bp (3.44x), and the borrow narrative's wrong denominator (36/100 -> 8/52) and overclaim ("cannot be shorted at any price" -> "not shortable at Alpaca") are corrected against the data.
result.detail:
1) PER-SIDE COSTS. `CostModel` no longer has a side-agnostic spread/slippage term. New `split_turnover(previous, target)` in costs.py decomposes every position change into the leg that OPENS exposure and the leg that CLOSES it (+1 -> -1 is a 1.0 exit AND a 1.0 entry), asserted to sum exactly to the old |dpos| so it reallocates turnover rather than inventing charge. engine.py L~596 now calls it and passes both legs; `BacktestResult` reports `entry_turnover`/`exit_turnover` per segment so the split is auditable. The old call sites fail LOUDLY rather than cheaply: `spread_and_slippage_fraction()` and a one-argument `trade_cost_fraction()` both raise Refused naming the defect, and a `CostModel` built without an exit side refuses to construct.

EXIT PRICING, sourced. `exit_half_spread` = max(2.5 bp Dyhrberg/Shkilko/Werner JFE 168 (2025); half of B22B's OWN measured mean quoted spread over the 429 triggered stock-days = 4.818/2 = 2.409 bp) = 2.5 bp — two unrelated sources within 4% of each other, and the larger is charged per the guardrail. `exit_extra_slippage` = the entry's measured magnitude charged AGAIN (1.5452 bp) under a new provenance `ADVERSE_PROXY_FOR_AN_UNMEASURED_LEG` so it can never read as a measurement of the exit; rationale is that a stop-out is triggered BY the adverse move and an MOC takes the auction clear, so neither is systematically gentler than a stop entry, and the alternative was zero. `retail_taker_costs()` now mirrors entry on exit by default (5.0 bp round trip); `stress_ladder()` applies its rung to BOTH sides; zarattini stays a 0 bp straw man and `zero_cost_model()` a 0 bp diagnostic.

CORRECTED ROUND TRIP: 1.6265 bp -> 5.5904 bp (entry 1.5452 + exit 4.0452), i.e. the old wiring was 3.44x too cheap — matching the verifier's "~3x". The measured model is now MORE expensive than `retail_taker_costs()` (5.00 bp), which is the right way round since it is the one carrying an unmeasured leg. It is no longer biased cheap: every uncertain term is charged on the adverse side and each says so in its own source string.

4) DECONTAMINATED MEAN. Verified the verifier's claim from the raw 31 per-day checkpoints: the 1-ATR filter does NOT remove the cited TSLA 2025-03-12 case (sell stop $244.30 triggered by a $223.92 print against a $248.07 bid = 0.923 ATR through, notional slippage -152 bp); it removes only QQQ. Built a full ladder into `research/B22B_SLIPPAGE_RESULT.json -> t6_decontamination_ladder` (post-hoc, labelled, alongside the preregistered numbers): unfiltered 0.8132 bp, 1.0 ATR 0.8525 (+4.8%), 0.5 ATR 1.2104 (+48.8%), 0.1 ATR 1.5452 (+90.0%), 0.05 ATR 1.6549 (+103.5%) — reproducing +49%/+90% exactly. Default threshold is 0.1 ATR, defensible because R is DEFINED as 10% of ATR(14), so it is "the trigger print was more than one full R beyond the stop" in the paper's own risk unit, and it is the adverse end. `atr_filter=None` still returns the raw mean and the component then calls itself CONTAMINATED. Percentiles stay unfiltered (every removed point is favourable, so that is the conservative read).

2)+3) LANGUAGE AND DENOMINATOR. Measured from the checkpoints + B22G: the ORB rule ACTUALLY screened 52 of the 100-name pool, of which 8 are hard-to-borrow = 15.4% (not 36 of 100, which is the screen INPUT); 7 of the 11 HTB names with an obtainable IBKR rate have shares AVAILABLE to borrow there at 2.32-259.96%/yr; and 38 of the 39 unavailable short signals are leveraged/inverse ETPs (SQQQ 10, TSLL 10, SOXL 8, MSTU 6, SOXS 4) — an Alpaca PRODUCT restriction — with exactly 1 an ordinary common stock (ONDS). Written to `research/B22G_BORROW_COST.json -> t6_correction_screened_universe`; `measured_borrow_annual()` now reads it, says "NOT SHORTABLE AT ALPACA", and REFUSES if the block is missing rather than reverting to the old wording. DECISIONS.md gets a new entry that withdraws both overstated claims by name.

5) TESTS CATCH THE OLD BEHAVIOUR. tests/test_t2_backtest_harness.py: 101 -> 113 tests, all passing. New `PerSideCostTests` (12) plus the existing spread-not-charged-twice test extended to require a NON-zero exit. Negative control run: a rebuilt pre-T6 model (exit inheriting the entry components, contaminated mean) FAILS the exit-costs-more assertion, the >=5 bp round-trip assertion and the lumped-turnover refusal, and passes against the fix — so these tests catch the regression rather than lock in the new numbers. `python -m scripts.trading_bot selftest` runs clean. Full repo suite: 4318 passed / 12 skipped / 3526 subtests, with one PRE-EXISTING unrelated failure (tests/test_mutation_sweep.py memecoin staging guard tripping on research/b11a/b11a_creates.jsonl, dated 11 Aug, untouched by this work).

verdict.reason:
The headline survives and reproduces. The per-side fix is structurally real, not cosmetic: engine.py:623 calls split_turnover(previous, pos) and hands both legs to trade_cost_fraction, which prices them at different rates; spread_and_slippage_fraction() and the one-argument trade_cost_fraction() both raise Refused by name; a CostModel built without an exit side refuses to construct. I confirmed engine.py is the only consumer in the T2 rig. Arithmetic verified live: entry 0 + 1.5452, exit 2.5 + 1.5452, round trip 5.5904 bp against the pre-T6 2 x 0.81324 = 1.62648 bp, i.e. 3.437x. That is honest work and I reproduced it.

ONE REAL DEFECT, and it is in the forbidden direction. measured_exit_half_spread() (costs.py:750-754) reads result["spread_bp"], which build_slippage_result.py:113 computed with FLOOR integer division: (spread_micros * 10_000) // fill_micros. Recomputing the same 429 observations exactly from the same checkpoints: the mean quoted spread is 5.3261 bp, not 4.8182 bp, so the measured half-spread in this universe is 2.6631 bp, not 2.4091 bp. Three consequences: (1) max(2.5 literature, measured) resolves the WRONG WAY — the honest measured half-spread EXCEEDS the literature number and should have been the binding term; (2) the shipped round trip should be 5.7535 bp, so the delivered model is ~2.8% cheaper than its own data supports, and the ratio is 3.54x not 3.44x; (3) the source string printed in every cost report ("mean 4.818 bp full spread ... i.e. a 2.409 bp half-spread in this exact universe") understates the measured spread by ~10%, and the "two unrelated sources within 4% of each other" corroboration narrative is an artifact of the truncation. So the DETAIL sentence "It is no longer biased cheap: every uncertain term is charged on the adverse side" is FALSE as written, and the guardrail "when uncertain, cost MORE" is violated on this one term. Required precision: set exit_half_spread to the exactly-computed 2.6631 bp (round trip 5.7535 bp) or recompute spread_bp in centi-bp, and withdraw the "no longer biased cheap" sentence.

Primary rung charges 0.37 bp/day: SEC s31 at 0.278 bp (top of the 2016-2026 range, both periods), FINRA TAF $0.000166/share charged on every share (~2x over-charge, conservative), borrow at B22G's MEASURED 33 bp/yr ETB. Stress ladder per leg vs T3's first-party h=1.43 bp: 0 cost +1.21 bp; primary +0.84; 0.5h -0.59; h -2.02; 2h -4.88; 4h -10.60. Half a half-spread per leg kills it, so M0 (unperformed) is now load-bearing for TWO dead candidates.

TAX, OWNER-FACING - and EDGE_SHORTLIST's framing was WRONG. For a one-day capture there is NO rate differential: the dividend is non-qualified ordinary income (a 1-day hold can never meet the 61-in-121-day test, IRC 1(h)(11)(B)(iii)) but the offsetting price fall is a SHORT-TERM capital loss, taxed at the same ordinary rates. The real obstacle is loss USABILITY under IRC 1211(b). Per year at 50% long / 221 event-days / 0.613% mean yield: +67.7% of equity in ordinary dividend income, -65.9% in short-term capital losses the strategy generates no gains to absorb, to earn +1.86% pre-tax. Case A (losses fully absorbed elsewhere): +1.21%/yr at 35%. Case B (standalone taxable, the default): -21.8%/yr at 35% (-14.4% at 24%, -25.8% at 40.8%); the $3,000/yr deduction recovers 4.6% of the losses at $100k. Break-even needs drop-off ratio < 1-t = 0.65; measured 0.95. ANSWER: #2 does not clear the bar after tax, and did not clear it before tax either. A tax-deferred account removes the tax objection entirely but the statistical verdict is unchanged - stated because it is an owner-disposable account-type question that should not sink a FUTURE candidate that passes on the statistics.

EXPLORATORY, FLAGGED AND BURNED. Exiting at the ex-date OPENING auction (excluded from the grid in advance) is +3.72 bp/day held out (t 3.29), +3.63 bp vs the same-day non-ex-dividend control (t 3.18, permutation p 0.042): the residual appears overnight and is given back intraday. No verdict follows, and I record explicitly that I have now looked at 2022-2026 for it, so that period is BURNED - any pre-registration of it needs a prospective forward test. Its tax arithmetic is identical and just as fatal.

NOMINATION + FORK FOR THE OWNER (T7_RESULT.md s9). Ranked successor is #3 turn-of-month, nominated as ranked but recommended AGAINST: ~60 held-out month-ends, after T7 just died on a null 2.4 bp wide at n=1,019. Recommendation: spend the next slice on M0 (bounded, a measurement not a search, both dead candidates rest on it), then #4 spin-off forced-selling drift (U=4, highest uniqueness available; its 243 spin-off records are already on disk from this run's universe-wide sweep). Third option: pre-register the close-to-open variant as a prospective forward test. Scope call left to the owner, not taken.

Independent sanity checks run before trusting the rig: the equal-weight non-ex-dividend control underperformed SPY by -1.36 bp/day on design event-days (-3.0%/yr), reproducing the known RSP-vs-SPY gap for 2016-2021 which the rig was not built to reproduce; and the identity excess = yield x (1 - drop-off ratio) reconciled to 0.1064 bp both ways on the design period, ruling out an arithmetic bug behind the negative result.

The headline is fully supported by the artifacts and, more importantly, by independent re-execution: re-running the design phase reproduces the frozen config byte-for-byte (sha256 2f25e00c…) and re-running the held-out test reproduces T7_HELDOUT_RESULT.json with zero differences on every leaf value. All eight design trials are genuinely negative and the frozen pick is genuinely the argmax of design net annualised Sharpe. Both failing gates recompute by hand (DSR benchmark 0.05940, z −1.431, Φ 0.0762; permutation p 0.213 with a null that is if anything generous to the strategy because it embeds the equal-weight drag). The tax arithmetic recomputes exactly (0.5 × 221 × 0.613% = 67.71% ordinary dividend income; 67.71 − 1.857 = 65.86% short-term capital loss; −21.84%/yr at 35%; break-even ratio < 1−t = 0.65 against a measured 0.95; $3,000/$65,856 = 4.6%), and the correction of EDGE_SHORTLIST's 'rate differential' framing to an IRC §1211(b) loss-USABILITY problem is legally correct — a 1-day hold cannot satisfy §1(h)(11)(B)(iii) and the offsetting short-term loss carries the same ordinary rates. The owner-facing answer (does not clear the bar after tax, and did not clear it before tax either; a tax-deferred account removes the tax objection but not the statistical verdict) is stated as an owner-disposable account-type question rather than decided. No guardrail was violated: HEAD is unchanged at 7c5c870, no order endpoint is reachable from any T7 code path, T3's frozen artifacts were not touched, and the costs.py edit is one additive enum member whose own definition requires the accompanying half-spread stress rung that §5 supplies. Three cosmetic imprecisions, none in the flattering direction: (1) T7_RESULT.md §1's '0.1064 bp both ways' reconciliation is the EVENT-equal-weighted mean excess (I recomputed it at 0.10641 bp, so the number is real) but it reconciles against an implied event-weighted ratio of 0.9983 that appears nowhere, while §4 reports 0.9748 dollar-weighted and 0.9994 day-clustered — three unlabelled weightings in one document; (2) '~2.9 bp/event' is the held-out dollar-weighted residual (2.92 bp verified) presented in §9 as if general, where the design equivalent is 1.58 bp dollar-weighted / 0.11 bp event-weighted; (3) §1 labels 6.1 as 'median events per day' when the underlying JSON key is mean_events_per_day. The one substantive weakness is that the test is underpowered — 58.9 bp/day of portfolio noise against a ~1.2 bp signal at n=1,019 — so DEAD here means 'the pre-registered kill conditions fired', not 'the mechanism is proven absent'; the document says exactly that ('the mechanism is visible and the trade is not there') and does not overclaim. The exploratory close-to-open variant (+3.72 bp, t 3.29) is explicitly refused as evidence and the held-out period is explicitly recorded as burned for it, which is the honest handling. tasks.title: M0: measure whether MOC/MOO orders actually fill at the official auction print, and at what cost
tasks.why: Both dead candidates (#1 pressure-reversal, #2 ex-dividend) assumed MOC/MOO orders fill at the official close/open auction price with ZERO spread -- the auction rail. That assumption is unmeasured (M0) and load-bearing: their own stress ladders show half a half-spread per leg kills them. If auction fills are not clean/free, that is decisive on its own and reshapes every future candidate cost model.
tasks.acceptance: PRIMARY (answerable now from data we hold): using SIP official auction prints (/v2/stocks/auctions, back to 2016) plus surrounding NBBO quotes and trades, quantify how achievable the official closing/opening print actually is -- e.g. auction print vs the closing-second NBBO midpoint and vs the volume-weighted closing minute, across liquid and less-liquid names, as a distribution in bp. State whether the zero-spread auction-rail assumption holds and, if not, what half-spread a MOC/MOO leg should really be charged. SECONDARY (optional, forward): place a bounded batch of small PAPER MOC/LOC/MOO orders for the next session(s) and compare realized fill to the official print, noting this accrues over real sessions. This is a MEASUREMENT, not a search -- no strategy. Write research/trading_bot/M0_AUCTION_FILLS.md and, if it changes the number, feed the honest exit/entry auction cost back into scripts/trading_bot/costs.py.
guardrails: PAPER account ONLY if any orders are placed; flatten and verify 0 open positions/orders at the end. Never a live/real-money order.
Report honestly: if fills deviate from the official print it likely invalidates the auction-rail premise of #1 and #2 -- say so plainly.
Do not git commit.

result.headline: M0 measured: the zero-spread auction-rail charge SURVIVES for the top-500-ADV universe (official closing print exists on 99.96% of symbol-days, median $37M cleared), but the print is at the closing NBBO midpoint only 1.9% of the time and availability collapses to 62% past ADV rank 3000 — so neither dead candidate died of its cost model.
result.detail:
MEASUREMENT. New harness scripts/m0_auction_fills.py: Alpaca SIP /v2/stocks/auctions + NBBO quotes + 1-min raw bars, 66 days seeded (20260817), 6 per calendar year 2016-2026, six ADV-rank tiers (1-50, 51-200, 201-500, 501-1500, 1501-3000, 3001-6000), 15 names per tier per day. 64 days collected (two 2016-01 days have no month m-1 screen, same limit T3 recorded); one early close (2019-11-29) excluded as T3/T7 did. Final: 63 sessions, 5,670 symbol-days.

The claim was decomposed into four parts. C1 (a print exists), C2 (where it sits), C3 (how big it is) are answerable from the tape and were measured. C4 (our broker's order joins the cross) is NOT answerable from history and remains unmeasured.

C1 AVAILABILITY. Official close print: A 99.89%, B 100.00%, C 100.00%, D 99.47%, E 94.60%, F 62.12%. Open print: 99.89/100/100/99.79/98.73/77.25%. Top-500 proxy (A+B+C, n=2,835): 99.96% both legs.

C2 PLACEMENT — the decisive table. Where the closing print sits in the closing NBBO, pooled n=5,250: at bid 27.4%, at ask 29.7%, inside-not-mid 9.9%, AT MID 1.9%, below bid 14.6%, above ask 16.5%. Mega-caps clear OUTSIDE the closing NBBO on 48.7% of days. |print - closing mid| median 2.43 bp (A 1.61, C 1.83, D 2.26, E 4.61, F 11.34), p95 19.1 bp; expressed in half-spreads the median is exactly 1.00 in EVERY tier and the p25 is 1.00 pooled. |print - VWAP(15:59)| median 3.46 bp. |print - 15:59 last trade| median 1.89 bp, mean 5.21, p95 17.95.

Stated explicitly in the doc: this gap is NOT a cost for a backtest that marks at the print and executes at the print (T3's MOO exit, T7's both legs). It becomes a real unmodelled cost the moment a backtest marks at a mid/bar-close/VWAP and claims auction execution.

C3 SIZE. Median closing auction notional: A $104.7M, B $37.8M, C $15.6M, D $3.4M, E $0.55M, F $14.2k. Opening auction ~7x smaller (top-500 median $4.8M, p05 $669k). The closing cross is 2.5x the entire last minute's volume at the median. Capacity for a T3-shaped 477-name book, using p05 opening auctions at a 1% participation ceiling: ~$3.2M of capital ($16M at 5%).

OPEN LEG. |print - first post-print NBBO mid| median 11.3 bp pooled (A 3.4, D 14.9), p95 108.7 bp — but the 09:30 NBBO is itself a median 20.7 bp wide, and against the opening minute's own VWAP the print is only 1.38 bp away, shrinking to 0.00 in thin names because there the print IS the minute. Honest read: the opening print is executable and dominant-volume, but low-certainty; prefer the close where a candidate has the choice.

BROKER MECHANICS (Alpaca docs, fetched 2026-08-17). MOC/LOC = tif=cls, MOO/LOO = tif=opg. cls submissions REJECTED 15:50-19:00 ET — T3's D2 15:50 cutoff confirmed at the broker level, not just the exchange. opg REJECTED 09:28-19:00. Routed to primary exchange, "per the exchange's auction rules" — which is a mechanism description, not a guarantee, i.e. exactly C4.

VERDICT ON #1 AND #2 (guardrail 2, and it went the opposite way to the task's hypothesis, so it is said plainly). M0 does NOT invalidate the auction-rail premise for the universe they traded, and does not revive them either. T3 stays dead on DSR 0.9379 vs 0.95; T7 stays dead on permutation p=0.213 and DSR 0.076. T3's fourth stress rung (h entry + h exit) turns out to have been OVER-conservative for a top-500 MOO exit. What the measurement does kill is the shortlist's FRAMING — "fills at the official price with zero spread" is half right: there is no spread to cross, and there is also no midpoint.

EXPLORATORY, LABELLED NOT PRE-REGISTERED. (a) Reversion of the print's deviation overnight: pooled slope -0.597, t -4.50, but R2 0.0039 and the tier slopes range -3.72 to +1.41 with two below -1, which is not physically sensible. Reported as UNRESOLVED, not as a finding. (b) The print leans the way the last ten minutes leaned: dev ~ r10 slope +0.04639, t = +11.69, n=4,964 (quintile means -0.26 bp to +0.52 bp). Firm, and a warning for any future close-window candidate. The follow-on regressions (overnight ~ r10, and ~ r10 + dev) are t = -0.81 and -0.60/-1.25 — this estimator is not T3's and confirms nor refutes nothing.

COSTS.PY — ADDITIVE, no existing number changed, tests/test_t2_backtest_harness.py 113/113 still pass (full suite 4,547 passed / 1 pre-existing unrelated failure in test_mutation_sweep.py about research/b11a/b11a_creates.jsonl). (1) New SlippageProvenance.MEASURED_M0_AUCTION_PRINT, gated in assert_available() on the M0 JSON existing AND covering >=5,000 symbol-days, same pattern as MEASURED_B22B; its own text states it does NOT claim C4. (2) EXCHANGE_MECHANISM_UNVERIFIED_FILL's text amended — it used to say M0 was UNPERFORMED; it now names which half is done and still requires an accompanying real-half-spread stress rung. Kept, not deleted, so T7_HELDOUT_RESULT.json stays readable. (3) New measured_auction_leg(leg, tier) returning (half_spread=0 bp, extra_slippage=non-fill provision read from the M0 result), REFUSING for tiers E and F rather than extrapolating a zero. Non-fill provisions: A 0.0019 bp, B 0.0000, C 0.0000, D 0.0187, E 0.4520 (refused), F 9.1622 (refused) — P(no print) x a full quoted spread to unwind by hand, a FLOOR that excludes overnight gap risk.

SECONDARY (live paper) NOT RUN, and why: guardrail 1 requires 0 open positions/orders verified at session end, and an on-close order satisfying that inside one agent run is one CANCELLED before the auction, which measures nothing. A real C4 test holds a live cls order through 16:00 and accrues across sessions — a process/authorisation call that is the owner's. §10 of the document is the ready-to-authorise protocol: PAPER only, 20 symbols/session (5 each tiers A-D), 1 share, cls day 1 / opg to flatten, >=10 sessions, ~$1k paper notional/session, primary metric = fill rate and (fill - print) in bp; paper.py's submit() still refuses by construction and would need the owner-gated diff first.

NOT DONE / FLAGGED FOR THE OWNER: no FINDINGS.md index entry was written (that is a verdict-writing call in this programme's convention); impact is not priced (only participation ratios); the overnight gap risk of a non-fill is not priced.
result.guardrail_note: (1) PAPER-only / no orders: NO order of any kind was submitted, on any account. Only read-only endpoints were touched — data.alpaca.markets for auctions/quotes/bars, and paper-api.alpaca.markets for /v2/calendar, /v2/assets, plus a final read-only /v2/positions and /v2/orders check which returned 0 rows each. The live host api.alpaca.markets was never contacted and is refused by construction in scripts/trading_bot/data.py. paper.py's submit() remains unimplemented and was not implemented. (2) Honest reporting: the result went AGAINST the task's stated expectation — the auction-rail premise survives for the universe #1 and #2 traded — and the document leads with that in its first paragraph rather than burying it, while equally plainly recording the two things that do count against the framing (the print is at the mid 1.9% of the time; availability collapses to 62% past ADV rank 3000) and the half of M0 that stays unmeasured (C4, the broker's fill). The unresolved reversion regression is reported as unresolved rather than as its flattering pooled row. (3) No git commit, no git add, no branch, no push — verified with git status: all five artifacts sit uncommitted in the working tree.

verdict.rigor: Kind = MEASUREMENT, so leakage/DSR/permutation/freeze-then-test are largely N/A and are correctly not invoked for a verdict. Leakage: the only lookahead is the disclosed "name must have a bar in month m" survivorship screen, which touches selection, not any measured quantity; the closing-NBBO reference is the last quote before 16:00 (verified: 5,246/5,250 quote timestamps land in the 15:59 ET minute, 4 in the fallback window), so no post-print information enters the reference. Out-of-sample: not applicable; sample is pre-seeded (20260817), stratified 6 days/calendar year 2016-2026, disclosed before analysis. DSR/permutation: N/A, no strategy or search is claimed; the two regressions that could have been dressed up as findings (§8a reversion, §8b P2/P3) are labelled EXPLORATORY and explicitly refused as evidence, including the flattering pooled row. Freeze-then-test: N/A, but the T3/T7 preregistration SHA256s are byte-identical to their frozen configs (401fd377..., 7bd072a7...), so no frozen artifact was touched. Reproduction: I recomputed C1/C2/C3 from research/data/m0_cache/records.json.gz independently — availability 99.89/100/100/99.47/94.60/62.12% and top-500 99.965%, placement at bid 27.39/at ask 29.70/at mid 1.94/outside 31.07%, |dev| median 2.432 bp p95 19.08, half-spread ratio median 1.000, notionals A $104.71M / B $37.79M / top-500 $37.0M, open p05 $670k, print/last-minute-volume 2.51x, |print-VWAP1559| 3.46 bp, open |dev| 11.34 bp vs 20.71 bp half-spread and 1.38 bp vs opening VWAP — all match the document to rounding. Provisions, reversion slopes and D3 regressions in the JSON match the doc exactly. tests/test_t2_backtest_harness.py 113/113 pass. Alpaca doc claims (cls rejected 15:50-19:00 ET, opg rejected 09:28-19:00 ET, "routed to the primary exchange ... per the exchange's auction rules") verified against the live doc page.
verdict.reason: The claim survives a hostile re-derivation. (a) No guardrail violated. No order was submitted by this task: the paper account holds 0 positions and 0 open orders; the only 3 orders that exist (SPY, 1 share, tif=cls/opg) were created 2026-08-16T19:56Z and cancelled within 1.4s — ~12h BEFORE the M0 run (cache written 2026-08-17 10:07 CEST) and immediately before paper.py's own mtime, i.e. a prior session's broker probe, not this one. paper.py submit() still raises Refused; the live host was never contacted; nothing was committed (HEAD is still 7c5c870, all five artifacts untracked); no pinned/frozen file was edited and both preregistration hashes still match. costs.py is additive — no existing number changed, and measured_auction_leg has no callers, so no prior result can move. (b) Rigor as above; the measurement replicates end to end from raw records. (c) The headline is supported but carries two presentational overstatements the owner should see, neither of which reverses a conclusion. FIRST, "the print is at the mid only 1.9% of the time" is substantially a tick-grid artifact: 3,838 of 5,250 symbol-days (73%) have an odd-cent spread whose midpoint is off the penny grid, so at-mid is arithmetically impossible; conditional on the mid being attainable the rate is 6.1% (86/1,412), and for 2-cent spreads it is 9.2%. The companion "median exactly 1.00 half-spread in EVERY tier" is near-tautological where the spread is one tick (53% of rows). The qualitative claim — the auction is not the midpoint, and 31% of prints clear outside the NBBO — still holds, but the 1.9% figure is not the clean economic fact the doc's "decisive table" framing implies. SECOND, "availability collapses to 62% past ADV rank 3000" is sensitive to an undisclosed-in-impact condition-code choice: the harness accepts only condition '6' (close) and 'O' (open). I queried /v2/stocks/auctions directly and confirmed that 160 symbol-days (142 in tier F, 17 in E, 1 in A) carry a closing record under condition 'M' (Market Center Official Close, typically 100 shares at Arca/BZX) with no '6'. Counting those would move F to ~77% and A to 100%. The '6'-only reading is defensible — an M-only record looks like an exchange-published official close with no cross to join, which is the right answer to "is there an auction to fill in" — and it errs conservative, since it is what drives costs.py's refusal for tiers E/F. But the doc does not state that the number depends on this choice. THIRD, the weakest part of the change is epistemic, not numeric: the new SlippageProvenance.MEASURED_M0_AUCTION_PRINT returns half_spread = 0 under a "MEASURED" label while C4 — that our broker's order joins the cross, the only thing the zero actually rests on — is unmeasured, and unlike EXCHANGE_MECHANISM_UNVERIFIED_FILL its text does not mandate an accompanying real-half-spread stress rung. It discloses the gap in its own string, and nothing consumes it yet, so this is a latent softening of a safeguard rather than a live error. Minor factual slips in costs.py comments: "65 full sessions" (63) and "61.8%" (62.1%). Everything the executor flagged as not done is genuinely not done and honestly flagged — notably research/FINDINGS.md still reads "M0 still unperformed", which is now stale and is an owner-level index call.

result.headline: Spin-off forced-selling drift (equity edge candidate #4) is DEAD BY INSUFFICIENT POWER: only 62 tradeable held-out events exist, giving a minimum detectable effect of 5.51% against a 2.40% literature effect — and it also fails all three statistical gates (net −0.82%/event t −0.39, permutation p=0.627, DSR 0.063).
result.detail:
FREEZE-THEN-TEST, done properly. Pre-registration T9_PREREGISTRATION.md written and sha256-hashed (cd36949cce70cce4fabe1a268b549a0e99a6518e1be3f2e41a3f4fcf16715510) at 08:06 UTC BEFORE any price was divided by any other price; only record counts and bar-presence checks preceded it. scripts/t9_evaluate.py refuses to run if that hash changes. No fitted parameter exists anywhere: the configuration was declared a priori from EDGE_SHORTLIST.md's own pre-data wording ("1-60 trading days"), because the design window turned out to be unusable.

FINDING 1 — the "243 spin-off records already on disk" claim (in FINDINGS.md §10 and T7_RESULT.md §9) was this programme's own count and it was wrong about the world. 243 raw -> 228 unique by provider id -> 225 unique by (source,new,ex_date) -> 177 with a ticker-shaped new_symbol (48 are contingent value rights, escrow/contingent entitlements and bare CUSIPs like 878CVR018, 007ESC031) -> minus 13 new==source restatements, 15 duplicate stubs, 39 that never traded, 23 sub-$5, 5 sub-$1M dollar volume -> 82 tradeable events. Held out: 62 at H=60. Design: 14. I verified the 39 "no entry price" drops are genuine: all 39 have NO daily bar at all in the 5 sessions after ex-date, not a missing auction print.
