result.detail:
METHOD. Pre-registration `T10_PREREGISTRATION.md` sha256 7f66195125718298c5eb545ae936e9bac89ca537482009b2e8e531a75bbb6d99, frozen 2026-08-17T09:11:58Z before any price was divided by any other price for this candidate (only counts were read first). Design 2016-02-01→2021-12-31 (1,468 sessions), held out 2022-01-03→2026-08-14 (1,140 sessions), 1,242,102 symbol-days, both legs official auction prints from the T3 cache (3.62M prints). 8 trials declared: Family A = market-level paired difference (SPY, EW top-100/300/500); Family B = Lou-Polk-Skouras cross-sectional tug-of-war (K∈{21,63} x cut∈{0.10,0.20}). Selection = highest design net annualised Sharpe. Frozen config `T10_FROZEN_CONFIG.json` sha256 bc5531956560bab380b0518e2bbd4458bba6770e38e6d49dc7799b3eb3a84545 -> B3 (K=63, decile, top-500). `test` refuses to run without the frozen file. Held out run ONCE.

VERDICT: DEAD — UNDERPOWERED.
- Gate 1 net mean > 0: +1.482 bp/session, t +0.47 — passes meaninglessly.
- Gate 2 permutation p < 0.05: p = 0.0020 — passes, but see METHOD FINDING below.
- Gate 3 DSR >= 0.95 at trials=8: 0.3772 — FAILS. Observed per-obs Sharpe 0.01405 is BELOW the expected-max under the null, 0.02342. Below the chance ceiling. DSR at 24 trials: 0.277.
- Power label declared in advance: MDE 1.304 annualised Sharpe vs benchmarks 0.903 (design) / 0.382 (B22F) -> UNDERPOWERED.
Design->held-out Sharpe shrinkage +0.903 -> +0.221. All 8 design trials positive (the T3 shape).

FRICTION, and it is a SEPARATE death that needs no power argument. Turnover measured and asserted, not assumed: 3.9989 of gross notional traded and 1.9995 SOLD per session. SEC §31 alone = 0.556 bp/session = 138 bp/yr; total charged friction 193 bp/yr (M0 measured_auction_leg for the rail, non-fill provision at the dearest liquid tier, TAF on every share = deliberate 2x over-charge, B22G borrow on overnight short). Gross edge only +4.29%/yr. BREAK-EVEN = 0.370 bp per auction leg = 0.26 x the measured quoted half-spread of its own universe. Ladder: 0.5h -> −4.68%/yr, 1h -> −11.19%/yr, 2h -> −22.91%, 4h -> −41.93%. M0's unmeasured live half (C4) is now worth 1,414 bp/yr to this candidate — four dead candidates rest on it.

WHAT DID REPLICATE (declared diagnostics, held out, on auction prints): SPY overnight +7.29%/yr Sharpe 0.724 vs intraday +3.15%/yr Sharpe 0.284; EW500 +7.15%/0.670 vs +2.38%/0.228. The Lou-Polk-Skouras 2.5x asymmetry is real and reproduces on a second instrument and a later window (B22F had 0.87 vs 0.43). Harvesting it is what fails.

TWO METHOD FINDINGS.
(1) A cross-sectional label permutation is the WRONG instrument for a factor-loaded sorted RETURN series. p=0.0020 on a series with t=+0.47: the real decile book carries 3.88x the per-session dispersion of a random partition of the same names (105.5 bp vs 27.2 bp), and it is NOT market beta (β=−0.036, residual Sharpe unchanged). Report that ratio beside any permutation p on a sorted portfolio. Does not overturn T3 (its p and t agreed) but should be reported for it.
(2) DECLARED DEVIATION, found by auditing the code against the pre-registration's own timing sentence: the frozen signal's most recent term ends at C(t−1) — the print the overnight leg is entered at, which an MOC due at 15:50 cannot see (1 of 63 terms). Corrected to C(t−2), held-out net RISES +1.48 -> +2.97 bp and DSR 0.377 -> 0.571 — still failing 0.95, on a variant that is a 9th post-freeze trial. T3's lookahead was worth +half its result; T10's was worth MINUS half. Lookahead does not always flatter.

RIG CHECK before the held-out window was touched: EW top-500 full-day minus SPY full-day = −0.823 bp/day = −2.05%/yr, reproducing the known equal-weight-vs-cap-weight gap (RSP vs SPY ≈ −3 to −4%/yr) on a rig built for something else.

RECOMMENDATION (owner scope call, not taken autonomously). The binding constraint is now quantified: at 80% power, certifying a true annualised Sharpe on daily data needs (2.80/S)^2 years of held-out data — S=1.3 -> 4.6 yr, 1.0 -> 7.8, 0.8 -> 12.2, 0.5 -> 31.4, 0.3 -> 87.1. We hold 4.6 years held out. Every remaining directional shortlist candidate sits below Sharpe 0.5, so a fifth directional candidate buys another honest negative and no new information. Recommend the RISK/SIZING PIVOT, because both survivors of this whole programme (crash-filter drawdown, deadness screen) are distribution-shape claims rather than mean claims — which is exactly why they survived. Order: (1) M0's C4 live paper-order batch (bounded, days not years, now worth 1,414 bp/yr to any rail-dependent candidate); (2) risk/sizing work as pre-registered distribution-shape questions, including the overnight exposure of §6 framed as risk shaping — and noting it is NOT free (~70 bp/yr even at two legs a day, and levering back to full-day vol pays margin interest that consumes the difference). Alternatives stated so the owner chooses: #5 CEF discount reversion (note: `scripts/t12_cef_discount.py` and a t12 cache already exist on disk, so a peer seat appears to be on it), or pre-registering T7's close-to-open variant as a prospective FORWARD test.

GUARDRAILS. (1) Freeze before fitting: prereg hashed 09:11:58Z, first design run 09:21:39Z; negatives reported in full, including the two method defects found by self-audit. (2) T6-corrected per-side cost model used throughout with `costs.measured_auction_leg` (M0) on both legs, charged against exact per-name turnover via `costs.split_turnover`; full stress ladder plus the B19P frictionless diagnostic. (3) No git commit (HEAD still 7c5c870), read-only market data only, no orders placed. Note for the owner: `research/trading_bot/` is entirely untracked in git — every T3/T7/T9/T10 artifact is uncommitted, which is pre-existing and not something I changed.

DSR: yes — I recomputed Bailey/López de Prado from scratch: observed per-obs Sharpe 0.014045 vs expected-max 0.023421 at 8 trials, z −0.3127, DSR 0.3773 (reported 0.37719); the failure is robust to the trial count — even an undeflated PSR against zero is only 0.68. The declared diagnostics also replicate exactly (SPY overnight +7.2884%/Sharpe 0.7239 vs intraday +3.1542%/0.2838 on n=1055), as does the census (128 universe months, 1,648 symbols, 3,618,237 prints) and the rig check (EW500−SPY full day −0.823 bp/day = −2.05%/yr). The verdict DEAD is driven by the single pre-registered gate that failed (DSR 0.3772 < 0.95, observed Sharpe below the chance ceiling) and does not depend on any discretionary choice: the undeflated PSR-vs-zero is 0.68, and the post-hoc lookahead-corrected 9th trial reaches only 0.571. Guardrails hold: HEAD is still 7c5c870 (no commit), no order-placing code anywhere in the T10 scripts, only cached read-only market data, no pinned or frozen file altered (prereg and frozen config both predate every downstream artifact), and the blind memecoin window-2 material is untouched (`results_unlocked: false`; the supervisor_state.json change is the peer pipeline quarantining a failed stage, not a T10 action). TWO PRECISIONS, neither of which overturns the claim. (1) "Dead twice over / a SEPARATE death" is rhetorically stronger than the artifact: at the pre-registered primary rung the strategy is net POSITIVE (+2.30%/yr, t +0.47). The friction result is a sensitivity — it dies only if M0's unmeasured live-fill half (C4) is wrong by ≥0.26 of one measured half-spread. The result document and the pre-registration both state this explicitly (§7, §12), so it is disclosed rather than hidden, and the error direction is conservative; but a reader of the one-line headline would take a conditional for an established fact. This is the same limitation as T3/T7/T9, and the one genuine contamination (B22F's SPY split, which makes A1 non-blind) is disclosed in advance in prereg §0 and does not touch the selected configuration. Everything the claim asserts about the method findings — the wrong-instrument permutation argument and the lookahead that ran the other way — is supported by artifacts I checked and by numbers I reproduced.

result.detail:
FREEZE-THEN-TEST, exactly as T3/T7/T9. Pre-registration research/trading_bot/T11_PREREGISTRATION.md frozen at sha256 b2aa8c60419a5058437ba26a1df6093d7c85a752f9010a16322edf6ae43e9880 BEFORE any price was divided by any other price; scripts/t11_evaluate.py refuses on hash mismatch. Design 2020-2021, held out 2022-01-03 to 2026-08-14, run ONCE.

TWO BLOCKERS MEASURED BEFORE THE FREEZE, not assumed. (1) /v1/corporate-actions gives effective date and cash rate but no ANNOUNCEMENT date. The shortlist's own "cheap first step" was executed on 80 random deals (seed 20260817): a loose Benzinga headline rule recovers a date on 42/80 (52.5%) with roughly a one-in-three false-positive rate (matches include the acquiree ACQUIRING someone else, an activist letter, a litigation headline); a strict object-position rule recovers 14/80 (17.5%), bounded by 64% of delisted acquirees having no issuer name and by tickers being RECYCLED to live unrelated instruments (LMNX to a Defiance ETF, MIC to a 2x daily ETF). 17/80 acquirees have ZERO news items in the 760 days before close, and the recall failure concentrates in exactly the small under-covered deals the mechanism claims edge in. (2) The feed contains ONLY deals that COMPLETED -- a break leaves no corporate action of any type, so the left tail is structurally absent, not rare.

DESIGN RESPONSE: an ORACLE UPPER BOUND. The book is granted (A) completion -- it never takes a break loss -- and (B) the close date -- it enters exactly H sessions before the last trading day. Both favour the strategy and neither is available live, so a failure is a fortiori (the B19P "even trading for free loses" instrument applied to information instead of cost). Lookahead from Oracle B was fenced by a declared +20% discount cap (a pre-announcement entry shows as an implausible discount); the cap deletes only winners, so it is conservative.

HELD-OUT RESULT, H=63 (selected on the design window by the pre-declared criterion; design t: H=5 -0.92, H=21 +0.02, H=63 +1.80). All five gates fail:

- net mean excess over T-bills: -0.827%/event, t -0.985, annualised -2.81%, n=330
- event-label permutation vs T3 top-500 control pool: p_right = 0.876 (null median +0.88%, p95 +4.04%)
- DSR at 3 declared trials: 0.0391 (observed per-obs Sharpe -0.0188 against a chance ceiling of +0.0290); 0.0027 at 12 trials
- break gate: b* negative -- already below T-bills before a single deal breaks
All three horizons negative: H=5 -1.370% (t -2.56), H=21 -1.815% (t -2.77), H=63 -0.827%. Paired vs SPY -2.36%/event, t -2.58. Year by year 2022 +1.76 / 2023 -2.48 / 2024 +0.37 / 2025 -0.04 / 2026 -4.00.

NOT A FRICTION DEATH. Stress ladder at 0x / 0.5x / 1x / 2x / 4x the measured half-spread: -0.779 / -0.803 / -0.827 / -0.875 / -0.972%. Frictionless B19P diagnostic (every cost zero, regulatory included): -0.776%, t -0.92. The whole ladder spans 20 bp on an 83 bp loss. First equity candidate in this programme where cost is irrelevant. Half-spread measured first-party on the merger targets themselves, [15:59:59,16:00:00) ET on their actual entry days: 2.41 bp median held out (n=1,048 symbol-days over 750 days), 2.64 bp design.

THE FAT LEFT TAIL, MODELLED THREE WAYS (guardrail 2). Empirical held-out distribution: mean -0.83%, median +0.54%, sd 15.25%, skew -4.93, kurtosis 30.7, p01 -99.7%, min -102%, 33.6% of events lose. Break-even break rate b* reported across L in {-10,-20,-25,-30,-40}%.

THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING. The pre-declared symmetric |spread| <= 20% variant removes 13 tail events (3.9% of the book, mean -66.5% each) and gives the most favourable object this dataset can produce: n=317, +1.866%/event, t +6.87, +6.66%/yr over T-bills. The merger spread IS real and about the size the literature says. Applying the pre-registered b* formula to it: b*(L=-25%) = 6.68%, against a gate of >10% and a commonly quoted 5-10% deal-failure band -- it fails at every loss assumption of -20% or worse. So the spread is exactly the compensation for its own tail: precisely the null the shortlist wrote ("annualised spread capture equals the risk-free rate after deal-break losses"). This is the programme's first candidate killed by a TAIL rather than by the friction floor or the chance ceiling.

verdict.reason: The load-bearing claim survives my attack: candidate #5 is DEAD, it was genuinely frozen before fitting, and the whole verdict re-runs bit-for-bit from cache. The kill conditions that fired do not depend on any judgement call — the held-out net mean is negative, so DSR fails by arithmetic no matter what benchmark is used, and permutation p = 0.0539 fails on the gross series (net is worse). The multiple-testing discipline is real and is the most impressive part: trials 5/6 (raw discount level) came out at +12.9/+14.5 bp/wk out of sample with DSR 0.991/0.997, and the executor refused to promote them, instead attacking them in T12_DIAGNOSTICS.json and routing the fork to the owner. I verified all five attacks (persistence 0.814/0.791 vs 0.506/0.392 for the primary; NAV leg +9.45 vs +18.78 like-for-like; 57.19% short-leg borrowable; 131/360 survivorship magnitude with an explicit HEURISTIC_WARNING; and the self-correction on the equity-vs-bond regression) and they are all present, honestly caveated, and correctly labelled DIAGNOSTIC ONLY. ONE SUBSTANTIVE OVERSTATEMENT, which I could not talk myself out of: the history gate's "PASS" is wrong by a factor of two, and with it the claim's boast that the candidate "did not die of thin history but on the merits". The gate compares min-detectable annualised Sharpe 1.745 against a benchmark of 0.06/σ̂ = 1.859, where σ̂ = 3.227%/yr is measured on the implemented book, which is 0.5 long / 0.5 short (gross 1.0). Pontiff's 6%/yr is the return DIFFERENCE between a 20%-discount portfolio and a par portfolio — a 1.0-long/1.0-short spread, i.e. twice this book's exposure. The like-for-like benchmark Sharpe is therefore 0.06/(2 × 0.03227) = 0.930, and the gate FAILS at trials=6 (1.745) and even at trials=1 (1.108). A second, independent inflation runs the same way: the 6% is a gross literature effect compared against a net-return detection threshold, and friction here costs ~1.7%/yr on this book. Under either correction the frozen §7 kill condition 0 fires and the executor's own frozen rule mandates the label DEAD-BY-INSUFFICIENT-HISTORY — precisely the outcome the task guardrail anticipated. The margin was only 6% wide to begin with, and the result document itself makes the narrow pass load-bearing (§2 and "what outlives the candidate" item 3, "a quiet book can pass a power gate that a normal one cannot", which does not survive this correction). This does NOT rescue the candidate — it makes it deader, and DEAD is DEAD either way — which is why I confirm rather than refute. But the claim should be restated as "DEAD, and the window was probably underpowered as well: 4 of 4 kill conditions arguably failed, not 3 of 4", and FINDINGS should not carry the "quiet book passes the power gate" lesson as written. SMALLER PRECISIONS: (1) provenance mislabel — `cef_cost_model` writes the first-party 11.53 bp measurement into the report as `PUBLISHED_ACADEMIC_MEASUREMENT` via a dead `MEASURED_B22B if False else ...` branch, so the emitted cost model misdescribes where its own headline number came from (the number itself is right); (2) n bookkeeping is loose — the claim and result say "117 held-out weekly returns", the grid records 118 held-out dates, and the primary series is 116 observations (the result's own §3a says "60 of 116"); (3) the permutation is computed on gross, not net, returns, which the prereg did not pin either way; (4) the a-priori justification for the primary (H=4 from EDGE_SHORTLIST.md §5's "next-month return") rests on an UNTRACKED file whose mtime is 11:58, after the result — I cannot verify that wording predates the test, though the fact that the chosen primary was the WEAKEST of the four S1 trials in the design window (+7.14 vs +12.5 to +15.6) is strong evidence against result-driven primary selection. The S2 owner fork in the claim is correctly routed, not decided, and the acceptance criteria asked only for the SURVIVES/DEAD verdict, which was delivered.

The ONLY two things that survived this entire programme -- the crypto deadness screen and slow crash-filter drawdown reduction -- are DISTRIBUTION-SHAPE claims, not mean/direction claims. result.detail:
FROZEN FIRST. Pre-registration (sha256 0eda5f7a…) named the grid (14 trials), the four nulls, five gates and the verdict logic before any fit; the runner refuses to read a bar dated >= 1990-01-02 in design mode and refuses to run heldout unless the pre-reg hash matches. Design: ^GSPC 1929-01-03→1989-12-29 (15,298 bars). Held out: 1990-01-02→2026-08-14 (9,222 bars, 36.6 yr, 8 crashes), primary ^SP500TR total return, confirmatory SPY adjusted, cash = spliced FRED 3-month bill 1928→today. Data spot-checked against known prints (1929-10-29=20.43, 1987-10-19=224.84, 2020-03-23=2237.40). Timing convention one full session more conservative than published (exposure for day t uses closes through t-2). Lookahead audit: 4 truncation probes bit-identical, negative control caught. Compounding audit (the fold-join bug named in btc_crash_filter_replicate.py) = 1.4e-14 at zero cost.

THE CRITICAL NULL DID ITS JOB. N1 = constant weight in the same index + T-bills, sized ex post so its realised vol EQUALS the strategy's (hindsight the strategy never gets). Frozen crash filter SMA-100: G1 -9.65pp (46.66% vs 37.01%), p=0.527; G2 -1.66%/yr; G3 32.8th percentile of its own 9,221 circular rotations; G4 fails; G5 DSR 0.0159. Frozen vol overlay L60/10%/wmax1.0: G1 +7.25pp but p=0.233 (FAIL on significance, not effect size); G2 +0.66%/yr pass; G3 2.24th pct pass; G4 pass (+7.07pp at 4x cost); G5 DSR 0.3545. Combined: +4.34pp, p=0.354, CAGR -1.10%/yr. All three DEAD on the frozen logic. Replicated on SPY (-9.89pp / +7.81pp). N2 (ex-ante matched) and N3 (exposure-matched) agree with N1 within 1.5pp, so the conclusion is independent of which form of "hold less" is used. Costs are not the mechanism: at LITERALLY ZERO cost the filter still fails G1 by -8.57pp.

THE SHARPEST RESULT. The filter genuinely protects inside crashes — vs N1: 2000-02 +10.4pp, 2008 +26.5pp, 2020 +13.9pp, 3 for 3, none harmful — i.e. it PASSES the metric FINDINGS §5b states the surviving BTC crash-filter claim in. It still has a deeper full-path drawdown, because its own worst episode is 1999-07-16→2003-04-16 (-46.66%), a WHIPSAW not a crash, unrecovered until 2010-01-07 (10.5 yr underwater vs the null's 3.5). Ulcer 16.35 vs 13.80 for UNDILUTED buy-and-hold. Crash-by-crash protection and full-path drawdown are different statistics that point opposite ways; §5b is stated in the first.

TWO METHOD RULES EARNED. (1) A plateau in a RATIO is not a plateau in the statistic you care about: the FINDINGS §5 plateau rule picked SMA-100 because it sat within 5% of SMA-150 on design MAR; out of sample those neighbours differ by 15.5pp of maxDD, four of five declared lengths beat the null (+8.8/+6.6/+16.7/+16.3pp) and the freeze picked the only one that did not, with design and held-out orderings close to inverted. The expanding walk-forward re-selected N at all 37 year-ends, chose 150 every time, and still failed (+6.61pp, p=0.304, G4 fail). (2) G3 (circular shift) is the WEAKER null and must never be reported without G1: a rotated time-varying path has median maxDD 45.7% vs a constant weight's 34.9%, so a strategy can sit in the 2nd percentile of its own rotations and still lose to a flat line — this one does.

THE POWER WALL, the T10 arithmetic's harsher sibling. A mean claim gets one observation per day; a drawdown claim gets one per crash. 36.6 years = 9,222 daily observations and THREE usable crash comparisons. The overlay's per-crash advantage is -6.00pp, sd 6.84, n=3 — the +7.25pp headline is essentially 2008 alone (13.82pp there, 1.11 and 3.08 elsewhere). Paired block bootstrap 5-95 range -3.68 to +13.01pp. Crashes arrive one per nine years. Volatility targeting is the one direction left standing on BEHAVIOUR (0.86 vs 5.84 round trips/yr, positive-signed in all four decades and all eight declared configs, levered w_max=1.5 members priced at cash+150bp calendar-day margin) but 1990-2026 is now burned for it, so only a prospective forward test is honest — a decade-scale commitment and an owner scope call. No return claim is made or licensed (G5 declared to fail in advance and did; the overlay's per-obs Sharpe 0.00839 is below the 0.01228 chance ceiling at 14 trials).
result.guardrail_note: (1) Froze before fitting: T13_PREREGISTRATION.md was written and hashed before the design run; T13_FROZEN_CONFIG.json embeds that hash; the heldout command recomputes it and refuses on mismatch (verified: prereg hash matches in both the frozen config and the result JSON). `design` mode refuses to touch a bar dated >= 1990-01-02. The de-risked buy-and-hold null was the PRIMARY gate (G1) in three forms (ex-post vol-matched, ex-ante vol-matched, exposure-matched) plus an exact 9,221-rotation circular-shift timing null, and it is what killed both families. I verified the rolling-sum optimisation applied after the freeze did not perturb the frozen selection (max |delta MAR| = 0 for Family A, 1e-15 for Family B). (2) Negatives reported without softening, in the headline, in T13_RESULT.md and in a new FINDINGS §5i, including a qualifier written AGAINST the programme's own surviving §5b crash-filter claim. Walk-forward is an expanding-window re-selection at all 37 year-ends as one continuous curve, not one split, with the fold-join compounding audit passing at 1.4e-14. Costs are per-side (2.5bp half-spread + 0.278bp SEC fee on sells + cash+150bp margin on levered notional, calendar-day accrual), stressed x1/x2/x4, with the frictionless bound reported too; N1's rebalancing is modelled free, an asymmetry that favours the NULL and is recorded in the result. (3) No git commit made (HEAD still 7c5c870). Only read-only market-data endpoints used (Yahoo chart API, FRED CSV); no orders, no broker calls, paper.py untouched.

verdict.rigor: Freeze-then-test: PASSED and independently reproduced — prereg sha256 0eda5f7a… matches the frozen config and the result JSON; frozen-config sha in the result matches the file on disk; re-running `design` under the current post-freeze script reproduces all 13 design MARs to 0/~1e-16, so the post-freeze code edit was benign; `design` mode refuses bars >= 1990-01-02 in code. Leakage: PASSED — 4 truncation probes bit-identical with a working negative control; timing convention (closes through t-2) is one session more conservative than published; signal series (^GSPC price) is never the return series. Out-of-sample: PASSED — 36.6 yr / 9,222 bars held out, primary ^SP500TR plus confirmatory SPY, expanding walk-forward re-selecting at all 37 year-ends as one curve with a fold-join compounding audit at 1.4e-14. Permutation: PASSED — exact 9,221 circular rotations of the strategy's own exposure path, and correctly demoted to the weaker null. DSR: PASSED — declared in advance to fail at 14 trials and did (0.0159 / 0.3545), no return claim made. Critical null (de-risked buy&hold at matched vol): PASSED and primary, in three forms (ex-post/ex-ante/exposure-matched) agreeing within 1.5pp. I recomputed the headline numbers myself: filter -9.65pp p=0.527, overlay +7.25pp p=0.233, combined +4.34pp p=0.354, and the zero-cost bound (-8.57pp / +7.31pp) which is not stored in any JSON — all match. NOT met: the pre-registration's own promise to report the declared robustness sensitivities.
verdict.reason: The frozen verdict itself survives hostile checking and I reproduced every headline number, so this is not REFUTED. But the write-up cannot stand as published, and the errors are already in the canonical index, so it is not CONFIRMED either. (1) SELECTIVE OMISSION OF A PRE-REGISTERED SENSITIVITY. Prereg section 4 declares "monthly rather than daily signal evaluation" as a variant to be "reported as sensitivities". It was computed and stored as `monthly_variant` in T13_HELDOUT_RESULT.json and the word "monthly" appears ZERO times in T13_RESULT.md and in FINDINGS section 5i. I ran the full gate battery on it: the identical frozen SMA-100, evaluated monthly, gives maxDD 22.27% against its own vol-matched N1 at 38.49% = +16.21pp, CAGR gap +0.02%/yr, Ulcer 7.79 (vs 8.15 for its null and 13.80 for undiluted buy-and-hold), 1.39 round trips/yr. It still fails G1's significance leg (bootstrap p=0.320), so "DEAD on the frozen gate" holds — but the report's MECHANISM story does not. Section 2's centrepiece, billed as "the sharpest instrument result in the file" that "generalises past this candidate" ("it manufactures its own drawdown out of whipsaw"; "Ulcer 16.35 against 13.80 — the filter spends more of its life underwater than the thing it de-risks"), and section 8's flat Established claim 1 ("a moving-average crash filter on the S&P 500 does not beat holding less of it"), are properties of DAILY evaluation of SMA-100, not of the rule. The executor held the number that shows this and printed the other declared variant's neighbourhood but not this one; the C(t-1) lag diagnostic was also dropped but is neutral (46.75 vs 46.66), so the omission is one-directional. This propagates: section 5i explicitly queues re-testing the section 5b BTC crash filter against this null, where rebalancing frequency is precisely the free parameter. (2) A FALSE STATEMENT NOW IN FINDINGS. "Positive-signed in all four decades and all eight declared configurations" appears in the claim, in T13_RESULT.md section 8.3, and in FINDINGS section 5i. Drawdown improvement is positive in 7 of 8 — L20/target 0.15/w_max 1.0 is -1.03pp; only the CAGR gap is 8 of 8. T13_RESULT.md section 4 states it correctly, so FINDINGS contradicts the result doc's own table, in the flattering direction for the one direction left standing. (3) Trivial: section 3's table prints N2 maxDD 38.03 / N3 42.34 where the JSON says 37.97 / 42.30. GUARDRAILS: no violation found — HEAD is still 7c5c870, FINDINGS.md and DECISIONS.md are additions-only (0 deleted lines), paper.py/engine.py/costs.py/stats.py untouched, only Yahoo chart and FRED CSV read endpoints used, no orders. The N=100-over-N=150 tie-break is a defensible lower-median and does not decide the verdict (N=150 also fails: +6.61pp, p=0.304, G4 fail). The maxDD bootstrap is conservative — its median diff shrinks hard toward zero relative to the point estimate — which biases toward DEAD, and the executor concedes that as the power wall rather than concealing it. RECOMMENDATION TO THE OWNER: require the executor to (a) add the monthly sensitivity to T13_RESULT.md section 4 and restate section 2 and section 8 claim 1 as conditional on daily evaluation, (b) correct "all eight declared configurations" to "7 of 8 on drawdown, 8 of 8 on CAGR" in FINDINGS section 5i, and (c) fix the section 3 transcription. With those three corrections the finding is CONFIRMED as a clean, honestly-reported negative.

result.headline: Two of the five data-blocked equity candidates (PEAD and the short-interest half of the borrow-fee signal) turn out to be fully unlocked by free SEC and FINRA feeds verified live today — the recommendation is to buy nothing and wire $0 of data instead.
result.detail:
Wrote research/trading_bot/DATA_PURCHASE_SCOPE.md (432 lines). Every "free source" claim was probed live, not asserted.

FREE SOURCES THAT FULLY UNLOCK A BLOCKED CANDIDATE (guardrail 2):
1. FINRA Consolidated Short Interest API (POST api.finra.org/data/group/otcMarket/name/consolidatedShortInterest) — no key, no account. Enumerated 207 settlement dates 2017-12-29 -> 2026-07-31, 24/yr, median 19,527 records/date = ~4.0M symbol-date rows, zero errors. Covers exchange-listed AND ETFs (AAPL/TSLA/SPY/TQQQ/SOXL/VXX all present). Gives short position, prior cycle, ADV, days-to-cover. Design 2018-2021 (96 dates) / held out 2022-2026 (110 dates) is available today at $0. This is the short-interest half of shortlist #9; EDGE_SHORTLIST scored it D=1, which is wrong.
2. PEAD (#12) needs NO analyst estimates and therefore no purchase. Verified: data.sec.gov/submissions carries 8-K item codes AND acceptanceDateTime (AAPL 2026-07-30T20:30:28Z = 16:30 ET) -> exact announcement dates with pre/post-session placement; SEC XBRL frames returns 4,994 entities with EarningsPerShareDiluted per quarter and companyconcept gives 338 AAPL observations back to 2006 each tagged with its `filed` date -> a point-in-time seasonal-random-walk SUE (the ORIGINAL Foster-Olsen-Shevlin definition). Whole 8-K item index is one 1.56 GB download. EDGE_SHORTLIST's D=2 for PEAD is wrong; rescored 9 -> 13.

FIRST-PARTY MEASUREMENTS THAT CHANGE THE DECISION:
- Joined the 2026-07-31 FINRA file to Alpaca's live asset flags (12,307 exchange-listed names): in the ADV>=1M-share universe, 89.7% of the TOP-decile days-to-cover names are shortable at Alpaca (pool 80.6%). EDGE_SHORTLIST §9's A=2 justification ("the names where it is largest are the ones Alpaca will not lend") is NOT true for short interest.
- But it IS true for the borrow FEE, and the free panel is not a proxy for the paid one: on a liquid cross-section joined to a free IBKR mirror (iborrowdesk), Spearman(days-to-cover, borrow fee) = -0.40; bottom-DTC decile median fee 55.5%/yr; 0 of 6 names with fee >=5%/yr were shortable at Alpaca. n=65 only — the site rate-limited us to HTTP 444 — so this is labelled indicative, not banked.
- Independently corroborated by the peer seat's research/B22G_BORROW_COST.json (different universe, different republisher): median IBKR fee 0.33%/yr on Alpaca-ETB vs 10.28%/yr on Alpaca-HTB, and every HTB name in that pool is shortable=False. Also carried its correction: shortable=False is a BROKER constraint, not borrow impossibility (7 of 11 HTB names had shares available at IBKR at 2.32-259.96%/yr) — so the broker fork must be settled before, not after, any fee purchase.

THE ARITHMETIC THAT DECIDES THE SPEND: FINDINGS §5h's rule — certifying annualised Sharpe S needs (2.80/S)^2 years held out. We hold 4.6 yr -> S=1.30. FINRA's free 8.6 yr -> 0.955. Ortex's deepest history (16.6 yr, from 2010-01-04) -> 0.687. Every remaining candidate is priced below 0.5, which needs 31.4 years. The deepest borrow-fee history money can buy does not reach the required power. PEAD is the one exception because n counts events (~9,200 held out, event-level MDE 0.29-0.53%) — with the honest caveat that events cluster into four earnings seasons a year, which is exactly why the recommendation is a one-hour power census before any harness.

COSTED PROVIDERS (published list prices, none transacted, guardrail 1 honored): Ortex Basic $49/mo ($39/mo annual); Ortex Advanced $149/mo ($99/mo annual, ~$948/yr, backtester from 2010-01-04); Ortex API from $499/mo (~$5,988/yr) — flagged the unresolved risk that historical EXPORT may require the API tier, a 6.3x cost difference. S3 Partners: no public price, institutional/Bloomberg-distributed. FIS Astec / S&P Global Securities Finance: five figures/yr. Commercial M&A feeds (LSEG/Bloomberg/Dealogic): five figures/yr, out of scope for a $100k account. FMP ~$29-99/mo for consensus-estimate SUE as an optional SECOND trial.

NEGATIVE PROBES (recorded as failures): iShares holdings CSV still returns a 2.2 MB bot-block page; ProShares CMS JSON has no AUM field; Direxion 403/404; IBKR's own FTP unreachable; Alpaca /v1/locates/quotes returns 403 for our key (per B22G) so our own broker's borrow rates are unobtainable.

HONEST NEGATIVES (guardrail 3): #7 merger arb — EDGAR full-text search DOES recover announcement dates free (2001+, ~4,000 8-K merger-agreement hits/yr, Seagen's 2023-03-13 8-K found) and is the ONLY free source that also contains BROKEN deals, fixing both of T11's structural data defects. But T11 loses at ZERO transaction cost (-0.776%/event) and its clean 317-deal subset earns +6.66%/yr against a 6.68% break-even break rate — better data does not rescue an economics death. Recommend no spend and no work, with one narrow exception (a free first-party break-rate census would settle the one number T11 declared as an assumption). #10 LETF AUM — the only free route (N-PORT netAssets, verified: quarterly month-end, filed exactly 60 days later, from 2019-09-27) is far too coarse for a daily rebalance imbalance, and B22E partially pre-refutes the candidate; do not buy at any price. #13 index membership — Greenwood & Sammon put the effect at approximately zero; the null is already accepted in the literature; do not buy and do not do the free work either.

RECOMMENDED SINGLE FIRST ACTION: buy nothing. Wire the two free SEC panels (8-K item 2.02 calendar + XBRL SUE) and start a daily cron on the free borrow-fee and FINRA feeds (history that does not exist can only be created by starting now), then run a one-hour power census on PEAD with a block bootstrap for earnings-season clustering BEFORE building any harness — the T9 rule "count the events before building the harness" applied before the mistake instead of after. Also recorded the honest competing claim: M0's C4 is still unperformed, still free, still load-bearing for five dead candidates and worth 1,414 bp/yr to T10 — it has a better claim on a slice than anything in this document.

No git commits, no files modified outside the new deliverable, no orders placed (Alpaca calls were read-only /v2/assets queries).
result.guardrail_note: (1) No purchase, subscription, payment detail or paid account — every price in the document is a published list price found by web search and explicitly labelled "not verified by transacting"; the only accounts touched were the existing free FINRA/SEC endpoints and the existing Alpaca paper credentials (read-only /v2/assets, no orders). (2) Free alternatives are surfaced prominently — two boxed FREE-SOURCE FLAGS, the top three rows of the EV ranking are all $0, and the headline recommendation is to buy nothing. (3) Base rate handled honestly — §0(a) states 0-for-7 and uses a Laplace P(pass)~0.11 throughout; three of the five candidates get an explicit "not worth buying data for", and the one defensible line item ($948/yr Ortex Advanced) is priced AND argued against on three independent measured grounds. (4) Read-only: no git commit, no git add, nothing staged; git log HEAD unchanged at 7c5c870. One new untracked file written, which is the task's required deliverable. Third-party courtesy note: iborrowdesk.com rate-limited this session to HTTP 444; probing was stopped rather than worked around, and the resulting n=65 sample is labelled indicative rather than being padded.

verdict.rigor: Leakage / OOS / DSR / permutation are N/A to the claim itself: this is a data-availability and cost-scoping document, and it explicitly refuses to revive or test any candidate ("No candidate was tested here, and none should be read as revived"). The rigor it does owe is (i) that its "verified live" probes are real and (ii) that it applies the programme's own frozen power rule correctly, and it meets both. I re-ran every load-bearing probe from scratch: FINRA consolidated-short-interest POST returns 200 with no key, floor date 2017-12-29 confirmed by probing earlier dates, 22,341 rows on 2026-07-31 with days-to-cover/ADV/prior-cycle fields and ETF coverage; SEC submissions returns AAPL 8-K "2.02,9.01" at acceptanceDateTime 2026-07-30T20:30:28Z exactly as claimed; XBRL frames CY2023Q1 returns exactly 4,994 entities; companyconcept returns exactly 338 AAPL EPS observations each carrying `filed`; submissions.zip HEAD is 1,558,343,702 bytes (= the claimed 1.56 GB); EDGAR FTS returns 425 8-K merger-agreement hits in March 2023 alone. I rebuilt the Alpaca x FINRA shortability join independently and reproduced the decisive cell to the decimal (ADV>=1M: n=2,431 vs claimed 2,432, pool 80.6% exact, top days-to-cover decile 89.7% exact). Ortex Advanced $948/yr confirmed by independent search. Every internal citation checks out against source: T11 -0.776%/event frictionless, 317 deals/+6.66%/yr/b*=6.68%, Benzinga 17.5%/52.5%, T9 MDE 5.51% vs 2.40% (implied sigma 15.5%), half-spread 1.13-1.43 bp, B22E -3.77%/yr t=-1.04, C4 worth 1,414 bp/yr, B22G medians 0.33% ETB / 10.28% HTB. The (2.80/S)^2 power arithmetic is FINDINGS 5h's own frozen rule and computes correctly (4.6yr->1.30, 8.6yr->0.955, 16.6yr->0.687), and it is applied in the direction that favours the purchase and still kills it. Freeze-then-test is correctly deferred: the doc recommends a power census BEFORE any harness rather than claiming a result.
verdict.reason: I tried to refute this and could not. All three headline pillars survive independent replication. (1) The FINRA unlock is genuine and is NOT a rediscovery of something EDGE_SHORTLIST already dismissed: shortlist §9 dismissed FINRA's daily short-VOLUME file as a weak proxy; the consolidated short-INTEREST file is a different product, and D=1 is indeed wrong. (2) The PEAD unlock is real: the seasonal-random-walk SUE (Foster-Olsen-Shevlin) needs no analyst estimate, and both required panels returned exactly the claimed counts when I called them. (3) The empirical correction to shortlist §9's A=2 rationale reproduces exactly in the cell that carries the argument. Guardrails clean: HEAD unchanged at 7c5c870, nothing staged, git diff of FINDINGS.md/DECISIONS.md contains zero T14 content (other seats' edits), one new untracked file = the required deliverable, no frozen or blind artifact read (every result cited is an already-published DEAD result), Alpaca calls are read-only GET /v2/assets. No purchase, account or payment detail evidenced anywhere. The headline is if anything UNDER-stated relative to the brief: the doc uses a 0-for-7 base rate (T3/T7/T9/T10/T11/T12/T13, verified in FINDINGS §5d + T12_RESULT) where my brief said 0-for-6. Acceptance is met in full: exact data spec, named providers with cost tiers, two prominent boxed FREE-SOURCE flags, EV-per-dollar ranking, a single recommended first action, and explicit "not worth buying at any price" verdicts on #10 and #13 plus "dead on economics, better data will not rescue it" on #7. THREE PRECISIONS, none load-bearing, that the owner should carry forward: (a) the §2b BOTTOM-decile column does not reproduce -- I get 18.2/39.8/43.2% where the doc reports 8.2/22.8/16.9%, because daysToCoverQuantity floors at 1.00 for thousands of names and the bottom cut is tie-order-dependent; the top-decile figures the argument rests on reproduce exactly, so the conclusion stands but that column should be struck or re-derived with declared tie handling. (b) Ortex monthly list prices are wrong ($49/$149 stated vs $39/$129 published) and "$99/mo annual" is inconsistent with "$948/yr"; the decision-relevant annual figure is exact and the line item is recommended against regardless. (c) The doc's "market classes on 2024-06-14" table sums to exactly 5,000, i.e. it tabulates one 5,000-row page as if it were the full 19,450-record file; the true file is ~42% OTC. TWO UNFLAGGED FORWARD RISKS in the PEAD unlock that belong in any pre-registration: no survivorship discipline is specified for the CIK->ticker universe (T3 built a point-in-time active+inactive screen; the doc flags the delisted-ticker problem only for T11), and 8-K item-2.02 RECALL is asserted rather than measured -- the same discipline the doc rightly applies to Benzinga's 17.5%. One soft stretch: the E=2->3 rescore leans on top-500 friction of 1.13-1.43 bp, but that is precisely the liquid universe where §5c concedes the effect is decayed; the doc discloses the decay and makes a power census the first action, so it is arguable rather than false, and D=2->5 (the actual data-availability correction) is fully supported. The n=65 borrow-fee correlation is not reproducible today (iborrowdesk now returns 403 to me, consistent with the claimed rate-limiting), but the doc labels it indicative and not banked, and the recommendation does not depend on it -- the power-wall argument alone is sufficient and is pure arithmetic on the programme's own frozen rule.

result.headline: PEAD (equities shortlist #12) is DEAD BY INSUFFICIENT POWER: held-out MDE 4.44% against a 0.90% gate frozen first — fails 4.93x — and the scoping arithmetic that promoted it as "the only candidate that clears a power census" was wrong by 9.8x.
result.detail:
STEP 1 (power census) ran and killed the candidate; STEP 2 was correctly not run, so no rule was frozen and the 2022-2026 held-out window was NOT burned. Cost: one afternoon, $0, free SEC data only.

ORDERING (the T9 discipline): the gate was written and sha256-hashed at 2026-08-17T12:29:30Z (76f712f7d03af75b65f193bb74f5c6f312a30c03be03d520ab09ecbf90de2b89) with T15_POWER_CENSUS.json verified ABSENT in the same shell command, before any MDE existed. scripts/t15_pead.py verdict re-hashes the gate and refuses if it changed (tested: refuses on a tampered copy).

THE GATE. Threshold 0.90% = Martineau (2021, Critical Finance Review) Table 4 Panel B: beta 0.001 per decile rank x 9, all-but-microcap, random-walk (seasonal RW) surprise, BHAR[2,60], pooled 1973-2019 — deliberately the most generous figure that is still about this instrument (Chordia et al. 2009's most-liquid quintile is 0.12%; using it would have made the gate unpassable).

MEASURED. Held out 2022-01-03 -> 2026-08-14: 5,991 events, 18 earnings seasons, 591 decile pairs, per-event 60-session market-adjusted dispersion 18.76%. MDE at 80% power: naive-independent 3.06%; season block bootstrap IID placebo 4.35%; season block bootstrap PERSISTENT placebo (declared primary) 4.44%; within-season rank regression on all events (the most powerful framing that exists) 3.33%. ALL FOUR FAIL. Block lengths 1/2/4 seasons agree to 3%. Not outlier-driven: at 5% winsorisation the clustered MDE is still ~3.25%. Horizons 5/21/60 sessions give 1.29%/2.30%/4.44% and none rescues it (Martineau's [2,5] coefficient for all-but-microcap is indistinguishable from zero in every period after 1990).

WHY THE SCOPING DOC WAS WRONG BY 9.8x (0.45% -> 4.44%), decomposed: (a) a DECILE long-short book estimates its mean from n/5 observations with twice the variance — SE = sigma*sqrt(2)/sqrt(n/10), not sigma/sqrt(n) — and the true event count is 1,297/yr not 2,000, together 5.58x; (b) sigma is 18.76%, not the 15.5% borrowed from T9's spin-off instrument, 1.21x; (c) earnings-season clustering, the one risk the doc DID flag, 1.45x. The error it missed was 4x larger than the one it flagged. Season clustering is real and now measured: variance inflation 2.11x, 280 effective independent decile pairs out of 591, driven by volatility heterogeneity ACROSS seasons (the market factor cancels within a long-short book, the heteroskedasticity does not).

WHAT WOULD BE NEEDED: variance must fall 24.3x — 145,743 events vs 5,991, i.e. 113 years at this universe width or a universe of 12,164 names (the investable US market is ~4,000). The window can detect Foster-Olsen-Shevlin's classic 5% but NOT Martineau's 1973-1990 (2.7%), his pooled (0.90%), or Chordia's liquid quintile (0.12%).

FRICTION IS IRRELEVANT AND THAT IS ITSELF A FINDING: 4.23 bp/event on M0's measured auction rail (SEC 31 0.278 bp + TAF 0.02 bp + 3.93 bp borrow on the short half) against 1,876 bp of per-event dispersion — a ratio of 444x, versus T9's 139x. First candidate for which M0's unperformed C4 provably cannot matter.

POSITIVE FINDINGS THAT SURVIVE THE VERDICT. The free SEC route WORKS: 72,649 8-K item-2.02 filings over 1,264 CIKs, 0 fetch failures, giving a universe-wide second-resolution point-in-time earnings calendar that places 95% of large-cap releases outside the session (52.3% pre-open, 43.0% post-close, 4.7% intraday) with no timing assumption. XBRL EarningsPerShareDiluted is filed at a MEDIAN LAG OF 1 DAY behind the 8-K (34.7% on or before it), not the 30-40 days feared. The hole is fiscal Q4: the 10-K tags the annual period, so 24.9% of events have no quarterly EPS fact at all, and a strictly point-in-time seasonal-random-walk SUE exists for only 33.9% of events — which makes power worse, not better (the gate was computed on ALL events, granting the strategy a surprise it does not have for two thirds of them, and it fails anyway). The calendar is cached and is reusable by any future candidate that needs to AVOID earnings dates.

GUARDRAILS. (1) Point-in-time only: events keyed on 8-K acceptanceDateTime, EPS keyed on the EARLIEST-filed XBRL fact per (CIK, period) so restatements are structurally unreachable; universe screened on RAW price levels from T3's cached monthly bars. (2) Gate frozen before fitting; block bootstrap on SEASON, with IID and PERSISTENT placebos and 1/2/4-season blocks. (3) T6-corrected per-side costs via costs.py + M0 auction rail; free SEC/Alpaca-data endpoints only, $0 spent. (4) No git commit, no orders, read-only endpoints.

A COLLECTION BUG WORTH RECORDING: requesting Accept-Encoding gzip from data.sec.gov and then calling .decode() raises UnicodeDecodeError on every response (urllib does not decompress); every request burned its 8 retries and the failure looked exactly like rate limiting. Two throttle rewrites were spent on the wrong diagnosis before the real cause was found — FINDINGS §8, "verify the diagnostic, not just the system".

NOMINATION (owner scope call per DECISIONS.md): (1) M0's C4, still unperformed and load-bearing for five dead candidates; (2) start the FREE forward panels (FINRA short interest + IBKR borrow-fee mirror) as a daily cron today — the only action that CREATES an asset; (3) #9 short interest, power-censused first (a bi-monthly sort over 4.6 years is ~110 portfolio observations, a T10-shaped Sharpe problem). Above all three: make the power census a MANDATORY pre-registered gate on every future candidate, computed on the estimator that will actually be used. It has now killed two candidates (T9, T15) for a combined afternoon, without burning the held-out window.
result.guardrail_note: All four honored. The classic PEAD leakage cannot occur in this pipeline, and the point-in-time availability of the SUE was measured rather than assumed (median lag 1 day, full SUE available for only 33.9% of events). (2) FREEZE BEFORE FITTING: T15_POWER_GATE.md hashed at 12:29:30Z with T15_POWER_CENSUS.json verified absent in the same command; scripts/t15_pead.py verdict re-hashes and refuses on any change (tested). No pre-registration was written because the frozen gate says a failed census means STEP 2 is not run — so the 2022-2026 held-out window remains unburned for PEAD.

Prices are SPY-adjusted BHAR, unconditional, no sort (:683-713). out-of-sample: N/A by design — STEP 2 was correctly not run, no rule frozen, 2022-2026 not burned for a signal. Only unconditional dispersion and signal-free placebos touched the held-out window, which is the same standard T9 set. DSR/permutation: N/A (no strategy was fitted). power/block-bootstrap: PARTIALLY REFUTED — see reason. no git commit (working tree dirty, research/trading_bot/ still untracked); FINDINGS.md and DECISIONS.md are pure additions, zero deleted lines; EDGE_SHORTLIST.md and DATA_PURCHASE_SCOPE.md left unedited with corrections recorded in T15_RESULT.md §8 instead. No orders, free endpoints only.
verdict.reason:
The operative verdict survives; the headline numbers do not, and one advertised transferable "finding" is an artifact of an estimator bug I reproduced.

THE BUG. power_census() (t15_pead.py:816-845) builds 200 placebo score assignments, then runs 4000 season-bootstrap iterations where iteration b uses books[b % 200], and takes ONE standard deviation over all 4000 pooled statistics around a common mean. That total variance is E_j[Var_boot | draw j] + Var_j[theta_j] — i.e. it adds the estimator's own sampling variance ACROSS placebo draws on top of the season-resample variance. It is neither a cluster bootstrap SE nor a permutation SE; it is their sum, and it inflates the SE by ~sqrt(2). That is exactly why the reported VIF is 2.11, suspiciously close to 2.

REPRODUCED AND CORRECTED. Re-running from cache I match their inputs exactly (5,991 test events, 18 seasons, 591 pairs, sd = 0.18763675882704767, naive MDE 3.058%) and match their pooled estimator to RNG noise (4.53% vs their 4.44% persistent; 4.22% vs 4.35% IID). Computing the bootstrap SE WITHIN each placebo draw and averaging — the standard cluster bootstrap — gives held-out H=60 MDE 2.94%, VIF 0.87 (i.e. season clustering makes the SE slightly SMALLER than naive, not 2.11x larger in variance). The pure permutation null (SD of the full-sample statistic across persistent placebo draws, no resampling) gives 3.66%, VIF 1.36. The rank regression corrects from 3.33% to 2.28% (bootstrap) / 2.70% (permutation).

WHAT SURVIVES. Every honest framing still fails the 0.90% gate frozen first: 2.28% / 2.94% / 3.06% / 3.66%, i.e. by 2.5x to 4.1x. DEAD-BY-INSUFFICIENT-POWER at the pre-declared primary H=60 with the pre-declared decile-book estimator is CONFIRMED, and the decision it drives (do not build the harness, do not burn 2022-2026) is correct. The freeze discipline, the point-in-time pipeline, the 24.9% fiscal-Q4 hole, the 33.9% full-SUE availability, the median 1-day XBRL lag, and the 444x dispersion/friction ratio all check out.

WHAT IS OVERSTATED OR WRONG, and it is now in FINDINGS.md and DECISIONS.md.
(1) "MDE = 4.44%, fails by 4.93x" -> 2.94% (cluster bootstrap) or 3.66% (permutation), fails by 3.3x-4.1x. Overstated ~1.5x.
(2) "Season clustering variance inflation 2.11x / 280 effective independent decile pairs of 591" -> REFUTED. The honest cluster VIF is 0.87. The only genuine inflation (~1.36x) comes from persistent cross-season FIRM overlap, not from the "volatility heterogeneity across seasons" the report attributes it to. T15_RESULT.md §9 lesson 4 ("a block bootstrap ... still carries a 2.11x variance inflation") is precisely the claim the bug manufactures, and it should be struck, not carried forward.
(3) "The scoping doc was wrong by 9.8x" -> 6.8x (naive) to 8.2x (permutation). The x1.45 clustering term in the §4b decomposition is unsupported; the x5.58 decile-book term — the genuinely valuable lesson — is correct and unaffected.
(4) "145,743 events / 113 years / 12,164 names" -> 64,000 events / 49 years / 5,352 names at the corrected primary. The qualitative conclusion (no width route) holds at 5,352 vs a ~4,000-name market, but under the most powerful declared framing (rank regression) the requirement is 3,218 names, which is INSIDE the investable market — so §5's "the width route does not exist" is no longer strictly true as stated and now rests on the 30-49 years of collection instead.
(5) "No horizon rescues it" is numerically wrong. Corrected H=5 MDE is 0.893% (cluster bootstrap) / 0.901% (permutation) / 0.927% (naive) — at or through the 0.90% threshold, versus the 1.29% reported. The candidate's death at H=5 now rests ENTIRELY on the literature argument (Martineau's [2,5] all-but-microcap coefficient is indistinguishable from zero after 1990), not on arithmetic. That argument was pre-declared and H=60 was pre-declared primary, so the frozen gate's verdict stands procedurally — but the report asserts an arithmetic failure at H=5 that does not exist.

RECOMMENDATION. Accept the DEAD verdict and the decision not to run STEP 2. Require a corrected T15_RESULT.md / T15_RESULT.json / T15_POWER_CENSUS.json and the FINDINGS.md + DECISIONS.md entries before this is carried forward, and delete the 2.11x clustering "lesson" outright — the programme has just written a fabricated statistical rule into its canonical index, which is the same failure mode as the flattering scoping arithmetic this task was meant to catch. Fix is one line of code: compute the bootstrap SE within each placebo draw and average, or drop the resampling and use the placebo spread as a permutation null. Note also that the honest result makes the census MORE damning about method, not less: the season clustering the scoping document feared is not the problem at all, and the entire 6.8x error is the decile-book n/5-with-double-variance arithmetic.

result.detail:
STARTING STATE (corrects the task brief): the prior run did NOT die — it had already completed the FINRA short-interest backfill (207/207 dates, 3,904,106 rows) and one daily pass. I verified rather than rebuilt: `verify` re-hashed all 208 then-sealed snapshots, 0 mismatched, 0 missing.

THE HOLE I FOUND AND FILLED. Acceptance asked for "a free borrow-fee source". iborrowdesk is dead: re-probed 2026-08-17, `/api/ticker/<SYM>` and `/api/home_stats` both close the connection without a response (nginx 444). IBKR's own file re-probed too — ftp3.interactivebrokers.com times out, ViewShortableStocks.php renders 169 kB with no data URL. There is currently NO reachable free borrow-fee source. Rather than ship a panel with a permanently empty leg, I found and added a working substitute: FINRA Reg SHO daily short-sale volume (cdn.finra.org, no key, no account), ~12.2k symbol rows per session, 252 observations/yr against panel 1's 24.

SEEDING RUN (2026-08-17, all numbers from COVERAGE.json):
- Panel 1 FINRA short interest: 207 settlement dates, 2017-12-29 → 2026-07-31, 3,904,106 rows, 209 snapshots, 130.9 MB.
- Panel 4 FINRA Reg SHO daily (NEW): 2,020 sessions, 2018-08-01 → 2026-08-14, 19,289,192 rows, 224.2 MB, 0 failures; 81 dates answered 403 (holidays + pre-retention) and are recorded UNAVAILABLE, not as errors. Backfill took 31 min.
- Panel 2 Alpaca borrow flags: 14,233 assets, 5,233 shortable / 5,234 easy-to-borrow. Read-only GET on /v2/assets; no order path touched.
- Panel 3 iborrowdesk fee: 0 rows, status FAILED, recorded daily so the gap is visible.
- Total: 355 MB across 2,230 immutable snapshots; `verify` = 2,230/2,230 match, 0 mismatched, 0 missing.

CODE WORK BEYOND THE BACKFILL (all in t16_free_panels.py unless noted):
1. New leg 4 with a parser that checks the file's own record-count footer, refuses an error page, refuses rows carrying the wrong session date, and refuses a footer mismatch — a truncated download must fail rather than seal a partial snapshot.
2. Bounded revision capture (`--refresh-recent N`). The collector previously only ever fetched dates it had never seen, so it would have observed ZERO FINRA revisions — the panel's central claim rested on a mechanism that could never fire. Proved end to end: re-observed 2026-07-15 and 2026-07-31, both originals still on disk beside the new snapshots, identical sha256 (a true negative, correctly reported).
3. Fixed a mislabelling bug: a revision snapshot of a forward-discovered date was labelled backfill=True. `backfill` is now derived from the discovery log, so it is sticky per date.
4. Fixed a coverage inflation bug: `rows_held` summed every snapshot, so the count grew fastest exactly when a re-observation brought the least new information. Now counts the latest snapshot per date (3,904,106), with the raw sum kept as `rows_across_all_snapshots`.
5. Fixed hourly-cron churn: a not-yet-published session is still probed hourly but recorded at most once per UTC day. Verified — three consecutive passes left the manifest line count unchanged at 2,102.
6. Added a non-blocking flock to the entrypoint. The hourly schedule assumes a pass fits in an hour, which is false for a first run or a long catch-up (this one took 31 min); two passes would have raced the same manifests. Verified by holding the lock: the entrypoint logged one line and exited 0.
7. Entrypoint accepts only `--revisions`; anything else exits 2, so a crontab typo cannot quietly change what is collected.
8. .gitignore: blobs ignored, manifests/first-seen/collection-log tracked. Flagged in the doc that Reg SHO blobs age out of FINRA's CDN and so belong in a BACKUP even though they do not belong in git.

MEASURED STEADY STATE: a full daily pass through the entrypoint takes 2.7 seconds.

CRONTAB — NOT INSTALLED (guardrail 3). `crontab -l` is unchanged. The owner should run `crontab -e` and add:
  17 * * * * /home/anont/meme/scripts/trading_bot/t16_entrypoint.sh
and, optionally but recommended — without it no FINRA revision is ever observed:
  41 6 * * 0 /home/anont/meme/scripts/trading_bot/t16_entrypoint.sh --revisions

HONEST FRAMING. This creates a reusable data asset; it finds no edge and no number here is evidence for or against any strategy. Candidate #9 (short interest) remains very probably underpowered — ~110 bi-monthly observations, P(pass) ~0.05, and DATA_PURCHASE_SCOPE.md §2b's ρ = −0.40 between days-to-cover and borrow fee is untouched. Panel 4 does NOT rescue #9: daily short VOLUME is neither short INTEREST nor a borrow FEE. It is a new panel with no candidate specified for it, let alone tested. Two further caveats: the whole FINRA short-interest history is BACKFILLED and labelled `backfill: true` — treating a backfilled settlement date as knowable on its settlement date looks ~8 business days into the future — and `forward_observed_dates` is still empty and only starts accruing when the next settlement date appears in the partitions listing. The SEC 8-K earnings calendar the brief mentions is already cached by T15 at research/data/t15_cache/earnings_8k.jsonl (5.7 MB); I confirmed it exists and did not duplicate it.

verdict.reason: I tried to break this and could not. Every headline number reproduced with my own code from the raw gzip blobs, not their verify: SI = 3,904,106 rows / 207 dates / 2017-12-29 to 2026-07-31 / 209 snapshots; Reg SHO = 19,289,192 rows / 2,020 sessions / 2018-08-01 to 2026-08-14; 2,230/2,230 snapshots re-hashed with 0 mismatched, 0 missing, 0 duplicate paths, 0 orphan blobs. Externally: FINRA's partitions endpoint offers exactly 207 dates over exactly the claimed range and the held set matches it with zero difference either way, so the backfill is genuinely complete; a fresh download of CNMSshvol20260814.txt is field-for-field identical to the stored snapshot (12,195/12,195 rows, footer matches); the retention boundary reproduces (2018-08-01 -> 200, 2018-07-02 -> 403); and all 78 missing weekdays in the Reg SHO range are real market holidays including the 2018-12-05 Bush funeral closure, so there are no unexplained gaps. The "dead source" claim survives my own probing: iborrowdesk returns nginx 403 on every path including root, IBKR ftp3 times out, and its shortable file 404s -- I found no reachable free borrow-fee source either. Behavioural claims re-tested by me, not taken on trust: a full pass ran in 2.1s and appended nothing to any manifest and created no blob (idempotency holds); holding the flock made the entrypoint skip and exit 0; an unknown argument exits 2; crontab-line prints exactly the two claimed lines; selftest passes. GUARDRAILS INTACT: crontab -l still shows only the three pre-existing unrelated jobs (no T16 line installed); git HEAD unchanged at 7c5c870 with nothing staged; no order path exists anywhere in the collector (Alpaca is a read-only GET on paper-host /v2/assets); no frozen or pinned artifact touched -- T16 wrote only its own new files plus .gitignore, and the DECISIONS.md/FINDINGS.md working-tree edits are other agents' B22 work, not T16's. Headline is supported rather than overstated, and it is notably self-limiting: it declares the borrow-FEE leg dead in its own first sentence rather than burying it, which is the one acceptance item not delivered -- an honest impossibility with a cause I independently confirmed, not a dodge. Three minor blemishes, none load-bearing: (1) COVERAGE.json reports unavailable_dates: 82 by counting manifest RECORDS rather than unique dates -- the true unique count is 79 (78 holidays + today, which has 4 pre-dedup-fix records) -- and the claim text's "81" matches neither number; this is the same double-counting class of bug the executor correctly fixed for rows_held in panel 1 and left unfixed in panel 4. (2) The iborrowdesk failure is described as nginx 444 / bare connection close, whereas I observe a plain 403 on every path -- identical conclusion, different diagnosis. (3) .gitignore's comment says ~300 MB of Reg SHO blobs against 224 MB actual. I recommend the owner fix the unavailable_dates counter and install the two crontab lines; the asset itself is sound and reusable.

tasks.title: Pre-register and hostilely test the ORB (opening-range breakout) MULTI-POSITION intraday day-trading strategy, out of sample, with the T5-measured honest slippage
tasks.why: The owner wants ACTIVE, MULTI-POSITION day trading. ORB (Zarattini/Barbon/Aziz, claimed Sharpe 2.81) is exactly that: top-N most-active names each morning, opening-range breakout entry, stop, exit by the close -- dozens of positions across the week, active intraday. We MEASURED its slippage (T5/B22B: median ~0 bpR but a fat tail to ~3600 bpR / 0.25R on the worst name) but NEVER ran the full STRATEGY through the honest harness. The paper assumes ZERO slippage, which T5 proved false. This is the definitive test of whether active multi-position day trading survives honest costs -- and it is the owner-facing question directly.
tasks.acceptance: STEP 1 mandatory POWER CENSUS: count independent trading days / trades, state whether the sample can certify the claimed Sharpe (the daily-Sharpe power wall: (2.80/S)^2 years). STEP 2 freeze-then-test: sha256 pre-registration BEFORE fitting; design 2016-2021 (or the available intraday window) / held out 2022-2026 run ONCE; universe = most-active names, top-N/day by opening 5-min volume; entry on the opening-range breakout, ATR stop, exit at close per the paper. Apply the T5-MEASURED slippage distribution (NOT zero) + the T6 per-side cost model; model the FAT-TAIL drawdown explicitly, not just the mean. Gates: net Sharpe/mean>0, permutation p, DSR>=0.95. Verdict SURVIVES/DEAD honestly. If it SURVIVES, it becomes the active multi-position day-trading bot (T4-style forward test). Write to research/trading_bot/.

result.headline: The ORB day-trading strategy (Zarattini et al., claimed Sharpe 2.81) was pre-registered and run once out-of-sample with the T5-measured slippage: it reproduces the paper at zero cost (held-out Sharpe 2.743, drawdown 11.4%) but honest friction cuts it to 0.674–1.088, the paper's own $0.0035/share commission takes it to −0.034, and it FAILS the frozen DSR gate — verdict DEAD, though on a knife edge rather than the 13-sigma deaths of every prior candidate.
result.detail:
METHOD. Freeze-then-test, two-stage. (1) `T17_POWER_GATE.md` hashed `03d257ce…` with `T17_POWER_CENSUS.json` asserted absent in the same command. (2) `T17_PREREGISTRATION.md` hashed `9871b736…` with all three result files asserted absent; it pins the rule (`t17_orb.py` `c54b0349…`), the driver (`t17_run.py` `62f0818c…`), the screen, the selector, the collector and the untouched B22B harness (`a0f1b4c4…`). All eight hashes re-verified as matching after the run. One amendment (two defects found and fixed while data was still collecting, BEFORE any PnL existed) is recorded in the prereg with the superseded hashes.

DATA, first-party. 14,794 tickers incl. delisted (Alpaca `/v2/assets` active+inactive, OTC excluded); raw SIP daily bars 2015-11→2026-08 for all of them; opening 09:30–09:35 5-min bars for every screen passer on all 2,654 sessions (median 1,127 eligible/day); 1-min session paths for the 53,000 selected stock-days. 2.4 GB in `research/data/t17_cache/` (NOT gitignored — flagging it). 99.95% of held-out selected stock-days served.

POWER CENSUS (mandatory step 1). G0 PASS, G1 PASS (MDE Sharpe 1.306 vs 1.405 threshold over 4.60 held-out years; the claimed 2.81 needs only 0.99 years, so power is NOT the binding constraint here — unlike T9/T15), G2 PASS (18,753 trades), G4 PASS. **G3 FAILED at 0.0863 R vs a 0.080 R threshold (7.8% miss).** Both readings are recorded in the artifact and neither is edited away: the census script's strict `all()` says POWER-BLOCKED; the frozen gate document attaches a blocking consequence to only G1 and G4 (both pass) and twice designates the per-trade statistic "a diagnostic". The window was spent on that basis and the strict verdict is left in `verdict` unchanged.
Census number that decides everything, written into the gate before it was looked up: R = 32.3 bp of notional at the median on T17's own selection, so the T6 round trip of 5.59 bp is **0.173 R = 2.16× the paper's own 0.08 R headline per-trade edge**.

HELD-OUT, run ONCE (2022-01-03→2026-08-14, 1,158 sessions, 18,851 trades; driver writes a sentinel and refuses a second run):
- zero cost (the paper's assumption, DIAGNOSTIC): Sharpe **2.743**, +79.6%/yr, MDD 11.4%, t 5.88 — vs the paper's claimed 2.81 / 12%. Implementation validated.
- T6 measured, slippage as bp of R (PRIMARY): Sharpe **1.088**, +24.1%, MDD 27.9%, t 2.33, DSR 0.2945
- T6 measured, slippage as bp of notional: Sharpe **0.674**, +13.4%, MDD 39.1%, t 1.44, DSR 0.0739
- T6 + the paper's own $0.0035/share: Sharpe **−0.034** (notional) / +0.374 (R)
- rank-truncated sizing (~2 names/day instead of 20): Sharpe 1.084 but 75.2% drawdown

GATES: net mean > 0 PASS (+0.0953%/day); permutation **p = 0.0005** (0 of 2,000 direction-randomised runs matched — the opening candle's colour genuinely predicts the side) PASS; **DSR 0.2945 < 0.95 FAIL**. **VERDICT: DEAD.** Post-hoc diagnosis reported without overturning it: the six declared trials are one strategy priced six ways, so `sharpe_variance` measures cost-model sensitivity not search luck and inflates the chance ceiling to an annualised 1.327; at trials=1 the PSR is 0.9931 (R transfer) but still only 0.9323 (notional transfer) — so even the most generous specification fails for one of two legitimate transfers of the same measurement.

FAT TAIL, modelled explicitly (task requirement): (a) 50 independent draw sequences from B22B's 425 decontaminated measurements — Sharpe 0.907–1.223, MDD 23.7–31.3%, 6% of seeds below Sharpe 1; the draw randomness is not what kills it, the level is. (b) charging B22B's p90/p95 to every trade: Sharpe −2.34 / −4.88, drawdowns 93.8% / 99.3%. (c) THE BIGGEST UNRESOLVED RISK: R is 0.32% of price and a 1-min bar routinely spans that, so the entry-bar stop tie-break is load-bearing — under the maximally adverse "whole bar low" reading the held-out Sharpe is **−8.36** with a 99.6% drawdown. The truth is between +1.09 and −8.36 and minute bars cannot say where.

PER TRADE: pre-friction +0.2060 R, price slippage −0.0535 R, notional charge −0.0793 R, net +0.0732 R — friction consumes 64%. 85.6% stopped out, 13.9% net winners, median trade −1.10 R, p99 +20.4 R. All profit is a 5% right tail. Long-only 0.721 / short-only 0.719 (symmetric, so not a short-side artifact).

POST-PAPER window (2024-01→2026-08, entirely after the authors' sample): same pattern, zero-cost 2.865, T6 1.207/0.921, DSR 0.4186 — DEAD on the same gates. No decay since publication: what removes it is cost, not crowding.

RECOMMENDATION (owner's call, put with a recommendation per standing process): do NOT forward-test yet. The one measurement that would settle it is tick-level EXIT and entry-bar timing on the held-out stock-days — B22B's frozen harness already does the entry half, the exit leg has never been measured (half the T6 round trip is an `ADVERSE_PROXY_FOR_AN_UNMEASURED_LEG`), and it resolves a −8.36-to-+1.09 spread. Second unresolved item: capacity — B22B measured tens-to-hundreds of shares resting at the touched side, and this test charges a price but never asks whether 20%-of-equity per name fills.

Power census: RAN FIRST but its own verdict field reads POWER-BLOCKED (G3 0.0863 R vs 0.080 R) and the window was spent anyway on a post-hoc reading of which gates carry a blocking consequence — disclosed both ways, ex-ante text supports it, no positive claim rests on it.
verdict.reason: The headline verdict DEAD is correct and I could not refute it; every correction I found pushes further toward dead, not less. I reproduced the primary held-out result bit-for-bit from the cache, re-verified all eight pinned hashes, confirmed the freeze ordering by mtime, confirmed the empirical slippage file really derives from B22B's 100 ms rung, and confirmed the DSR/permutation arithmetic by hand. Guardrails hold: HEAD is still 7c5c870 with research/trading_bot and scripts/trading_bot/t17_* untracked, the .gitignore diff is T3/T16 only (not this agent), DECISIONS.md and FINDINGS.md mtimes predate the T17 window and contain no "T17", and the collector is GET-only against data.alpaca.markets and paper-api /v2/assets with no order path. The flagged 2.4 GB research/data/t17_cache is real and git check-ignore confirms it is NOT ignored. Two things are overstated in the supporting narrative and should be corrected before this is indexed. (1) I ran the adversarial test the executor did not: ZERO COST under the maximally adverse entry-bar rule gives held-out Sharpe -6.155 with 98.8% drawdown and mean gross -0.368 R, versus +2.743 / 11.4% / +0.212 R under the frozen "close" rule. So T17_RESULT.md section 6 item 1 ("the ORB rule is real and this rig reproduces it") is not independent implementation validation — the reproduction of the paper's 2.81 is a property of the bar-granularity choice, which the same document elsewhere calls its single most load-bearing unresolved assumption. By extension "honest friction cuts it to 0.674-1.088", the "knife edge" framing and "what removes it is cost, not crowding" all hold only under that favourable choice; under the adverse one the rule is destroyed before any friction is charged. The executor does disclose the -8.36 full_bar sensitivity prominently and says the truth lies between +1.09 and -8.36, so this is a framing error rather than concealment, but the "Established" list should not contain the reproduction claim. Relatedly, the pre-friction +0.206 R against the paper's own +0.08 R is attributed to relative-volume selection with no test; the paper's figure sitting between the close-rule +0.21 and the full_bar -0.37 is at least as consistent with the close rule being too generous. (2) The drawdown match "11.4% against the paper's claimed 12%" is quoted on the held-out window; on the design window, which is the one that actually overlaps the paper's 2016-2023 sample, the same rig gives zero-cost max drawdown 28.0% — a number T17_RESULT.md never reports. One process deviation for the owner: T17_POWER_CENSUS.json's verdict field literally says POWER-BLOCKED because G3 failed at 0.0863 R against 0.080 R, and the held-out window was spent on an interpretation of which gates block that was articulated after the failure was observed. It is defensible from the frozen gate's own ex-ante text (blocking consequences attached only to G1 and G4; the per-trade statistic twice designated a diagnostic), both readings are preserved unedited, and the outcome was negative so no false positive rests on it — but the held-out window is now spent, which bears on the executor's own recommendation to re-run under a new pre-registration after tick-level exit measurement. Recommend the finding be recorded as DEAD with the reproduction claim downgraded to "reproduces the paper conditional on the entry-bar stop rule", and the owner asked whether the spent window and the tick-measurement follow-up are worth the next slice.

result.detail:
WHAT WAS BUILT

1. `scripts/trading_bot/forward_eval.py` (1,319 lines) — a read-only evaluator over any registered paper-strategy ledger. Subcommands: `report` (text/`--json`), `status-line`, `list`, `selftest`. It reports: realised PnL two ways (unit-notional curve with the T-bill leg, and the broker's paper equity, with the note that the paper account earns no interest so `model_excash` is the comparable curve); exposure path (min/mean/max/latest, changes/yr, time at cap) plus a reconstruction check that every logged weight equals `min(w_max, target/realised_vol)` from the rule the record itself carries; drawdown vs the un-overlaid benchmark (labelled `DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY`) AND vs the T13 ex-post vol-matched constant-weight null N1 (bisection-solved on the forward window); days/sessions/years elapsed with >5-session discontinuities; raw and paired-vs-N1 hit rate; FG3 fidelity; FG4 rail measurement; a five-gate summary in the frozen read order; and the certifiability readout.

2. `research/trading_bot/ITERATION_PROTOCOL.md` (277 lines) — the honest-iterate half. §0 one rule: a running strategy's rule is immutable, improvement is a NEW pre-registered forward test with its own ledger. §2 a table mapping every observation to its permitted response (for "the curve is down" and "a parameter would obviously have been better", the permitted response is *none*). §3 the maintenance-vs-rule-change test ("would the fix change the weight the strategy targeted on a day it already traded?"). §4 the eight-step stand-up procedure with the POWER GATE FIRST and frozen before it is computed (T15 precedent: killed by its own gate before burning the held-out window). §4b two tests may run at once but both count as trials forever. §7 seven declared retirement conditions with distinct verdicts (DEAD / INVALIDATED / DISCONTINUED / SUPERSEDED / OWNER CALL) and the rule that ledgers are closed, never deleted. §8 eleven explicitly forbidden moves.

3. `research/trading_bot/FORWARD_REGISTER.json` — the machine-readable register. The evaluator verifies each entry's pre-registration sha256 on every run and REFUSES to score a strategy whose document moved. T4 registered as RUNNING with its prior verdict (DEAD on T13's gate) recorded in the entry.

4. `scripts/trading_bot/t4_eval_entrypoint.sh` + cron line: `30 22 * * 1-5 /home/anont/meme/scripts/trading_bot/t4_eval_entrypoint.sh` (this box is Europe/Amsterdam and ET is local−6 year-round, so 22:30 local = 16:30 ET, half an hour after the close; a `CRON_TZ=America/New_York` variant is documented too). It writes `FORWARD_EVAL.json` and refreshes `FORWARD_STATUS.txt`.

5. One-line dashboard status, e.g. `T4 T13-VOL-L60-T0.1-WMAX1.0 PAPER | 0 settled sessions (0.00y) | realised n/a | N1 n/a | crashes 0/3 (3 more, ~27y) | NOT CERTIFIABLE -- NO VERDICT`. It leads with the denominator, never the PnL (asserted in a test). Written to `research/trading_bot/FORWARD_STATUS.txt`.

6. `tests/test_forward_eval.py` — 49 hermetic tests, all passing; `tests/test_t4_forward.py`'s 52 still pass (101 total in 48s).

GUARDRAIL 1 ENFORCED IN CODE, NOT PROMISED. `_refuse_if_protected()` runs before every write and refuses any path ending `_LOG.jsonl`, `_STATE.json`, `_AUTHORISATION.json`, `_PREREGISTRATION.md/.json`, `_FROZEN_CONFIG.json` or `FORWARD_REGISTER.json` — by suffix, so a future strategy's ledger is protected the day it is created. Verified end-to-end: `report --write research/trading_bot/T4_FORWARD_LOG.jsonl` exits 2 with REFUSED and the ledger's md5 is byte-identical before and after (9f4b11788a74f405caaf9c82115b72cb). There is no subcommand, flag or code path in the module that alters a rule.

CURRENT HONEST READING OF THE REAL LOG. 2 run records, 0 settled sessions, 0 reconciled fills — the first weight (0.7242) was decided and a 93-share MOC submitted on 2026-08-17, but the close it earns has not printed. Every metric is therefore null *by arithmetic*, and the report says so rather than emitting zeros. Certifiability: 0 of 3 crash episodes; 3 more ≈ 27 years before ANY verdict; recomputed power table gives 5.0 / 10.2 / 13.7 crashes for 50/80/90% power ≈ 45/92/123 years (matches T4 prereg §6 exactly).

VALIDATION ON A 400-SESSION SYNTHETIC LEDGER CONTAINING ONE ≥20% CRASH. This is the finding worth carrying: the easy benchmark comparison reads **+11.57 pp** while the honest vol-matched null reads **+1.17 pp** — a ~10× gap on identical data. That is precisely the T13 §5i error the N1 gate exists to catch, now demonstrated numerically by the evaluator itself, and it is why the benchmark figure is shipped tagged `DIAGNOSTIC_ONLY` and can never be printed without N1 beside it. The N1 null matches the strategy's realised volatility to 1e-6 (asserted). Injecting a single bad weight makes FG3 report `FAIL -- WINDOW INVALIDATED`.

HOW THE FORBIDDEN NUMBERS ARE FENCED. T4 prereg §8 forbids a CAGR/Sharpe/p-value from a short sample, but a power calculation needs an effect-size estimate. Rather than hide it, every such number lives under `certifiability.power_arithmetic.inputs_that_are_not_results`, which carries its own all-caps disclaimer; the FG1 bootstrap is withheld entirely below 252 sessions and, when computed, ships a `NOT_LICENSED` field; FG2 is reported as NOT READABLE *because computing a CAGR is forbidden*, not because it is hard. `claims_licensed` is `[]` and `certifiable` is `false` at every sample size (asserted at n = 0, 60, 400).

To surface the status line on the dashboard, add to the `/api/state` return dict: `"forward_test": (ROOT / "research" / "trading_bot" / "FORWARD_STATUS.txt").read_text().strip() if (...).exists() else None`, and render `st.forward_test` in `app.js`'s header. Four lines, read-only.
