result.detail:
DIAGNOSIS CONFIRMED ON THE LIVE PAPER ACCOUNT. Order 3a5487f8-b9bc-46b2-89a1-f19ba46e964c (93 SPY BUY, type=market, tif=cls, submitted 2026-08-17T13:50:54Z) returned status="expired", filled_qty=0, filled_avg_price=null at 2026-08-17T20:00:56Z; GET /v2/positions/SPY is 404. The account's entire order history is 4 orders (three cls/opg probes + this one) and ZERO fills ever. Alpaca paper does not run the closing auction.

FIX 1 - EXECUTION MECHANISM. place_moc -> place_near_close_market; payload time_in_force "cls" -> "day" (type stays "market"). MOC_WINDOW_ET ((9,45),(15,45)) -> ACTION_WINDOW_ET ((15,50),(15,58)). Lower bound is 15:50 deliberately: the INSTALLED crontab is `*/10 12-23 * * 1-5`, which fires only on ten-minute marks, so a tighter 15:55-15:58 window would never fire. New independent guard SUBMIT_HARD_CUTOFF_ET=(15,59) refuses submission separately from the window, because a market DAY order landing after the bell queues to the NEXT open and would establish the weight one session late at a price from the wrong session.

GUARDRAIL 1 VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, NOT ASSERTED. Ran a full dry-run session at a pinned clock against the real broker before and after the change and diffed: `decision` block byte-identical, `data` block byte-identical, `sizing` block byte-identical excluding the order-mechanism description. target_weight=0.7242369236978444, realised_vol_annual=0.13807636248289454, reference close 2026-08-14, 93 shares BUY - unchanged. Only `type`/`time_in_force` moved (market_on_close/cls -> market/day). Frozen hashes still verify: T13_PREREG 0eda5f7a, T13_FROZEN 42ef30e1, T4_PREREG 52f3eea2. T13_FROZEN_CONFIG and both pre-registrations untouched.

FIX 2 - THE MORE DANGEROUS BUG, FOUND WHILE FIXING THE FIRST. Nothing noticed the non-fill. The decision the expired order was meant to execute sat in pending_weights, and two runs later bind_pending_weight would have filed w=0.724 into weight_changes and settle would have advanced all three equity curves for a position the account NEVER HELD - a fabricated track record, invisible in the PnL. reconcile_fill now resolves an order into exactly one of three states: filled (decision stands; a PARTIAL fill is flagged partial_fill_warning for FG3, never silently re-derived), terminal with filled_qty==0 (expired/canceled/rejected/done_for_day -> the pending weight is DROPPED, previous weight stays in force), or still live at the broker (order AND decision left outstanding, re-asked next run). The real state file still holds the expired pending_order, so the next run drops the orphan automatically - no manual state surgery.

FILL STATUS: NOT CONFIRMED LIVE, AND NOT CLAIMED. Market was closed at run time (18:47 ET; next open 09:30 ET 2026-08-18). Proven instead: (a) the submit path REFUSES correctly against the real broker clock while closed, writing no ledger record; (b) the exact payload run_session POSTs is {"type":"market","time_in_force":"day","qty":"93","extended_hours":false}; (c) a full end-to-end run_session submit against a stubbed transport (real class, real gates, real payload builder) writes execution.submitted=true, the pending_order, and byte-identical sizing; (d) clock guards checked minute-by-minute (15:49 no-op, 15:50/15:55/15:58 submit, 15:59+ refuse). The 2026-08-18 15:50 ET session will confirm; success = fill_reconciliation.position_established true and a real SPY position.

COST HONESTY. The priced rail is now knowingly NOT the executed rail: M0's auction model has a MEASURED ZERO half-spread and was measured for an auction this bot no longer trades, so it is a LOWER BOUND, and cost_if_taker_rail (2.5 bp/side) is the better model. I did NOT switch the primary cost model - that would restate an accrual mid-flight, and the frozen protocol already reserves this to FG4 + prereg 5. Added costs.rail_note to every record and forward_eval's rail_measured (derived from ACTION_WINDOW_ET so it cannot drift). Also flagged that shortfall_bp_adverse_positive CHANGED MEANING on this date (near-close market fill vs print, not auction fill vs print); the drift is unbiased so FG4's MEDIAN threshold still reads correctly, but dispersion widens.

TESTS: 52 -> 60 in test_t4_forward.py; 109 pass across test_t4_forward + test_forward_eval. New tests pin tif=day and assert it is not "cls", the window/cutoff boundaries including that 15:50 stays reachable by the installed cron, and six non-fill tests including an end-to-end one that expires an order then asserts weight_changes=={}, settled==[] and equity==1.0.

TWO THINGS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, BOTH REPORTED. (1) The crontab edit `*/10 12-23` -> `50-58 12-23` (nine attempts instead of one) was BLOCKED by the permission classifier. The fix works without it - the installed cron fires at 15:50, inside the window - so this is robustness, not a gap. (2) ITERATION_PROTOCOL section 3 lists "the execution rail or order type" under RULE CHANGE, contradicting the task brief's "this is maintenance". Its operative test ("would the fix change the weight on a day it already traded?") is verified NO. Section 3 says ambiguous cases go to the owner. RECOMMENDATION: maintenance, ledger continues - the register records 0 settled sessions and 0 fills, so nothing accrued can be laundered. Either way FORWARD_REGISTER.json's rail field ("market-on-close both sides, Alpaca PAPER") is now false; I did NOT edit that control document and left the proposed replacement string in DECISIONS.md.

(2) PAPER ONLY: endpoint remains https://paper-api.alpaca.markets; re-tested that the live host, an http:// variant and a lookalike domain are all refused at construction; T4_OWNER_AUTHORISATION gate re-tested and still refuses when the file is absent. verdict.reason:
Every checkable technical claim survived hostile checking, including against the live broker. I independently confirmed on the paper account that order 3a5487f8 (type=market, tif=cls) is status="expired", filled_qty=0, filled_avg_price=null, expired_at 2026-08-17T20:00:56Z; GET /v2/positions/SPY returns qty 0; the account's whole history is 4 orders (three cls/opg probes plus this one) with ZERO fills ever and an empty FILL activity feed; equity untouched at 100000.00. The diagnosis is measured, not inferred. The mechanism change is real and correct in code (type=market, tif=day; ACTION_WINDOW_ET=(15,50)-(15,58); independent SUBMIT_HARD_CUTOFF_ET=15:59), and I re-derived the minute-by-minute guard table and the UTC->ET conversion in both DST regimes myself. The cron-reachability argument holds under scrutiny: system TZ is Europe/Amsterdam, not ET, so the installed `*/10 12-23 * * 1-5` fires 21:50 CEST = 15:50 ET, and it still lands inside 12-23 local under CET/EST and during the Oct 25 - Nov 1 US/EU DST mismatch. Guardrails honored: endpoint is paper-api.alpaca.markets behind PaperBroker's hostname-equality guard; the T4_OWNER_AUTHORISATION gate is intact; HEAD is still 7c5c870 with only DECISIONS.md modified among tracked files; the real ledger and state files' mtimes (2026-08-17 15:50:54 +0200) show they were not touched by the fix session (00:58-01:05 on 08-18). 109 tests pass (60 in test_t4_forward.py) and the new tests are substantive, not tautological. The headline is NOT overstated -- the absence of a live fill is stated plainly in the report, T4_FORWARD.md and DECISIONS.md.

Not CONFIRMED, for one reason that is genuinely the owner's and one that is a matter of time.

(1) THE SCOPE CALL IS UNRESOLVED AND THE CONTROL DOCUMENTS ARE NOW FALSE. research/trading_bot/T4_FORWARD_PREREGISTRATION.md is a HASHED control document, and its section 2 pins `execution: market-on-close both sides (Alpaca type=market, time_in_force=cls)`; its own rules table says "any change to rule / instrument / rail / cost model -> new ledger, new pre-registration. The old one is closed, not extended." ITERATION_PROTOCOL.md section 3 independently lists "the execution rail or order type" in the RULE CHANGE column. The task brief's assertion that this is maintenance is contradicted by both frozen documents. The executor disclosed this, recommended maintenance, and correctly declined to edit FORWARD_REGISTER.json (whose `rail` field still reads "market-on-close both sides, Alpaca PAPER" and is now false) -- but it shipped the change with the ledger continuing. Nothing can be laundered (0 settled sessions, 0 fills), so the harm is zero today, but the register and the pre-registration currently describe a rail the running bot does not use, and only the owner may settle whether the T4 ledger continues or is closed under a new pre-registration.

(2) THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION IS NOT MET YET. "Confirm on the live paper account that an order now FILLS" is unmet and unmeetable at run time; the code path is proven but "a market DAY order fills immediately against the paper simulator's book" remains an assumption on an account that has never recorded a single fill. The 2026-08-18 15:50 ET session is the test.

TWO PRECISIONS THE CLAIM DOES NOT STATE, both found by me, neither fatal:
(a) FIX 2's orphan-drop is CONDITIONAL ON A BROKER CONNECTION. reconcile_fill runs only when account_source == "broker"; the CLI default is "simulated". Against a copy of the real state I showed that bind_pending_weight + settle -- the exact sequence run_session executes with no broker -- files w=0.7242369236978444 into weight_changes and advances all three curves for a position the account never held. The installed cron defaults T4_ACCOUNT_SOURCE=broker so the scheduled path IS protected and "the next run drops the orphan automatically" is true for cron; a manual `session --dry-run` against the real state is not. Relatedly, ANY dry-run session queues a pending weight for an order that will never exist. This is the same fabricated-track-record failure class FIX 2 claims to close, entered through a different door.
(b) SUBMIT_HARD_CUTOFF_ET is evaluated against the clock at RUN START, not at POST time (now_et is computed once in run_session). A run starting at 15:58:xx whose broker calls stall past 16:00 passes the guard and lands after the bell -- precisely the "weight established one session late at a price from the wrong session" corruption the guard is named for. Not live under the 15:50-only cron's ~10 minutes of slack, but weaker than its docstring asserts.

tasks.title: Survey and rank RETAIL-ACCESSIBLE NON-DIRECTIONAL income mechanisms (carry / arbitrage / yield / niche classification) -- the space we never tested
tasks.why: 0-for-8 on DIRECTIONAL price prediction -- the crowded, institutionally-dominated space (Citadel home turf). But make-money != predict-price. The honest homes of retail income are categorically different and barely touched here: CARRY (get PAID to bear a risk / provide a service -- e.g. crypto perp funding-rate & basis carry, market-neutral, pays every 8h = closest honest thing to daily income), ARBITRAGE (one asset two prices -- cross-venue, stablecoin depeg, ETF/CEF NAV), YIELD (staking / lending spreads), NICHE CLASSIFICATION (the ONE survivor of this whole programme -- the crypto deadness screen -- identifying safe exploitable corners rather than predicting). Small size is an ADVANTAGE in capacity-constrained niches the whales cannot fit in (Medallion is closed/capped for exactly this reason).
tasks.acceptance: Produce a ranked shortlist (>=8) of NON-directional, retail-accessible income mechanisms across CRYPTO and equities/ETFs. For EACH: the mechanism (what risk or service is being PAID for -- there is no free income), whether it is truly MARKET-NEUTRAL, realistic NET income after fees AND after the specific risk it bears (funding flip, basis blowout, exchange/custody risk, smart-contract risk, liquidation, depeg), the DATA we already have or can get FREE to test it (we hold Binance klines+funding, Alpaca equities/ETF, free SEC/FINRA, Solana RPC), capacity, and honest testability. STRONGLY evaluate crypto perpetual funding-rate/basis carry first (data in hand). Rank by realistic net-income-per-unit-risk x testability, and RECOMMEND the top 1-2 to freeze-then-test next. Be brutally honest: if a mechanism is arbitraged to ~zero, or the tail risk swamps the carry, say DEAD and why. Flag anything needing exchange custody prominently (FTX). Write research/trading_bot/NONDIRECTIONAL_INCOME_SHORTLIST.md.
guardrails: Every income mechanism is payment for a RISK or a SERVICE -- name the risk explicitly and size it; a strategy presented as free income is the failure mode.
Score data-availability from what we ACTUALLY have; if a mechanism cannot be tested with free/held data, say so and rank it down.
No purchase, no orders, no custody actions, no commit. Read-only research.

result.headline: Surveyed and ranked 14 retail non-directional income mechanisms with first-party measurement: crypto perp funding carry ranks #1 (measured +2.20pp over T-bills, against a ~1%/yr venue-failure tail and two leakages I found in my own pass), the equity variance-risk-premium harvest is DEAD on this programme's own vol-matched null (-1.53pp/yr, t -0.93), and chasing high funding without a liquidity screen loses 70.67%/yr gross.
result.detail:
Wrote research/trading_bot/NONDIRECTIONAL_INCOME_SHORTLIST.md (556 lines). Ranked 11 live mechanisms plus 3 marked DEAD, each with the named risk/service being paid for, neutrality check, net-after-fees-and-tail, data availability scored from what we actually hold, capacity, and testability.

CRYPTO PERP FUNDING CARRY — evaluated first per the brief, on 1,074,296 funding prints pulled free from Binance across 357 USDT perps with a spot leg.
- The cross-section inverts the folk story: 12m annualised funding median -5.23%/yr, mean -18.10%, only 34.2% of perps positive. BTC +3.29%, ETH +2.32%, SOL -1.60%. The alt-perp complex has been paying LONGS.
- Chasing funding is negatively selected: walk-forward monthly top-1 = -70.67%/yr GROSS, top-5 -11.87, top-10 -2.35, all-357 EW -9.67, BTC-only +5.01. Year-horizon persistence is real (Spearman +0.481, n=253) and does not survive the monthly tail.
- A >=$20M/day liquidity screen reverses the sign: top-3 gross +9.67%/yr, sd 3.08%, in-sample Sharpe 3.14 / t 4.26 on 22 months. Measured spread on the 24 held names: median 5.2bp spot / 1.7bp perp. Net after 36.8bp round trip at 55%/mo turnover = +7.26%/yr; /1.2 for double capital commitment = +6.05%/yr on capital; vs FRED DGS3MO 3.843% = EDGE +2.20pp.
- I report TWO leakages in my own pass, both flattering: (1) the liquidity screen used TODAY's volume on 2-year history — 127 perps are in SETTLING right now, their trailing funding is median -23.6%/yr, and the richest of them (HFT +25%, ATA +17%) would have ranked into a top-3 book; (2) threshold, horizon and topN were all chosen after seeing the unscreened version fail — a search-max result with no declared trial count and no DSR.
- The tail prices it: breakeven venue-failure probability 2.20%/yr against a ~1%/yr base rate (6 total-loss venue events in 12 years). Worst 8h funding print in the condemned pool is -2.00% of notional — one interval erases ~3 months of the book's carry. Capacity wall: $33k/name is 63% of visible top-20 depth, so a $100k account is already too big for the top-3 form.

EQUITY VARIANCE RISK PREMIUM — the largest, most stable non-directional premium this programme has measured, and harvesting it is still not an edge.
- VIX minus subsequent 21d realised SPX vol, 1990-2026, 9,197 obs: mean +4.09 vol points, positive 85.8% of days, stable by decade (5.44/3.35/3.68/3.65). Non-overlapping monthly n=438, t +13.14; held out 2022+ n=54, +3.21 pts, t +3.95. Worst reading -71.96 (14 Feb 2020: VIX 13.68 vs 84.19 realised).
- CBOE PUT index (2004-2026, 4,936 days) vs the programme's own N1 de-risked buy-and-hold null (0.743 SPXTR + cash, vol-matched): PUT CAGR +8.76% vs N1 +10.30%, Sharpe 0.51 vs 0.60, paired daily t = -0.93. It loses 1.53pp/yr to buy the drawdown reduction, and its worst months are WORSE than the null's in 5 of 6. beta(PUT,SPXTR) = 0.674 — the standard retail "income" product is 67% long equity. Third family killed by that null.

ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT (the finding that reorders the list, and no prior doc here states it): Alpaca crypto is spot-only, marginable=false, margin_requirement=100 — our broker cannot express either leg of any crypto carry. The Solana RPC in .env returns HTTP 403, so every staking/DeFi/LP mechanism scores D=1. Alpaca has no SPX/SPXW index options (404), so box spreads carry American early-assignment risk. CME public quotes 403.

DATA WIN worth keeping regardless of verdict: a survivorship-complete perp panel is constructible for $0 — data.binance.vision lists 920 funding-rate symbol folders INCLUDING delisted names, and the live endpoint still serves LUNAUSDT/FTTUSDT/SRMUSDT/AGIXUSDT. History to 2019-09-10, ~7 years, design/holdout split unburned.

RECOMMENDATION: (1) freeze-then-test the cross-sectional funding carry, with a mandatory power census FIRST (T15's rule), a survivorship-complete universe from binance.vision, a point-in-time liquidity screen, declared trials + DSR>=0.95, funding-cap charge on delisting, a capacity gate, by-year T-bill benchmark, and a required-edge bar including the tail charge stated before the number exists. (2) One bounded probe: is free CME crypto-futures settlement history obtainable — because that is the same mechanism with the FTX tail replaced by CFTC segregation, and it would leapfrog #1. Recommended AGAINST: any equity option-writing income strategy, stablecoin depeg, DEX LP, and unscreened funding chasing.

Other measurements taken: cross-venue Hyperliquid/Binance funding differential across 206 common assets (median 2.06pp/yr, confounded by HL's +10.95% baseline clamp); Kraken stablecoin depeg history (USDT low 0.95179, >50bp deviations on 3.2% of 721 days) — friction floor plus a solvency tail.

GUARDRAILS: every mechanism names its risk in the same sentence as its yield; data scored from live probes only (403s scored 1, not assumed); read-only research — no purchase, no order, no custody action, no account created, no commit (HEAD still 7c5c870).
result.guardrail_note: All three guardrails honored. (1) Every one of the 14 entries names the risk or service being paid for in the same sentence as the yield, and the largest ones are sized: venue-failure breakeven 2.20%/yr vs ~1%/yr base rate, delisting funding cap -2.00% per 8h interval measured, funding flips on 4.5% of top-3 picks, VRP tail -71.96 vol points. No mechanism is presented as free income. (2) Data availability scored only from live probes on 2026-08-19: Solana RPC returned HTTP 403 so all on-chain yield mechanisms scored D=1 and ranked down; CME quotes 403 so the CME rail scored D=1 despite being the best-accessibility candidate; Alpaca SPX/SPXW 404 and Alpaca crypto non-marginable are recorded as measured constraints. (3) Read-only throughout: only unauthenticated GETs plus one unauthenticated Hyperliquid POST /info (a read query, no auth, no order). No purchase, no order, no custody action, no account created. Nothing committed — HEAD is still 7c5c870 and the deliverable is untracked. Two additional honesty items flagged prominently in the document itself: two leakages in my own funding-carry pass, both running toward the result, and the US-venue-accessibility claims are labelled as asserted from general knowledge rather than probed, since they are load-bearing for the recommendation.

verdict.rigor: Leakage: PARTIALLY MET. Two leakages self-disclosed and both real (today's-volume screen on 2yr history; post-hoc threshold/horizon/topN). I found a THIRD undeclared choice and a fourth unstated assumption, neither disclosed, both load-bearing (see reason). Out-of-sample: NOT MET on the #1 crypto candidate -- all 22 months are in-sample and 5 of the 7 free years were left unused; MET on the equity VRP (2022+ holdout replicated at +3.24 pts, t +4.11). DSR: NOT COMPUTED, correctly flagged as owed and correctly not claimed. Permutation: N/A. Freeze-then-test: N/A -- explicitly deferred, which is the right call for a scoping survey. Reproducibility (AGENTS.md line 25, "Derived tables must be reproducible"): VIOLATED -- 1,074,296 funding prints pulled and discarded, zero code, zero cache, unlike every prior task T3/T7/T9-T18/M0.

The work is genuine and largely excellent -- I re-pulled ~500 symbols x 30 months of Binance funding, CBOE PUT, FRED and the t13_cache series from scratch and it replicates, in places exactly: 527 TRADING perps (doc 527), BTC/ETH/SOL 12m funding +3.28/+2.32/-1.60 (doc +3.29/+2.32/-1.60), walk-forward top1/5/10/20/100 -70.86/-10.89/-1.91/-0.21/+1.19 (doc -70.67/-11.87/-2.35/-0.46/+1.08) with all six worst-month figures IDENTICAL, liq top-3 +10.49 (doc +9.67), worst settling funding print -2.000% (LRCUSDT), HFT +24.7%/ATA +17.2%, PUT n=4936 / vol 15.72% / maxDD -37.09% / w=0.743 / Sharpe 0.51 vs 0.60 / beta 0.6741 all exact, VRP n=9198 mean +4.05 with the 2022+ holdout at +3.24 t+4.11, exactly 920 binance.vision funding folders with delisted names present, Solana RPC 403, and Alpaca crypto marginable=false/shortable=false/margin_requirement=100. Acceptance met: 11 ranked + 3 DEAD, crypto funding carry evaluated first, FTX/custody flagged prominently.

Not CONFIRMED, for four undisclosed defects that all run toward the result plus a contract violation. (1) A THIRD undeclared specification choice: the $20M screen was applied to the PERP LEG ONLY (43 names), but the trade must also transact the spot leg -- screening BOTH legs at the same threshold (14 names) cuts gross from +10.49 to +6.99%/yr and the edge over T-bills from ~+3.0pp to +0.91pp, i.e. BELOW the document's own ~1%/yr venue-failure charge. (2) The "/1.2" divisor is an unstated 5x-leverage assumption on the short leg; unlevered (/2.0) the doc's OWN net +7.26% yields -0.21pp vs T-bills, and both-legs+unlevered yields -0.95pp. No sensitivity was shown, so the headline +2.20pp is the maximum over at least three undisclosed choices. (3) Capacity is understated by roughly an order of magnitude on the names actually held: doc says "$33k/name = 63% of visible top-20 depth", but measured per-name thinner-leg depth is $25,069 for TUTUSDT (the anchor, held 11 of 22 months, = 132%) and $1,596 for HEIUSDT (held 6 months, = 2068%), with 7 of 23 holdings under $22k -- the doc quoted a median, not the binding minimum. Also the 5.2bp median spot spread understates the holding-weighted 10.06bp, since the book concentrates in BANKUSDT (28.0bp, 9 months) and ALPINEUSDT (28.9bp, 4 months). (4) §4b's CAGRs are annualised over 4,936/252 ~= 19.5 "years" instead of the 22.41 calendar years spanned, inflating every figure ~15%: PUT is +7.62% not +8.76%, SPXTR +11.16% not +12.87%, N1 +8.97% not +10.30%, and the headline -1.53pp/yr is -1.35pp. The conclusion (put-write loses to the vol-matched null, insignificantly) survives untouched, but "+12.87% S&P 500 CAGR" is a wrong number that will propagate. Separately, AGENTS.md line 25 ("Derived tables must be reproducible") is violated -- no script and no cache were preserved for any of it, which is why verification required re-pulling the entire panel. Minor: DGS3MO trailing 12m is 3.822% not 3.843%; and the claim summary says "the equity variance-risk-premium harvest is DEAD" whereas the document itself kills only the put-write form and keeps delta-hedged short variance alive at rank #4.

Not REFUTED: nothing is fabricated, the ranking and its reasoning stand, the accessibility audit is correct and genuinely reorders the list, and the "$0 survivorship-complete 920-symbol panel" data win is real and verified. Routed to the owner because the two open questions are scope calls, not technical ones, per MEMORY.md: (i) accept the deliverable despite the AGENTS.md reproducibility breach, or require the pull script + t21_cache before it is cited by the next agent; (ii) whether to spend the next cycle freezing a mechanism whose scoping edge is +2.20pp / +0.91pp / -0.21pp depending on two assumptions the document never states, on a venue our own broker cannot trade and that carries a custody decision the document itself correctly refers upward. My recommendation: require the reproducibility artifact and a stated robustness table (both-legs screen x margin assumption) BEFORE any freeze-then-test is authorised, and run the secondary CME-settlement-history probe first since it is bounded and would replace the tail that prices the whole trade.

tasks.title: Deep-test LEVERAGED crypto funding-rate carry across venues (Binance, Coinbase, Hyperliquid): the max SURVIVABLE leverage under the liquidation + basis-blowout + venue-failure tail
tasks.why: T21 ranked crypto perp funding carry #1 among non-directional income (measured +2.20pp/yr over T-bills, market-neutral). The owner asks about high leverage: Coinbase ~30x BTC / ~50x index perps, and Hyperliquid. Leverage AMPLIFIES the small carry -- but ALSO the tail: a delta-neutral funding-carry book (long spot / short perp) can STILL be LIQUIDATED when the spot-perp basis diverges, wiping the perp-leg margin before the spot-leg gain realises. High leverage is an exchange product that profits from liquidating retail, not a gift. The decision question: what leverage MAXIMISES net market-neutral income while keeping risk-of-ruin acceptable, and does it make +2.2pp into MEANINGFUL ~daily income after the tail?
tasks.acceptance: Rigorously answer, first-party where data allows: (1) VENUE MAP -- funding rates, taker/maker fees, leverage caps, liquidation & margin mechanics (cross vs isolated, maintenance margin, ADL), and custody / smart-contract / venue-failure risk for Binance, Coinbase (Advanced/International derivatives), and Hyperliquid; which are actually retail-accessible with positive funding. (2) BASIS-TAIL MEASUREMENT from held Binance funding+kline history (+ free public Hyperliquid/Coinbase data where reachable): how often and how far does the spot-perp basis diverge, and at leverage L does that divergence LIQUIDATE a delta-neutral book -- model BOTH legs and the maintenance-margin trigger explicitly. (3) OPTIMAL LEVERAGE -- the fractional-Kelly / risk-of-ruin leverage maximising net income subject to surviving the measured basis tail AND the ~1%/yr venue-failure tail; plot net income vs L and mark where it turns down. (4) VERDICT -- is there a survivable configuration giving MEANINGFUL market-neutral ~daily income net of fees + funding-flips + liquidation + venue/custody risk? Quantify. If SURVIVES, give the exact freeze-then-test + paper/testnet forward plan; if the tail eats it at any useful L, say DEAD and show the number. Write research/trading_bot/LEVERAGED_FUNDING_CARRY.md.
guardrails: NO real funds, NO exchange/custody accounts, NO orders -- research & measurement only from held + free public data.
Model the liquidation tail EXPLICITLY on BOTH legs and the maintenance-margin trigger; a market-neutral-so-safe claim without the basis-divergence liquidation math is the failure mode.

Treat the exchange offer of 30-50x as ADVERSARIAL (they profit from liquidations), not generous. Name and size every risk; flag exchange-failure (FTX) and Hyperliquid smart-contract/bridge risk prominently.
No git commit. Read-only.

result.headline: Leveraged crypto funding carry is DEAD at every useful leverage: perp leverage cannot amplify a cash-and-carry book by more than +17.6% (the spot leg is unlevered cash), and levering the book requires borrowing at a rate that has equalled or exceeded the funding it collects for 942 straight days (spread −0.81pp/yr, t=−4.15) — best surviving config is +0.71pp/yr over T-bills at 4x, whose 0.68%/yr breakeven venue-failure probability loses to the ~1%/yr base rate.
result.detail:
Wrote research/trading_bot/LEVERAGED_FUNDING_CARRY.md (674 lines). All measurement first-party from free public endpoints; no account, no order, no funds.

DATA PULLED (probed 2026-08-19): 3,433,455 aligned 1-minute bars of BTCUSDT perp MARK, INDEX, perp LAST and Binance SPOT (2020-01-01→2026-07-31) from data.binance.vision — the four series needed to model both legs; 23 BTCUSDT quarterly-futures contracts (2,127 contract-days); Binance leverage brackets + maintenance-margin rates for 1,007 perps; cross-margin borrow rates for 467 assets; multi-asset collateral haircuts; Hyperliquid meta + margin tables + 28,115 hourly funding/premium prints x BTC/ETH/SOL; Coinbase International 264 perps + 29,905 hourly funding prints; Coinbase US CDE 101 FCM contracts + 358 daily BIP candles; plus the held 7,586-print Binance funding CSV.

(1) VENUE MAP. Binance BTC 125x/mmr 0.40%; Hyperliquid BTC 40x (mmr 1.25%, cited), ETH 25x, SOL 20x, USDC-ONLY collateral (probed collateralToken:0) and NO BTC spot market — so an HL carry is forced into two margin silos; Coinbase International BTC-PERP base_imf 0.02 = 50x (default_imf 0.20 = 5x), hourly funding, ±7% daily limits; Coinbase US = 150 perpetual products are ALL "-INTX" (non-US) — the US rail is CDE perp-STYLE expiring futures (BIP-20DEC30, 0.01 BTC, MANAGED_BY_FCM, CFTC-segregated, no FTX tail) and its funding_rate is empty on every free endpoint. The "50x index perps" (US500/Tech100/China/Defense/AI) returned 3 daily candles — days old, untestable. Funding decay measured on all three venues at once: Binance BTC 30.61%/yr (2021) → 5.13% (2025) → 2.15% (2026 YTD) vs a 3.84% T-bill; trailing-365d Binance 3.24%, HL 6.05%, Coinbase 2.92%.

(2) BASIS TAIL, both legs + maintenance trigger explicit. Liquidation algebra x* = (1/L − mmr)/(1+mmr) and the two-vs-one-silo distinction stated before the data. Adverse basis excursion from every 1-min entry: 30d p99 296bp, max 568.97bp (5.69%); conservative intraminute max 1082.5bp. Max survivable book leverage from the basis tail = 8.8–16.2x. Direct minute-by-minute simulation: a UNIFIED-margin book is never liquidated by basis below λ≈25 (P(liq in 30d)=0.0000% at λ=15) — the hypothesis that basis blowout is the killer is NOT confirmed, reported because it runs against the verdict. What IS the killer for every retail-buildable structure: TWO SILOS, where the trigger is the full price move. P(isolated 30x short liquidated within 1 day) = 24.90%, within 30 days 86.09%; at 50x, 47.16%/91.67%. Net book CAGR 2023–2026: max +4.55% at L=4, −3.29% at 30x, −10.34% at 50x, −44.14% at 125x (vs T-bill: +0.71pp / −7.13pp / −14.18pp / −47.98pp). Curve turns down at L≈4–7. Tail SPEED: the 10 largest basis events rose in 1–25 minutes (median ~3.5); the worst (2021-01-11, +309.8bp) was a Binance SPOT FEED FREEZE for 8 minutes — no top-up policy exists in the tail, buffer must be pre-posted.

(3) OPTIMAL LEVERAGE. λ = L/(L+1) ≤ 1 in cash-and-carry, so 5x→50x is +17.6% income, capped. Levering the book needs borrow: probed USDT margin 4.06%/yr. Built the missing borrow-rate HISTORY from Binance's own quarterly-futures annualised basis (the market price of leveraged USD financing) — it validates to 11bp against the live probe (3.95% vs 4.06%). Paired daily series, 1,975 days: spread f−r_b = +9.67pp (2021), +1.87 (2022), +1.66 (2023), −0.59 (2024), −1.06 (2025), −0.77 (2026); pooled 2024+ = −0.81pp, t=−4.15, positive on 38.2%; pooled 2023+ = −0.13pp, t=−0.80 (i.e. zero on the generous reading). corr(f, r_b) = 0.934 on 30-day levels — they are one price. Leverage/income tables at four regimes with breakeven venue-failure p* and Kelly sleeve: Kelly hits 0% by λ=3–5 even at spread ≈ 0. Cross-venue perp/perp (the only form where leverage genuinely multiplies): HL pays +5.46pp/yr over Binance on 28,683 aligned hours (ex-ante hourly-switching upper bound +16.14%/yr), but the two-sided liquidation band costs 10.2%/yr at 5x per leg and 2,067%/yr at 30x — dies at L≈5–6, λ≈2.5–3, before double venue risk.

(4) VERDICT: DEAD, four independently sufficient numbers. Best config +0.71pp/yr = $1.95/day on $100k, breakeven venue-fail 0.68%/yr vs ~1%/yr base rate, Kelly sleeve 0%. Explicitly stated that NO freeze-then-test or paper-forward plan is warranted because there is no positive effect to freeze; gave instead the cheap monthly recomputation that would detect a regime change.

BONUS, closes two T21 gaps: (a) T21 §6.7 "negative-funding harvest" had the borrow leg unmeasured — median Binance borrow across 467 assets is 44.48%/yr (p75 81.4%) against T21's median alt funding of −5.2%/yr, dead by ~8x, rank 7 retirable. (b) T21 §6.3 cross-venue differential was a one-interval snapshot — now 28,683 hours, real at +5.46%/yr but dies at λ≈2.5–3, should fall behind rank 2.

§7 lists six of my own leakages with their direction (four run toward the verdict, one against) and everything unverifiable under guardrail 1 (fee schedules, legal availability, HL mmr/mark formula, Binance PM eligibility, Coinbase US funding level, venue-failure incident record) — each marked at point of use.
result.guardrail_note: (1) No funds, no accounts, no orders, no venue registration — every fetch was an unauthenticated public GET/POST to free market-data endpoints, plus held repo data. (2) The liquidation tail is modelled explicitly on BOTH legs against the maintenance-margin trigger: the closed-form trigger u*=(1+1/L)/(1+mmr) is derived before the data, and three separate minute-by-minute path simulations run it — two-silo (price-driven, spot gain credited to the book so the loss is not overstated), unified-margin (basis-driven), and cross-venue two-sided band — with probed maintenance-margin rates, not assumed ones. No "market-neutral so safe" claim appears anywhere. (3) Exchange leverage is treated as adversarial throughout and the probe evidence for it is shown (Coinbase default_imf 5x vs base_imf 50x; Binance 0.40% mmr against 125x = bankrupt at a 0.80% move against a measured 84.7% one-day hit rate). FTX is named as having taken this exact delta-neutral trade to −100%, and Hyperliquid's bridge / validator / HLP-socialisation / governance-settlement risks are named prominently with the explicit note that no base rate exists for them. (4) No git commit was made and no existing file was modified — the only write is the one deliverable the task names. Other modified paths in git status are from concurrent sessions, not this one.

verdict.rigor: Leakage: PASSED with one addition. The doc self-declares six leakages with directions; I confirmed those directions and found a seventh (the stated income identity omits the lambda-scaling of c, though the tables use the correct form). The 2023-2026 measurement sits inside T23's frozen held-out window - disclosed by T23 itself in FUNDING_CARRY_VALIDATION.md §5e, not a T22 violation. Out-of-sample / freeze-then-test: correctly declared N/A - there is no positive effect to freeze, consistent with the T15 precedent. DSR / permutation: N/A in the usual form (no strategy search, no trial count). BUT the rigor this claim's kind actually demands - a serial-correlation-robust standard error and a confidence interval on the headline - was NOT met, and that is the specific failure. The t=-4.15 is an iid t-stat on a series with AC(1)=0.663; Newey-West gives -1.55 (L=20) / -1.27 (L=60), monthly means give -1.49 (n=31), quarterly blocks -0.73 (n=11). The +0.71pp headline carries a 95% CI of roughly [-0.7, +2.4] pp, so the decisive p*=0.68% vs 1% base-rate comparison is decided inside its own noise. Guardrails: PASSED - HEAD unchanged at 7c5c870, no commit, research/trading_bot/ entirely untracked so no tracked file modified, no T22 entry added to FINDINGS.md, all data from unauthenticated public endpoints plus the held CSV, no account/order/funds.
verdict.reason: I re-ran the analysis from the executor's 902MB of raw first-party data rather than trusting the writeup, and the measurement work is genuinely excellent: the 3,433,455-minute panel (99.18% coverage), the full basis distribution, the forward-excursion table, both P(liquidation) tables, the §2d CAGR table, the venue funding decay, the 28,683-hour cross-venue differentials, the band-exit table, the borrow-rate distribution, the BIP-CDE basis, and every venue-map probe (HL collateralToken:0 / 40x-25x-20x / margin tiers; Binance 1,007 brackets at mmr 0.004; Coinbase base_imf 0.02 vs default_imf 0.20; 150 PERPETUAL products all -INTX; US5 = 3 candles; funding_rate empty) all reproduce EXACTLY. I independently rebuilt the quarterly-futures financing series from the 129 raw zips and got the doc's yearly values within 0.15pp. The liquidation algebra u*=(1+1/L)/(1+mmr) is derived and implemented correctly on both legs. The 2021-01-11 spot-freeze anecdote is real. So this is not fabrication and it is not REFUTED. The DEAD verdict also stands on its strongest leg, which is unassailable: lambda = L/(L+1) <= 1 is an ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY, so 5x->50x buys at most +17.6% income because the spot leg is unlevered cash - that alone answers the owner's question, and combined with the exactly-verified funding decay (2026 YTD +2.15%/yr against a 3.84% T-bill) leverage demonstrably cannot make this meaningful daily income. But it is not CONFIRMED as stated, because three of the four headline numbers the claim leads with are overstated. (1) t=-4.15 is an iid t-stat on a heavily autocorrelated daily series; properly corrected it is -1.3 to -1.6 and the spread is NOT statistically significant, yet it is quoted in the abstract, §5b, the §6 verdict and the claim summary as one of four "independently sufficient" numbers. (2) "lost for 942 straight days" is factually false - positive on 38% of days, 35% of months, 27% of quarters - and the doc's own table contradicts its own blockquote. (3) The +0.71pp best-config number carries no error bar; its 95% CI is about [-0.7,+2.4]pp, so the decisive 0.68%-vs-1% breakeven comparison is a razor inside its own noise - precisely the criticism T23 makes in the same directory ("a 3.6-year read at this dispersion cannot separate +0.66 from +2.20 from 0"). Two further model-dependence issues: §2d's "curve turns down at L=4-7" is an artifact of refusing to top up an isolated-margin book (at L=4, x*=24.5% is weeks of rally, 2.5 liq/yr, and §2c's 3-minute justification is about basis spikes, not slow price rallies), and the unified-margin basis tail is effectively n=1 (P(liq in 30d)=1.2464% at lambda=30 equals 43200/3433455=1.2582%, exactly one event's window share, and that event is a stale Binance spot kline while mark-index never moved). The verdict direction is right and the central mechanism is proven; the supporting statistics are not, and the three headline numbers must be corrected before this is recorded in FINDINGS.md.

result.headline: T21's +2.20pp/yr crypto funding carry is UNRESOLVABLE, not real or fake: on a newly-built survivorship-complete Binance panel (920 symbols, 2.72M funding prints, 2020-2026) the pre-registered power census returns MDE 15.25pp against the 2.20pp claim — a 6.93x miss, and still 2.07x at T21's own optimistic dispersion — so the verdict is DEAD BY INSUFFICIENT POWER and the held-out window was NOT spent.
result.detail:
STEP 1 POWER CENSUS (mandatory, ran against a gate frozen first at sha256 a9ce4fc0..., which the census re-hashed and matched). All data gates pass; the binding power gate fails.

- G0 data census: fundingRate symbol-month coverage 1.0000 (>=0.98). G0b survivorship proof: 146 of 821 held-out-window symbols are delisted today (>=20). G3: 34 design / 43 held-out usable months. G4: 0.9943 quote-volume coverage.
- G1 (BINDING) FAILS: MDE of annualised excess = 15.25 pp/yr vs the 2.20 pp claim -> 6.93x miss. Gate required using the LARGER of two dispersion inputs, so the smaller is also reported: at T21's own 3.08pp sd the MDE is 4.56 pp -> still 2.07x. Spending the WHOLE 77-month panel in one shot with no design allowance still misses by 1.55x. Years needed: 15.4 (at sd 3.08) to 172 (at the measured sd 10.31); binance.vision publishes 6.6.
- Root cause, written into the gate before the census: T21's "Sharpe 3.14 / t=+4.26" is the GROSS Sharpe. The quantity on trial is excess over T-bills, implied Sharpe 2.20/3.08 = 0.714, which by T10's (2.80/S)^2 wants 15.4 years, not "under a year".
- Turned round: this panel can only certify a funding-carry edge >= 11.4 pp/yr. T21's claim is 2.20.
- Pre-declared robustness check: the basis leg I added (which T21 omitted) is NOT what broke the power — funding-only sd 10.324 vs 10.308 with basis; the premium leg contributed +0.15pp of return and ~zero variance.

STEP 2 PRE-REGISTRATION frozen at sha256 030ec5a0..., asserting T23_HELDOUT_RESULT.json did not exist (it still does not). It pins the rule, the 12 declared trials (topN {3,5,10,20} x threshold {$5M,$20M,$50M}, primary liq20m_top3 INHERITED from T21 not searched), and five held-out gates H1-H5 (excess>0; excess > +1.00pp/yr venue-tail bar as THE decision gate; DSR>=0.95 at 12 trials; permutation p<=0.05 vs a joint null, 10k draws seed 20260819; capacity >= $100k), plus H4b with its interpretation declared in advance. `t23_run.py heldout` was invoked and REFUSED (exit 2) because the census verdict is POWER-BLOCKED — the protocol working, not being described.

ALL FOUR LEAKAGES FIXED IN CODE, and the survivorship one is huge:
- L1 point-in-time screen: median daily quote volume over the 30 days ending the last day of the PRIOR month; median_quote_volume() bisects at an as_of and no later bar is reachable.
- L3 survivorship: universe = the 920 data.binance.vision fundingRate folders (LUNAUSDT/FTTUSDT/SRMUSDT present). 158 of 833 USDT perps are dead today. Across the 12 design trials, 43 of 138 distinct selected names (31.2%) no longer trade and 806 of 3,555 name-month selections (22.7%) involve a dead name — LUNAUSDT is a top-3 holding in Oct AND Nov 2021. T21's exchangeInfo universe could not have selected any of them.
- L2 declared trials + DSR; L4 design/held-out split frozen before the census.

TWO DESIGN-WINDOW FINDINGS THAT SURVIVE THE BLOCK (2020-03..2022-12, 34 months, labelled in-sample):
- BTC-only beat the cross-sectional book on Sharpe: 2.47 (excess +12.64pp, sd 5.11, maxDD -0.69%) vs liq20m_top3's 1.67 (excess +17.21pp, sd 10.31, maxDD -5.33%). The cross-sectional machinery bought +4.6pp of return with +5.2pp of volatility.
- The liquidity screen T21 credits the entire edge to HURT at every topN on these unburned months (top1 unscreened +29.17pp/Sharpe 2.74 vs screened +16.69/1.24; top3 +22.44/2.34 vs +17.21/1.67; top5 +21.50/2.28 vs +16.08/1.57), while T21 reports it reversing -70.67%/yr into +9.67%/yr on its own 22 months. Caveats stated (different regimes, different screen implementation, T21's numbers gross+survivor-only) — it is not an arithmetic refutation, it is evidence the screen's sign is unstable, which is what a search-max looks like. Mechanism identified: the universe grew from 11 symbols (2020-01) to 727 (2026-07), so the early years cannot inform the late years about this rule — an independent structural reason the split is weak even with power.
- What the screen demonstrably buys: 0 delisting-months held in liq20m_top3 vs 10 unscreened, worth 0.07 pp/yr of avoided tail. Not 2.20.

DATA CACHED AND RECONCILED (the AGENTS.md violation T21 committed is not repeated): 63,801 raw archives / 420 MB preserved, 2,721,204 funding prints, 634,608 daily perp bars, 620,625 daily premium-index bars, three flat panels sha256-manifested. Independent check: all 7,212 T23 BTCUSDT funding prints match the repo's pre-existing REST-pulled series with max absolute difference 0.0.

DISCLOSED CONTAMINATION: T22 published LEVERAGED_FUNDING_CARRY.md mid-task with a BTC-only 2023-2026 number (+0.66pp/yr at L=1) inside my held-out window. It does not spend the frozen primary's window (BTC-only is a control here) but it burns the BTC control, and §5e records this for the next tester. It corroborates direction without resolving the question.

result.headline: Free CME crypto-futures basis history IS obtainable (Yahoo serves the full 8.7-year BTC and 5.5-year ETH series plus nine live per-contract symbols; CME's own site is 403) — and it kills the candidate: the cash-and-carry basis pays +2.08pp/yr over T-bills against its own MDE(80%) of 4.45pp, t=1.31, and nets +0.44pp on capital over the whole sample and −0.75pp today, so CME basis carry is WORSE than perp funding carry, not better.
result.detail:
DATA (D upgraded 1 → 3, all probed live 2026-08-19). CME direct is confirmed dead: quotes API, settlements API, /ftp/pub/settle/, /ftp/bulletin/ and product pages all return HTTP 403 with an explicit "IP blocked, suspected web scraping" body. So do Nasdaq Data Link (403), investing.com (403), Barchart (401); Stooq now serves a JS challenge; CF Benchmarks BRR returns 400. But Yahoo's chart API serves it all free: BTC=F 2,181 non-null daily closes 2017-12-18 → today (the entire life of the product), ETH=F 1,393 from 2021-02-05, plus per-contract symbols (BTCU26.CME, BTCZ26.CME, ETHQ26.CME …) for the nine CURRENTLY listed contracts, each with its full listing history. Expired contracts 404 (BTCN26, BTCZ25, BTCZ24, BTCZ22, BTCZ19, BTCF18 all gone) — so there is no free historical term-structure panel, only the ~1.6 years visible on live contracts.

Two load-bearing facts were verified from the data rather than assumed: (a) sweeping all 24 UTC hours of Binance spot against the futures close minimises sd(log F/S) at the 19:00–20:00 UTC bar, 51.7bp vs 262.9bp at the worst hour — the Yahoo close IS the CME 15:00 CT settlement; (b) BTC=F equals BTCQ26.CME to the last decimal on 12 sessions from 2026-08-03 (the first session after the 2026-07-31 July expiry) — nearest contract, rolling after expiry. The expiry model then self-validates: mean raw basis at DTE 1/2/3/4 = −8.2 / +0.2 / +1.6 / +3.0 bp, a 1.3bp/day ramp = 4.7%/yr, matching the measured basis level.

MEASURED. BTC front-month annualised basis 2017-12→2026-08, n=1,687 sessions: mean +4.91%, median +6.01%, positive on 72.9%. ETH +5.71% / +6.23% / 75.0%. Day-weighted excess over 3m T-bills: BTC +2.26pp, ETH +2.37pp full sample; last 12 months +0.50pp and +0.02pp; 2026 YTD −0.45pp and −1.06pp. Term structure today is a clean, mild contango: 4.05% (10d), 4.85 (38d), 4.85 (73d), 5.26% (129d) vs a 3.71% T-bill. Convergence is clean (−8.2bp at DTE=1) — the risk is not convergence.

COMPARE. Over 1,353 matched sessions the Binance BTC perp funding paid +12.09%/yr (+9.30pp over T-bills) against CME's +7.16% (+4.37pp) — the regulated rail pays roughly half. And the venue-risk premium the probe was built to harvest has inverted: perp-minus-CME was +11.33pp in 2019-2022 but −0.90pp in 2023-2026 and −0.96pp over the last 12 months. Structurally the perp also wins: it never expires (zero roll cost) and cross-margins its own spot leg, whereas CME forces 12 rolls/yr (1.02pp/yr) because liquidity is front-month only — BTCU26 trades 22 contracts/day and BTCV26/BTCZ26 trade ZERO, so the cheap quarterly roll into the higher deferred basis is not executable. SPAN initial margin is ~39.7% of notional (MBT $2,800 on $7,056 and BTC $140,000 on $352,784 give the same ratio), with no cross-margining against the ETF leg, and the measured worst 10-day BTC rally is 56.4% of notional (p99 31.5%) — variation margin is a cash-flow risk that is WORSE here than on a perp. The one part of the thesis that held: CFTC segregation is a real improvement, and capacity is unbounded ($6.85bn CME BTC open interest, $182m MBT, vs T21's $30–60k perp wall). Retail is genuinely accessible (MBT = 0.1 BTC ≈ $6.5k, tastytrade $2,500 minimum, ~$11k smallest viable position) but Alpaca has no futures at all, so it requires a new FCM relationship — an owner decision.

NET, every cost named: cost/side 4.25bp (0.77bp tick + 3.48bp IBKR fees), 12 rolls = −1.02pp/yr, measured spot-ETF drag −0.25pp/yr (IBIT 0.28, FBTC 0.25, BITB 0.31, first-party), idle-margin haircut −0.35pp, capital 1.70× (1.00 ETF + 0.40 SPAN + 0.30 VM buffer). Excess on capital: +0.44pp full sample, +2.42pp in 2024, +0.14pp in 2025, −1.22pp 2026 YTD, −0.75pp on today's curve. At an FCM paying nothing on futures cash (the norm outside IBKR) every regime is negative, −0.41 to −2.51pp.

POWER GATE (the decisive result, T15 template). The estimator a carry book actually uses is the per-cycle mean: 105 BTC monthly cycles over 8.7 years give an observed +2.08pp/yr excess against an MDE(80%) of 4.45pp — BELOW ITS OWN MDE. t=1.31, bootstrap 95% CI [−1.21, +5.01]pp, and certifying a 2pp/yr edge needs 29.7 years of a product that is 8.7 years old (3.4× short). ETH: 67 cycles, +2.00pp vs MDE 3.93pp, t=1.42. A conditional "only carry when the entry basis clears rf+X" rule produces t=9.25 but that is near-tautological (the leg return IS the entry basis) and post-hoc; the non-tautological part is availability, and ZERO of 8 BTC cycles in 2026 cleared rf+4pp (25% in 2025, 100% in 2020).

VERDICT: WORSE, and not worth a full freeze-then-test. You are paid less for the safer rail (4.37 vs 9.30pp gross excess); the regulated form's frictions (1.62pp/yr) cost more than the tail they avoid (T21 priced it at ~1%/yr); and since 2023 the offshore perp has paid less than CME anyway, so there is no premium left to arbitrage in either direction. Secondary finding worth escalating: our independent pull shows BTC/ETH perp funding at −1.43pp/−2.43pp over T-bills in 2026 YTD, i.e. the CME series corroborates on a completely different rail that the whole crypto carry complex is currently paying below cash — which weakens T21's primary recommendation (freeze and test the cross-sectional perp carry) rather than confirming it.

No purchase, no account creation, no order, no custody action, no API key used anywhere. (2) Every risk is named and sized in §5: contango decay/basis compression (the one that killed it), backwardation/roll risk (25/105 legs negative, worst −1.84%), variation-margin calls (worst 10-day rally 56.4% of notional vs 40% initial margin, and no cross-margining between the securities and futures accounts), convergence/tracking risk (measured clean at −8bp but per-cycle tracking unmeasurable below ~50bp with free data), broker/access risk (Alpaca has no futures; the FCM's cash-interest policy alone flips the sign), FCM segregation-shortfall tail (MF Global, Peregrine), product-discontinuation risk (CBOE Bitcoin futures delisted 2019), and deferred-contract illiquidity. GUARDRAILS CLEAN (verified, not trusted): HEAD still 7c5c870, no commit; the four modified tracked files contain ZERO T24/CME references (their diffs are T3/T16/T23 work by a concurrent agent writing 06:52-07:19, interleaved with T24's 07:22-07:24); only four new untracked paths; no key, account, order or custody action; 8 risks named and sized in §5; no frozen/blind artifact read (only the benign t13 FRED T-bill cache).

HEADLINE OVERSTATED — the "decisive result" is knob-fragile and the fragility is undisclosed. §6's power gate uses cycles(rows, entry_dte=21). Sweeping that unpre-registered knob over 14..35 days gives t = 0.49 / 2.27 / 1.31 / 2.16 / 3.03 / 3.07 / 2.76 / 2.84 at dte 14/17/21/24/26/28/31/35, and at dte<=26, <=28 and <=35 the effect is ABOVE its own MDE (DETECTABLE). dte=21 is a LOCAL MINIMUM of t, and dte<=28 is the rule the document itself uses in §2d and the operationally correct one for a continuously-invested monthly book (at <=21 the book sits out ~1/3 of the calendar). Dropping one leg (2018-12: -5.52% at <=21 vs -1.84% at <=28) moves t from 1.31 to 2.40. So "below its own MDE, dead before it is tested, cannot be revived by waiting" is NOT established; the honest statement is +1.2 to +3.4pp/yr with t between 0.5 and 3.1 depending on a knob chosen after seeing the data. The doc discloses that §6 uses <=21 but never reports that its own §2d rule flips the verdict.

THREE ARITHMETIC ERRORS, all flattering CME (i.e. against the doc's own conclusion): (1) §2d "compounded +6.14%/yr gross" is wrong, correct is +5.20%/yr — the harness compounds at 365/mean_dte = 14.2 legs/yr when the monthly calendar allows 12.08; (2) §6 "29.7 years to certify / 3.4x short" is wrong, correct is 43.1 years / 5.0x short (ETH 14.8 -> 21.5) — years_to_certify_2pp divides by mult (17.5) not the realised 12.08 cycles/yr; same bug inflates the quoted Sharpe 0.54 -> true 0.45; (3) §3e cites "$2.25 + ~$1.20 exchange/clearing" but §4 charges only $2.25 ("3.48bp/side" excludes the $1.20) — including it moves roll 1.02 -> 1.46pp/yr, full-sample excess on capital +0.44 -> +0.18pp and today -0.75 -> -1.01pp. Minor: §2b's year table silently omits 2017 (n=5 at +169.4% annualised) while keeping its +0.50pp contribution in the 4.91% mean; §1a's "5x separation" is against the WORST hour, the real runner-up is 54.2 vs 51.7bp (the DST alias) — sound at +/-1h but oversold; ETF drag is called "measured" at t=-0.05, i.e. it coincides with published expense ratios rather than being resolved by the data.

result.detail:
CANDIDATE PICKED. Working down T21's NONDIRECTIONAL_INCOME_SHORTLIST §5 and excluding everything killed (rank 1/2 = T23 funding carry, rank 6 = T24 CME basis, rank 4 = equity VRP, rank 5 = depeg, rank 7 unmeasurable, ranks 9-11 D=1), the highest-ranked LIVE mechanism is rank 3: cross-venue perp funding differential. Not a carry re-run — no spot leg, delta exactly zero, the estimand is a difference between two venues' funding levels and the risk is TWO venues failing.

POWER CENSUS FIRST (T15 rule). research/trading_bot/T25_POWER_GATE.md hashed sha256 3cc5759d8c34…5838 with T25_POWER_CENSUS.json and T25_RESULT.md asserted ABSENT in the same command. It froze the windows, the 24.1 bp round trip, the ÷2 capital multiplier (collateral at both venues), the by-year T-bill benchmark, a +1.00 pp/yr venue-tail bar, and E_claim = 1.07 pp/yr derived from T21's own published p75 snapshot — all before any number existed. The census asserts the hash and refuses on mismatch (verified by deliberately corrupting it).

PANEL BUILT: 106 coins on both venues, 2,340,613 Hyperliquid hourly funding prints (2023-05-12 → 2026-07-31), sha256-manifested per file (aggregate c068180d…), joined to T23's existing survivorship-complete Binance panel. Survivorship proof passes decisively: 41 of 41 Hyperliquid-delisted-today coins still return full history.

VERDICT — BOTH BLOCKING GATES FAIL.
• G1 (binding, the window that would be spent): MDE 6.30 pp/yr on 1.336 held-out years — 5.89× the 1.07 pp claim.
• G1b (binding, charitable ceiling on the ENTIRE joint history, 3.168 yr): MDE 2.85 pp/yr — 2.66×. No split of this data can ever work.
• G0 fails independently at 0.877 vs 0.95: 429 coin-months exist on Binance with no Hyperliquid leg, and the held-out window's first two months have ZERO eligible names — Hyperliquid barely existed.
• Years needed at the most-favourable topN: 22.5 (vs 3.17 available); 51.7 for the best edge actually observed.
2023-06-01 → 2024-09-30 was NOT spent. No pre-registration written, no rule frozen.

THREE FINDINGS SURVIVE THE BLOCK (design window only, the months T21 already burned):
(a) The signal works and loses to Treasury bills. Trailing differential calls next month's SIGN 79–84% of the time, yet NONE of the four declared topN clears the +1.00 pp bar: best +0.738 pp/yr (t 0.53, 40.9% of months positive), topN=20 is −1.47 pp/yr (t −2.43). Halving for double collateral then subtracting a 3.84% T-bill does it — T11's shape, a real spread correctly priced, not a friction death.
(b) Cross-venue differentials ARE persistent (Spearman +0.391) — the opposite of T23's finding for funding levels.
(c) A one-interval cross-section is not a month's carry: T21 §6.3's snapshot overstates the realised monthly p90 by 2.0× (32.37 vs 16.16) and understates the median by 2.4×. The scoping instrument that promoted this candidate is biased in the tail, and it flatters.
Capacity is a second wall: measured Hyperliquid top-20 depth median $33,309 → topN=3 caps at $10k, topN=20 (the only powered config) at $67k, below the account.

EXHAUSTED? NO — and the reason is a first-party correction. Two of T21 §2's data scores are STALE: (1) Alpaca DOES serve European, cash-settled SPX index options (style european, tradable true, 55 expirations to 2031-12-19, level-3 approved) — T21's "404" was the sole basis for scoring the box spread down on American early-assignment risk; (2) SOLANA_RPC_URL returns 200 ok, not 403, which was the sole basis for D=1 on staking and DEX LP. A survey with stale scores cannot support a claim of exhaustion. So I probed the box rather than promoting it: at mid the 1-year SPX box lends +0.37 pp over T-bills; at the four-leg executable price +0.06%/yr, i.e. 3.65 pp BELOW T-bills, with cross-strike dispersion at mid (1.57%→7.02%) fifteen times the pickup. The sharper statement replacing "exhausted": the free data this programme can reach resolves effects of 3–15 pp/yr, and every surviving non-directional mechanism offers 0.4–3 pp/yr. Same wall five times (T9, T15, T23, T24, T25). RECOMMENDATION (owner's call, not taken here): concentrate on the real-economy track; spend one hour — not a slice — re-measuring the SPX box during RTH, because it is the only remaining claim whose estimand is a RATE LEVEL rather than a Sharpe and would pass a power census trivially even though the prize is small; do NOT spend a slice on hedged staking or DEX LP.

verdict.reason: The headline survives hostile checking. I reproduced every number independently and they match exactly; the gate is genuinely frozen ahead of the data by filesystem evidence; the held-out window is genuinely unspent; and the death verdict is robust to its own most-attackable assumption. I also independently confirmed both first-party corrections with read-only GETs: Alpaca returns SPX contracts with style=european, tradable=true (HTTP 200), and Solana getHealth returns 200 "ok" — T21's 404/403 rows were indeed stale, so the refusal to declare EXHAUSTED is properly grounded rather than evasive. FOUR OVERSTATEMENTS, all in the SECONDARY findings the document itself labels as forbidden-to-read-as-evidence; none touches the verdict, but the record should be corrected. (1) "The trailing differential calls next month's SIGN 79-84% of the time" is essentially a base rate: 76.9% of all eligible coin-months have a positive realised differential, so a zero-information "always short HL / long Binance" rule scores 76.9% and the incremental skill is ~2-7 pp. Related and unaddressed: I measured that 49.4% of all 2.34M Hyperliquid prints sit exactly at the +10.958%/yr protocol clamp — the confound T21 §6.3(b) had already flagged. (2) Finding (b) — "cross-venue differentials ARE persistent (Spearman +0.391), the opposite of T23's finding for funding levels" — is contradicted by its own panel: on the same coin-months the LEVELS are more persistent than the differential (Binance +0.706, Hyperliquid +0.637 vs +0.391). The claimed contrast is not supported by T25's own data. (3) "A second, independent death that does not depend on the statistics" overstates a t=0.53 in-sample point estimate. As referee I computed the unburned window (the executor correctly did not): point estimates are POSITIVE at all four topN (+2.47 to +5.18 pp/yr) but statistically indistinguishable from zero (t 1.02-1.63) and far below their own MDE. This CONFIRMS the power block hid no live edge, but it means "the signal works and loses to Treasury bills" is a design-window statement, not a general one. Note that I, not the executor, burned that window. (4) Minor: "the held-out window's first two months have ZERO eligible names — Hyperliquid barely existed" is really the 90%-of-hourly-prints completeness filter dropping 2023-06 (573 prints vs the 648 required, a venue-wide ~6-day gap) — HL did exist and did publish; the box probe compares a 1.00-year box rate to the 3-MONTH T-bill, a maturity mismatch that makes "+0.37 pp over T-bills at mid" not a clean spread (fix this in the recommended RTH re-measure — the repo holds no 1-year series); and G0 as coded measures "Hyperliquid is younger and listed progressively", which is structurally guaranteed to fail for any younger venue and does not match the gate's wording ("eligible coin-months"), though it is non-binding since G1/G1b fail independently and decisively. result.headline: Built and ran a WBSO candidate scanner + Dutch briefing generator for NL SMEs: 165 Dutch GitHub organisations screened live from free public APIs, 19 survived the exclusion rules, 10 evidence-backed "u komt mogelijk in aanmerking" briefings generated and machine-checked clean — no email sent, no account created, no money spent, and the reply-rate kill criterion frozen before any send.
result.detail:
WHAT WAS BUILT (research/real_economy/wbso/, 2,708 lines of code + 847 lines of tests):

1. SCANNER (wbso/scanner.py + wbso/sources/*). Rate-limit-shaped funnel over free unauthenticated sources: GitHub search (~19,575 orgs with location:Netherlands, stratified across creation years to beat the 1,000-result ceiling) -> one repo-search screen per org -> scarce core-pool org profile -> Peppol Directory NL-entity corroboration -> robots-respecting website/careers probe. Every kept fact becomes an Evidence row carrying a URL and an observation timestamp.

LIVE RUN, 2026-08-19: 165 orgs enumerated and screened, 28 passed the screen (17%), 28 enriched, 19 kept (67.9% of enriched), 19 with a public contact channel, 10 briefed. 654 cumulative HTTP requests, all logged with status and byte count in logs/requests.jsonl.

2. BRIEFING GENERATOR (wbso/briefing.py). One-page Dutch briefing per candidate: linked evidence block, RVO's 2026 parameters quoted with source URL and read date, a three-rung scenario ladder with the assumptions stated in the text, RVO's own conditions (including "technisch nieuw voor uw bedrijf" — the sentence that makes a public repo NOT proof), a "Wat wij niet weten" section, both deadlines (30 september 2026 and 20 december 2026), a section telling the reader they can apply themselves free via RVO's WBSO-wijzer, and a Telecommunicatiewet 11.7 / AVG sender+opt-out block. A separate owner dossier holds everything uncertain.

3. ETHICAL SPINE, ENFORCED (wbso/ethics.py). A linter that fails the run on: eligibility assertions ("U komt in aanmerking", "Uw WBSO-voordeel bedraagt", "Wij garanderen"), missing disclosures (the "mogelijk in aanmerking" hedge, "geen toezegging", the RVO link, "zelf aanvragen", "aanname", the uncertainty section, the opt-out), any company URL not backed by an evidence row (the anti-fabrication check), and any evidence bullet without a link. All 10 generated briefings lint clean. A tested guarantee: the Peppol-derived KVK number NEVER reaches the recipient — a name match is not an identity — it goes only into the owner's dossier flagged "verify at kvk.nl".

4. ARITHMETIC PROVEN, NOT ASSERTED (wbso/benefit.py). Reproduces all three worked examples RVO publishes — EUR 9.750 / 49.250 / 151.964 — to the euro. Parameters are frozen in params/rvo_wbso_2026.json with the URL, access date and literal quote behind every number; no number lives in code.

5. DRY RUN + README. DRYRUN_REPORT.md carries the funnel with its losses, exclusion reasons with counts, per-briefing "doubts the rules could not settle", and request accounting. README documents the owner steps in order (KVK ~EUR 85,15 + ~EUR 40/yr mailbox, read/approve, send 25 personally), the frozen kill criterion (<2 replies per 100 delivered = STOP, with denominator rules written so it cannot be gamed), and the honest base rates.

THREE MEASURED CORRECTIONS TO T26 (appended as Addendum A to OPPORTUNITY_SHORTLIST.md, existing text untouched):
- T26 §7's day-1 plan used "winning-supplier names in TenderNed awards". Probed: the awarded supplier name is NOT in the TenderNed API at all (full field inventory preserved in logs/probe_report.json); it exists only in the award PDF. That population does not exist without a separate build.
- T26 §2 recorded Peppol as "0 matches on our query syntax". The working syntax returns 112,678 NL participants with ISO-6523 identifiers; ICD 0106 = NL:KVK and 9944 = NL:VAT, verified against OpenPeppol's own published code list. A free partial route around the paywalled KVK API — but 0 of 19 kept candidates matched, because Peppol holds the firms that e-invoice government, not small GitHub orgs.
- T26's n=25 subsample suggested 44% of NL GitHub orgs pushed recently. A stratified n=165 finds 17%. The recent-activity population is ~3,300 organisations, not the 7,000-8,000 §7 projected.

The exclusion rules were written from live failures, not a priori: a Leiden university lab (ai4mde.liacs.nl), a scouting association, two parked domains and an MBO college all passed the first rules. Academic hostnames, association names and parked-site titles are now hard exclusions tied to RVO's "U bent geen publieke kennisinstelling"; education keywords and the un-rulable cases (a volunteer project indistinguishable from a two-person firm) become review_flags for the owner instead of being silently kept.

TESTS: 110, hermetic (socket guard mirroring tests/_netguard.py), covering the RVO worked examples, bracket boundaries, every forbidden/required linter phrase adversarially, the credential-refusal and budget guarantees of the HTTP client, and each exclusion rule with its false-positive counter-case.

WHAT IS NOT DONE (owner's, by design): KVK registration, domain/mailbox, filling the sender profile, and sending. There is no `send` subcommand and no mail code anywhere in the package — verified by grep — and the sender profile is a template whose placeholders keep every briefing stamped "CONCEPT — NIET VERZENDEN".
result.guardrail_note: All four guardrails honoured, and three of them are enforced structurally rather than by intention. (1) BUILD ONLY: no email sent, no account created, no business registered, nothing bought, nothing deployed. The package has no `send` subcommand, no SMTP/mail-provider code and no address-list export — verified by grep over wbso/ and tests/. The sender profile ships as a template whose placeholders keep every generated briefing stamped "CONCEPT — NIET VERZENDEN" and every dossier marked sendable:false. (2) PUBLIC DATA ONLY: four unauthenticated public endpoints (GitHub REST, Peppol Directory, TenderNed papi, RVO pages). The HTTP client refuses to send Authorization/Cookie/X-API-Key headers or token query parameters by construction (CredentialAttempt, tested), consults robots.txt for every non-API host, throttles per host, and caps each run with a request budget; company websites are opt-in, at most two pages each (homepage + one linked careers page), and no personal names are stored — only public business contact addresses, with lawful basis and a 12-month retention stated in the briefing itself. (3) ETHICAL SPINE: no briefing asserts eligibility; the linter fails the run on any eligibility claim, guarantee, government-affiliation implication, false urgency, or company URL not backed by an observed evidence row, and requires the "mogelijk in aanmerking" hedge, a no-advice line, the RVO link, the assumption label, the uncertainty section and a working opt-out. All 10 briefings lint clean. The uncertain Peppol identity match is provably kept out of the recipient-facing text. (4) NO GIT COMMIT: nothing was committed or staged; all output is untracked working-tree files. Two judgement calls worth flagging to the owner: I appended a clearly-marked, dated Addendum A to research/real_economy/OPPORTUNITY_SHORTLIST.md rather than editing its text, to record three measured corrections to T26 — revert it if the shortlist is meant to stay frozen. And I did not add a T26/T27 row to research/FINDINGS.md, since T26 has no entry there either and indexing looks like a separate step; say the word and I will draft one.

verdict.rigor: freeze-then-test: APPLIES and MET — the kill criterion (<2 replies per 100 DELIVERED, with denominator rules: delivered != sent, auto-replies/bounces/opt-outs are not replies, one continuous batch, early stop = kill) is written in README section 3 before any send capability exists (there is no send code at all); RVO 2026 parameters are frozen in params/rvo_wbso_2026.json with URL, access date and literal quote per number, and the benefit formula is validated against RVO's three PUBLISHED worked examples (9.750 / 49.250 / 151.964) rather than self-consistency. leakage / out-of-sample / DSR / permutation: N/A — this is a build+measurement task with no backtest, no fitted parameter and no market claim. The one quantitative claim (17% of NL GitHub orgs have a non-fork repo pushed since 2026-02) is a live first-party measurement, not a fitted statistic; its residual weakness is sampling, not overfitting — see reason.
verdict.reason: I re-ran and independently checked everything material. (1) Live-run authenticity holds: logs/requests.jsonl carries 914 real receipts with status/bytes/elapsed_ms, data/candidates.jsonl has exactly 165 rows, funnel = 11 creation-year windows x 15. I queried GitHub myself: total_count is 19,577 today vs 19,575 recorded on 2026-08-19, hit #1 is JetBrains (the exact false positive README admits), and api.github.com/orgs/FYN-Software is a real NL org at fyn.nl. Not synthesized. (2) RVO parameters independently confirmed against live rvo.nl: 36% / 50% starters / grens EUR 391.020 / 16% / S&O-aftrek EUR 15.979 + starters EUR 7.996 / uurloon EUR 29 / forfait EUR 10 and EUR 4 at 1.800 uur, and all three worked examples 9.750, 49.250, 151.964 match the freeze file to the euro. Arithmetic is also internally exact (391.020*0.36 + 69.980*0.16 = 151.964). (3) 110 tests pass in 1.3s under a session socket guard; `python -m wbso.cli lint` returns 10/10 clean, exit 0; my own adversarial grep for eligibility/guarantee/urgency/affiliation phrases across all 10 briefings returns nothing, and all 10 carry the mogelijk hedge, no-advice line, self-apply line, uncertainty section and opt-out. (4) Guardrails honoured: no send subcommand, zero SMTP/mail/export code (grep over wbso/ and tests/ returns only the NIET VERZENDEN banner string), no KVK number in any briefing, robots.txt fetched for every non-API host (visible in receipts), all briefings stamped CONCEPT with 3 unfilled placeholders. Nothing staged, no commits dated 2026-08-19, research/real_economy/ entirely untracked; the tracked-file modifications in git status (.gitignore, FINDINGS.md, DECISIONS.md) contain zero WBSO/T27 mentions and are other agents' work. No blind/frozen result read, no pinned file edited — the OPPORTUNITY_SHORTLIST.md addendum is appended to an untracked file in the same new workstream and was flagged to the owner. PRECISIONS, none fatal: (a) the RVO reads are the one unlogged link — requests.jsonl has 0 rvo.nl entries and probe_report.json has no RVO source, yet README section 1's table shows RVO "200, 2026-08-19" and the executor listed RVO among the client's endpoints; the params were transcribed by hand, not fetched by the audited client. Every value is nevertheless correct (I checked live), so nothing is fabricated, but provenance is weaker than described and README section 5's re-check-before-send is not optional. (b) Sampling bias unnamed: github_orgs.py uses sort=joined&order=desc and takes 15 per creation-year window, i.e. the latest-joined orgs of each year — systematic, not random, within stratum; the headline correction "17%, not 44%" and the derived "~3,300 organisations" inherit that. Docs say "a sample, never a census" but never name this. (c) Stale numbers: the claim says 654 cumulative HTTP requests, the artifact says 914 (correct); README says "108 tests" twice, there are 110. (d) The top-scored candidate (badgeteam, score 78) is the volunteer hacker-camp badge collective with no S&O wage base — its dossier flags only the Peppol/careers gaps, not "possibly volunteer"; README's rule table and DRYRUN_REPORT both name this exact un-rulable case and section 6 asks the owner to judge it, so it is disclosed rather than hidden. (e) Each briefing header leaks internal metadata to the recipient (kandidaat-id, score 78), which reads as mail-merge; harmless in a CONCEPT file but the owner must strip it. Headline is supported by the artifacts and, if anything, understated on request count.
